chapters.title: Chapter 1951 Leaving Iskaris
paragraphs: She gave him an emphatic nod while she chewed, already extending her plate for more.
The request spread down the benches. Even Maelstrom raised his plate when Ayame offered another helping, and Gorruk rumbled at Quinlan while presenting an entirely empty one.
"The cooked meat is better."
"Then you've come to the right cook."

Quinlan sent the bearkin a portion worthy of his size before returning to his place among the girls. Black Fang was eating beside Ayame, her blade put away, while Aurora sampled the results of their work with obvious satisfaction.
Between the chilled slices and the roast passing from plate to plate, they made a respectable start on the enormous catch.
Quinlan ate his fill, then leaned back on the bench to look out to sea.
"How about we get ready to leave? I'm eager to see what else is out there."
Every one of his wives had an abrupt change of expression, going from amicable women having fun to little demonesses ready to wreak havoc.
After the meal, Quinlan released the submerged curtains around the beach and opened a Domain Gate back to Miri Town for their preparations.
His wives went through, discussing clothes and supplies, the afternoon's play turning to excitement about where they might sleep tonight.
"Somewhere with a bed, preferably," Aurora said.
"I'll see what I can do," Quinlan smiled as he followed her through.
They had fought their way across Iskaris, won wars, married, and broken the wall that had imprisoned an entire continent.
He could finally take them beyond its shores.
He wanted unfamiliar monsters, new magic, people who could make him work for a victory. His own home contained precious little left that could help him grow.
And after that serpent, he was very eager to find out how the wider world rewarded a proper hunt.
"Quin?"
Jasmine caught his hand as the others headed off to change. She was still in her wedding dress, loose curls drying around her cheeks.
"Could we settle the soul army's arrangements before you go? I'll need help keeping the roads safe while we bring the new territories together."
"Of course. They're staying here."
He called Scar over. The soul general came through the gate with the Lilies, Void hanging from her back now.
"Master."
"You're welcome to travel with your old team, if you want to. Can your officers handle things here with Jasmine?"
Scar faced the governor.
"They can. I'll bring you the ones responsible for the patrols and garrisons. You can tell them where you need more soldiers."
"Thank you."

Quinlan wanted to make a more careful approach than letting his Elite Souls into the wide world. For now, he believed they were best used for defense and helping Jasmine establish proper internal order.
Void seemed to outright shine as the news registered. "Scar is coming with us..." She hugged her spectral friend tighter, nestling into her hair. "I'm glad..."
Quinlan then looked at Lilith. "Would you join us for the crossing?"
"...Yes. At least until we land on foreign land. Is that a problem?"
She asked, suspicious. Despite them being on friendly terms now, she knew him as someone who'd happily charge her for such a premium transportation service.

"Problem? No, not at all. It's my honor." Quinlan gave the woman his most charismatic of grins, making the Spellblade form a fist. This guy was truly shameless. But she released her fist within moments.
"I'm grateful. We'll be ready."
Lilith went to join her company, leaving Jasmine beside him. His governor watched the adventurers leave with a wistful smile.
Quinlan drew her against him.
"I will still come home with [Warp Gate], Jas. Once we find a place worth visiting, I'd like to bring you too."
"You'll have to. I refuse to let my entire honeymoon consist of one afternoon at the beach getting drenched."
She smiled up at him, then rose to kiss him. "Though it was a lot of fun..." Quinlan held her close, reluctant to let go even when she drew back to speak.
"I'll get things moving here. You can find me somewhere wonderful to visit. Deal?"
"Deal."
Jasmine squeezed his fingers before heading after Scar.
There was pride in her stride as she went to meet the officers and arrange their assignments. Quinlan watched her go, grateful all over again that he had her.
By the time Quinlan opened their gate back to the southern beach, the wedding dresses had been put away and his companions were armed for the journey.
Aurora had restocked their medicines, while the others filled their storage with food, fresh water, and their belongings. Familiar equipment hung at their sides, checked for the journey.
Quinlan then used [Slave Monitor] to restore Aurora's combat class, Essenceweaver.
Vex stepped through the gate with a little mirror in her hand, then stopped beside him to finish touching up her lips.
"One moment, Hubby~"
They were about to fly into an unknown world full of creatures that might try to eat them, and his Hexwitch was checking her makeup.
How couldn't she?
Her husband would be looking at her on the way there. She refused to give him anything less than her best.
Quinlan leaned over her shoulder until he appeared beside her in the mirror. Vex immediately tilted it to fit them both, her smile ruining her attempt to finish the corner of her mouth.
"Hubby! You're making this difficult!"
Quinlan merely kissed her cheeks, then said that she's already perfect.
"You wouldn't understand!" Vex insisted, though the woman's heart visibly brightened after the exchange.

Beside them, Blossom stood with her eyes shut, sniffing the breeze. She turned her head between the lingering smell of their roast and the salt coming off the waves, concentrating hard enough that Quinlan grew curious.
"What are you doing?"
"Preparing, Master! There might be a million new smells out there! Blossom has to prepare herself mentally so she isn't overwhelmed!"
Serika grinned and stepped upwind of her, opening a pouch of blended spices and dried herbs they'd used for lunch.
"Let me help."
Blossom's nose twitched, but she kept her eyes closed and took another careful sniff.
"Yes! Serika can come closer!"

His former teacher obliged, bringing the pouch nearer while Blossom tried to separate its contents by scent alone. Considering the blonde girl's turbo talented nature when it came to her sense of smell, she almost instantly solved the puzzle.
"Black pepper, garlic, cumin, crushed chili, dried rosemary, thyme, and sage!" Blossom announced. "There's barely any of the last one!"
"Hah! You even caught the sage!" Serika laughed.
Vex snapped her mirror shut beside Quinlan, satisfied at last, and leaned against his shoulder.
Iris emerged with her sword at her hip, glancing toward the ocean while Ayame tied back her hair beside him.
Feng remained on the other side of the gate with Felicity. The young queen and Alexios had a few last tasks to finish before they could set out, so Feng was staying behind to travel with them.
Rosie had come to see them off with Jasmine. His daughter caught his leg before he could turn toward the water.
"Daddy has to bring Rosie presents. It's his sacred mission."
Quinlan bent to pick her up. She wrapped her arms around his neck, holding on with a fierceness that made him hug her closer.
"What would you like?"
"Rosie doesn't know what's out there!"
"Neither do I. I'll look for something you'll love."
"Lots of things," she corrected against his shoulder.
"Lots of things," he agreed, kissing the top of her head.
Rosie stayed tucked beneath his chin while Scar came through the gate with the Lilies.
The general had finished introducing her officers to Jasmine, and the soldiers were already returning to their posts.

With the soul army helping the regular army protect the land and Jasmine overseeing the work, Iskaris could keep growing while he was away. Rosie would remain here with her Tree and the mirror concealing their home.
Quinlan lowered his daughter into Jasmine's waiting arms. Rosie caught his hand for one last squeeze before allowing him to step away.
With everyone through, Quinlan closed the gate.
Seraphiel moved beside him, gazing beyond the waves breaking near the shore.
"Do we have any idea where we're going?"
"Out there."
"That's what I thought," the gorgeous elf giggled, visibly excited for this journey into the unknown.

Quinlan called on [Masked Seat], concealing his sovereign presence and extending that protection to those who carried his mark. His crown would be hidden from foreign domains, but introductions were still his responsibility.
"Once we meet people, let's keep my name between us," he told the family. "I'd like to hear about their lives before they start asking about mine."
Lilith gave him an amused look.
"A man travelling with this many armed women will attract questions anyway."
"Those questions I can live with."
"If you tell them that you have a big spear down there and conquered us all, I won't be happy," the Spellblade decreed with a flat face.
"I'll think of something."

Smirking, Quinlan reached out with his wind magic and lifted the party from the sand. Air supported each of them beneath their feet and around their bodies, holding them upright as they rose above the beach.
He gathered a broad current behind them to carry the group forward, curving the oncoming air around their faces as they picked up speed.
"Papa!"
Quinlan looked back at his daughter's shout. Rosie was waving from Jasmine's embrace, and his governor was smiling at him from ear to ear.
This was not a tearful farewell but a quest to further the family's interests.
He waved to them, his wives calling their goodbyes on either side of him.
Then Ayame took his hand, and Quinlan turned toward the open water with his beautiful samurai beside him.

The wind carried them farther out to sea, past the waves breaking near shore. Black Fang flew on his other side, watching the depths, while Lilith laughed aloud as the beach began to recede behind them.
"Fucking finally!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1952 Looking For Life
paragraphs: Quinlan curved the wind carrying his companions eastward, following the direction they had chosen together. Iskaris's southern coast receded behind their left shoulders.
Ayame leaned against his arm as the beach dwindled behind them. Her hair brushed his cheek, and he reached around her waist, holding the petite woman close before looking toward the open sea.
"Do you think we'll go all the way to the eastern human continent?" she asked. "Or will we find other lands before we get there?"
Severely lacking in information, the gang decided their best bet was to go eastward, as they at least knew there was the eastern human land somewhere out there. However...
"There could be whole continents between us and it for all we know. I'd like to explore whatever we come across, at least from a distance."
"Hopefully the first people we meet can sell us a map," Aurora said from beside Lucille.
"It's enough if they have a map. We'll just borrow it," Lucille grinned. Despite being a delicate woman, she perfectly resembled her Bloodmonger class.
Ayame gazed ahead, her fingers tightening around his. Somewhere beyond all that water lay the homeland of the eastern humans, the place her ancestors had left.
She knew painfully little about what they might find there. Even reaching it would require better directions than the ones they possessed.
Still, the possibility made her heart race.
"I'd like to see it eventually," she admitted.
Quinlan smiled at her. "One day we'll get there for sure. But let's see what we find along the way."
"Preferably somewhere with people who know how to cook well," Serika added. "I'd love to try a new cuisine."
"We just ate a sea monster," Aurora reminded her.
"And it was both delicious and exciting, wasn't it? I'm feeling encouraged to be adventurous~"
Below them, the shallows darkened into deep blue. Quinlan raised the group on a climbing current, giving them a wider view as they passed beyond the pale seabed.
The coastline stretched away on either side behind them. Ahead, sunlight flashed across an expanse of water so vast that he kept searching for a break in it.
He wanted to know what lived beneath that surface and what waited on the far shore. Perhaps the first town they found would have something worth buying, or someone who could give him a proper fight.
His girls were discussing the same things around him, their voices overlapping in the sheltered air.
"Quin, look over there!" Seraphiel pointed down past his shoulder.
He followed her finger to a scattering of pale shapes beneath the water. As they drew closer, a school of fish broke the surface, their broad fins spreading to carry them over the waves.
"The fishes are flying!" Blossom exclaimed.
One skimmed above a crest before dropping back into the sea. More followed, flashing silver as they leaped.
Quinlan eased their course toward the school. The fish scattered beneath them, leaping in a widening fan, and his wives crowded closer to watch.
"Look at that one!" Serika laughed. "It went so far!"
"Blossom thinks it wants to come with us!!"
"It might be trying to get away from us," Aurora suggested.
The dogkin considered the fish vanishing below their feet.
Quinlan chuckled and carried the group onward. Blossom kept watching over her shoulder until the last silver flash disappeared.

Farther back, Lilith had turned toward Iskaris. Void, for once, didn't hang on anyone's shoulders. Mostly because Quinlan was already carrying her. Scar flew motionless while Bronnya was talking to Jallen about the size of the serpent they had eaten.
The captain's silver hair stirred in the breeze Quinlan allowed through his shelter. She watched the distant land, her lips parting as the low hills began to merge with the haze.
"We're really leaving."
Bronnya stopped talking and looked back too.
Lilith had wanted this for centuries. Every failed attempt to cross the Restriction had ended with the same familiar shore waiting for her, the same places to hunt, the same ceiling above her head.
Now she was watching that shore disappear while her company travelled beside her.
She could keep going.
The thought filled her with such fierce happiness that she began laughing again, helpless to contain it. Bronnya joined her, throwing an arm around Jallen as the captain faced the open ocean.
"Wherever we land, I'm finding something to fight."
"You might get destroyed in one attack," Jallen muttered.
Lilith grinned at the spearwoman. "True. Isn't it exciting?"
"...Haaah." Jallen could only exhale. Her team was full of nutjobs.
"Ah," Lucille murmured behind Quinlan. "I just realized something."
She was also looking toward their receding home. Aurora followed her gaze, then glanced at her face.
"What is it?"
"Jasmine is the only wife staying home with Rosie."
"Yes?"
Lucille smiled.
"All that time with her. Every meal, every evening... By the time we visit, our little girl might have a favorite mommy."
Aurora's mouth opened, then closed as she considered their governor's opportunities.
"Oh, she's absolutely going to take advantage of that."
"Jasmine wouldn't!" Blossom protested.
Ayame turned toward the dogkin. "She'll have Rosie helping with something important. Give her a little place beside her desk. Tell everyone what a wonderful assistant she has."
Blossom's ears sank. "That... Might work."
Their daughter would adore every moment of it.
"And when Rosie asks for a treat," Lucille continued, enjoying their dawning understanding, "who will be there to give it to her?"
Blossom caught his free hand, looking up at him with sudden urgency.
"Master, Blossom needs help choosing gifts! Rosie has to know Blossom was thinking about her too!"
"She knows. But sure, we'll find her something she'll love."
His reassurance brought her ears back up, though she continued studying the horizon as if a suitable present might appear at any moment.
Quinlan smiled toward the distant land, knowing that the girls were absolutely right. His Tyrant of Commerce absolutely would make use of the opportunity.
"You're very pleased about this," Ayame accused, watching his face.
"My daughter has a lot of wonderful mothers. I chose well."
"Hmph."
Once Iskaris disappeared behind them, the journey proceeded into the long hours of the evening.
"Still nothing, huh?" Kaelira muttered.
"Thalorind is truly a giant place..." Seraphiel agreed.
Despite the passage of time without finding any land, every member retained their full excitement for the adventure.

But mood alone wasn't enough to fill his women's bellies, so Quinlan conjured earth beneath his companions and compressed it into a long stone craft with swept wings. His wind supported its weight as he shaped a raised rim, curved seats, and a table with hollows for their cups.
"Oh, lovely," Lucille sighed, unpacking their food.
"Others row boats, and we travel like this," Kitsara grinned, getting seated.
Her lover had carved a special holding zone for her five tails.
Quinlan sat near the front, facing forward like a pilot, while the girls spread blankets over the seats. Vex joined him with a plate of meat, tucking herself beneath his arm.
"The foxy is right. This is amazing, so you deserve a reward. Here, Hubby~"
He accepted the bite she offered without a second thought. Vex smiled and leaned against him, choosing his next bite while he watched the ocean ahead.

Once everyone finished eating, they packed their belongings away. Quinlan lifted them from their seats with wind magic, then crumbled the empty craft into sand with his earth magic and let it fall into the sea.
The broad body had made them easier to spot from below. He preferred to approach unfamiliar lands as a group of distant figures, easily mistaken for birds.
More hours passed with his companions talking around him, their excitement renewed whenever someone thought they saw land. Each distant shape resolved into another bank of clouds.
By night, they had seen neither a shore nor a sail. Iskaris seemed very remote along this route.
In a sense, that was good news. At least the chances of hostiles finding the land seemed lower.
Tonight, not one of them slept.
Morning found Quinlan carrying his companions over another empty stretch of ocean, with the rising sun ahead of them.
The girls were about to start eagerly theorizing what their next destination might look like when Black Fang spoke up suddenly.
"There."
Her violet eyes were fixed on a point to the right of their course.
He followed her gaze. A dark thread rose against the brightening sky, and Quinlan curved the wind carrying his companions toward it.
As they approached, the smoke thickened into a smear above the horizon, and thin shapes began to rise beneath it.
Masts.
"Ships!" Seraphiel exclaimed, pointing at the masts.

Isn't it exciting?"
"...Haaah." Jallen could only exhale.
Her team was full of nutjobs.
"Ah," Lucille murmured behind Quinlan.
"I just realized something."
She was also looking toward their receding home.
Aurora followed her gaze, then glanced at her face.
"What is it?"
"Jasmine is the only wife staying home with Rosie."
"Yes?"
Lucille smiled.
"All that time with her.
Every meal, every evening...
By the time we visit, our little girl might have a favorite mommy."
Aurora's mouth opened, then closed as she considered their governor's opportunities.
"Oh, she's absolutely going to take advantage of that."
"Jasmine wouldn't!" Blossom protested.
Ayame turned toward the dogkin.
"She'll have Rosie helping with something important.
Give her a little place beside her desk.
Tell everyone what a wonderful assistant she has."
Blossom's ears sank.
"That...
Might work."
Their daughter would adore every moment of it.
"And when Rosie asks for a treat," Lucille continued, enjoying their dawning understanding, "who will be there to give it to her?"
Blossom caught his free hand, looking up at him with sudden urgency.
"Master, Blossom needs help choosing gifts!
Rosie has to know Blossom was thinking about her too!"
"She knows.
But sure, we'll find her something she'll love."
His reassurance brought her ears back up, though she continued studying the horizon as if a suitable present might appear at any moment.
Quinlan smiled toward the distant land, knowing that the girls were absolutely right.
His Tyrant of Commerce absolutely would make use of the opportunity.
"You're very pleased about this," Ayame accused, watching his face.
"My daughter has a lot of wonderful mothers.
I chose well."
"Hmph."
Once Iskaris disappeared behind them, the journey proceeded into the long hours of the evening.
"Still nothing, huh?" Kaelira muttered.
"Thalorind is truly a giant place..." Seraphiel agreed.
Despite the passage of time without finding any land, every member retained their full excitement for the adventure.
But mood alone wasn't enough to fill his women's bellies, so Quinlan conjured earth beneath his companions and compressed it into a long stone craft with swept wings.
His wind supported its weight as he shaped a raised rim, curved seats, and a table with hollows for their cups.
"Oh, lovely," Lucille sighed, unpacking their food.
"Others row boats, and we travel like this," Kitsara grinned, getting seated.
Her lover had carved a special holding zone for her five tails.
Quinlan sat near the front, facing forward like a pilot, while the girls spread blankets over the seats.
Vex joined him with a plate of meat, tucking herself beneath his arm.
"The foxy is right.
This is amazing, so you deserve a reward.
Here, Hubby~"
He accepted the bite she offered without a second thought.
Vex smiled and leaned against him, choosing his next bite while he watched the ocean ahead.
Once everyone finished eating, they packed their belongings away.
Quinlan lifted them from their seats with wind magic, then crumbled the empty craft into sand with his earth magic and let it fall into the sea.
The broad body had made them easier to spot from below.
He preferred to approach unfamiliar lands as a group of distant figures, easily mistaken for birds.
More hours passed with his companions talking around him, their excitement renewed whenever someone thought they saw land.
Each distant shape resolved into another bank of clouds.
By night, they had seen neither a shore nor a sail.
Iskaris seemed very remote along this route.
In a sense, that was good news.
At least the chances of hostiles finding the land seemed lower.
Tonight, not one of them slept.
Morning found Quinlan carrying his companions over another empty stretch of ocean, with the rising sun ahead of them.
The girls were about to start eagerly theorizing what their next destination might look like when Black Fang spoke up suddenly.
"There."
Her violet eyes were fixed on a point to the right of their course.
He followed her gaze.
A dark thread rose against the brightening sky, and Quinlan curved the wind carrying his companions toward it.
As they approached, the smoke thickened into a smear above the horizon, and thin shapes began to rise beneath it.
Masts.
"Ships!" Seraphiel exclaimed, pointing at the masts.

chapters.title: Chapter 1953 First Sighting
paragraphs: "Ships!" Seraphiel exclaimed, pointing at the masts.
Although Iskaris's people had been unable to sail the ocean, the girls were familiar with ships from the rivers connecting some settlements.
"But they're very big and built using a different technique." Kaelira's eyes instantly picked up on the details.
At last, people.
Quinlan slightly lowered their altitude while keeping proper distance because he wanted to see their faces and hear their voices.
Then a flash lit the side of the larger vessel.
*BOOM!*

A bolt fired from the smaller ship's mounted bow struck a translucent barrier curved around the larger vessel's hull. Light spread from the impact through the ship's inscriptions, illuminating ribs of metal beneath the wood before the whole vessel lurched sideways.

The wave it displaced struck the smaller ship beside it. That hull rose through the spray, its prow swinging toward the merchantman as its crew hurled hooks trailing chains across the gap. The hooks glanced off the barrier.
"They're fighting," Lilith said.
Quinlan stopped bringing his companions closer.

He held them above a ragged bank of cloud and curved the air around his companions with his wind magic. Their voices reached one another clearly, then his currents carried the sound upward into the sky, away from the ships.
He kept a clear route back toward open sea, then drew water into a curved lens before them.
Quinlan adjusted the curve of his water lens until the distant decks came into focus.
"Oh..." Kitsara leaned toward the magnified view.

The woman at the merchant ship's wheel had a humanlike torso, with a long coat hanging open over her chest. Below her waist, bronze scales continued into an enormous serpent's body coiled around the base of the helm.
She braced herself with that tail as another impact rocked her ship. A couple human sailors scrambled past her, some carrying weapons, others dragging wounded crewmates away from the rail.
"Quin... Do you think she was born like that?" Ayame asked, leaning against his arm to look through the lens. "I haven't seen any primordial that looked anything similar to her."
"We haven't met all the progenitors," Seraphiel answered in his stead.
"And it's also possible that further racial evolutions occurred in the long time the primordials have been locked away," Aurora theorized.
The captain shifted her coils, holding herself upright while her ship rolled beneath her. Ayame watched the movement with undisguised fascination.
"Look how easily she maintains balance... What would her home even look like?"
Quinlan found himself wondering the same thing. A house made for someone with that body, a street full of people moving as she did, children with little tails racing each other...
He wanted to see all of it.
His girls had spent the night guessing what they might find, and their first glimpse had already given them quite the surprise.
"Master! Look at the other ship!"
Blossom's eager voice drew their attention to the people on the smaller vessel.
Broad, blue-gray bodies crowded its deck. Each had four arms, the lower pair emerging beneath the ribs, and slits opened along their sides as seawater washed over them.
One held a shield above his head with an upper arm while his lower hands worked a boarding line. Another carried a spear and shield in his upper hands, leaving those below free to cast.
"They all have four arms!" Blossom exclaimed. "How does he move them all differently?!"
Serika leaned closer, her smile growing as she followed the movements of the sailor working the line.
"Imagine trying to get past his guard while he's got another pair of hands free..."
Several of his wives were leaning further to see everything going on. Quinlan widened the curve of water to give them room.
Then the spearman jumped.
Blue light flared beneath his feet when he struck the sea. His spell hardened the water beneath each step, sending him racing across the gap while the merchant's sailors shouted warnings.
"Fomorians! Fuck! Release 'it'!"
"Fomorians," Blossom repeated, tasting the unfamiliar word.
The spearman hit the merchant ship's barrier with his shield.
*CRACK!*
His first blow drove a deep dent into it. He thrust his spear through the weakened patch, tore the opening wider, and leaped toward the deck.
A statue moved beside the merchant ship's mast.
Its wings unfolded before the pirate landed. Gray fingers closed around his throat, and the winged figure hurled him back through the breach in the barrier.
The Fomorian skipped across the water, struck his own vessel's rail, and went through it in an eruption of broken wood.
"Holy shit," Serika breathed.
Kaelira's eyes widened.
"The statue moved! But they're nothing like the golems I've seen!"
The statue stepped into the light, its body carved from dark stone. It had a man's face, broad shoulders, and wings that scraped sparks from the metal fittings beside the mast.
Its chest rose as it drew breath.
"Does anyone else dare attack my charge?!" it roared across the water.
"He's talking like an arrogant bodyguard!" Seraphiel laughed in amazement. "Kaeli, look at his face!"
The smith was already staring at it. The winged man's mouth moved as he shouted to the sailors, his stone features twisting into an angry scowl.
"Is that his body, Quin? Or is he wearing it?"
"I am quite a bit lost, to be honest."
Kaelira laughed. His shy smith was laughing.
'A gargoyle...?'
A woman with a serpent's body was commanding that ship, a man apparently made of stone was defending it, and sailors with extra arms were trying to rob them both.
Then the Fomorian who had been thrown through the rail hauled himself upright.
Blood ran from his mouth. He spat it onto the deck and retrieved his spear with a lower hand while another sailor tightened a strap around his damaged shield.
Quinlan's smile grew.
That would have killed plenty of the people they knew, even those above level 70.
On the smaller ship, a black flag climbed the mast.

"I believe we're witnessing what my people call pirates," Quinlan grinned, seeing the Jolly Roger. He had watched far too many pirate movies not to get excited. "They're basically thieves operating on open waters, just a lot cooler. In this case, quite a bit cooler."
From below came another bellow.
"The riches, naga! You can keep your precious ship if you give me what's inside!"
"Naga," Ayame murmured, looking at the coiled captain again. "Is that what she is?"
Quinlan listened for more, eager to put names to the people they were watching.

The speaker stood beside the mounted bow on the smaller vessel. A filthy red coat had been slit down the sides to accommodate his lower arms. His upper right hand held a broad sword, his upper left a shield.
The lower hands remained empty. As he spread them, he used magic to raise seawater along both sides of the merchantman.
"You can drown, foul creature!" the serpent-bodied captain shouted back. "I'll give you nothing!"
The water surged over her ship.

The naga captain pressed her palm against a crystal beside the wheel, feeding power into the inscriptions. Light spread across the torn patch in the barrier, sealing the breach before the water could pour through.
The barrier shone beneath the weight, holding the sea above the deck in a trembling arch while her sailors ran for shelter.
"Definitely thieves," Serika noted. "What's so cool about being pirates, though?"
"They drink a lot of rum and sing great songs."
More than a dozen unimpressed gazes turned toward Quinlan.
He elected to move on, adjusting the lens toward the mounted bow. Its frame had handles at different heights, allowing the four-armed crew to brace it and wind its mechanism at the same time.
Light travelled along the grooves of another bolt as they loaded it.
"That bolt is enchanted. I'd like a closer look..." Kaelira murmured.
"Perhaps we should help the pirates," Quinlan offered. "They must know some interesting places."

chapters.title: Chapter 1954 Distressed Merchant Ship
paragraphs: High above the battling ships, Quinlan was still studying his water lens when Aurora gave his arm a pinch.
"Quin, please stop joking. You can't be thinking of becoming a pirate."
"They must have maps."
"And people hunting them. We don't even know which country we're near. Would you like our first introduction to be someone trying to arrest us?"
Ayame leaned against his other shoulder, smiling far too sweetly.
"Perhaps an imperial fleet. We could ask them for directions while they kill us."
"Baby..." Lucille shook her head, smiling slyly. "You won't have your way this time, I'm afraid."
"You wanted to keep a low profile," Seraphiel reminded him. "You know I'm always down to have a fun adventure, but this... I struggle to see the appeal."
"..." Quinlan remained silent, listening to all the opinions of his women.
He wanted to visit unfamiliar cities with his family, find worthwhile fights, and learn how people lived beyond Iskaris.
Beginning that journey on a wanted ship would make everything considerably more annoying.
Through the lens, a Fomorian spat into his lower palm and used it to smooth the greasy hair above his tusks. He then wiped the hand down a crewmate's back.
Vex stared.
"Hubby, fair warning. No sex while we're near such filthy pigs."
"Blossom can smell them from here."
His dogkin sounded personally wronged.
Quinlan chuckled and curved the breeze away from her face.
"Alright. It was just an idea."
"A sensible choice," Serika approved. "And we can still take the pirates' things."
Kaelira glanced at the mounted bow again.
"If it survives..."
Below them, the gargoyle launched itself at the red-coated captain. Their collision buckled the pirate vessel's foredeck.
"[Crushing Depths]!" the Fomorian roared, curling his lower fingers inward as seawater closed around the winged fighter.
Lilith leaned forward, her smile widening at the violence beneath them.

Quinlan kept the family above the clouds while he watched the other pirates. Several had stopped firing to support their captain. Others were slipping over the rail, their blue-gray bodies disappearing beneath the surface.
They were still very close to their own ship.
"Vex, could you conceal us?"
"Of course~"
His Hexwitch cast [Hex of Null Presence] over their group. Beside him, Black Fang was following the swimmers with her eyes.
"Once they can see us, let's use the spell names and gestures," Quinlan said. "I'd rather hear about their magic before they start asking questions."
Kitsara grinned. "Time to put on a performance!"
Quinlan drew his companions closer with his wind. The water below was full of people who could fight while swimming and cast while using their weapons.
He watched the swimmers as he lowered his companions, keeping the merchant ship between them and the mounted bow.
Captain Narethi felt the wheel lurch against her coils as another enchanted bolt struck her ship's barrier.
*BOOM!*
Light burst over the port rail. Her human first mate threw himself against a wounded sailor, taking them both beneath the splinters flying off the mast.
Narethi pressed harder against the crystal beside the helm. Mana burned through her palm as she fed the barrier, trying to keep the suspended seawater from collapsing onto her people.
"[Water Shield]!"
She traced a circle over the crystal with her free hand. Light spread from its inscriptions into the barrier, thickening the section beneath the hanging sea.
"Can we reach anyone?" she called toward the companionway.
The gnome crouched there had the distress artifact open across her knees. Its copper rings spun around a cloudy crystal, emitting a harsh whine.
"I'm trying!"
The gnome twisted one ring. A voice crackled inside the crystal, and Narethi's heart leaped.
Then a shriek of interference drowned it out.
Across the water, violet light pulsed from a forked metal rod fixed beneath the pirates' flag. The artifact on the gnome's knees answered with another screech.
"They're blocking us! Captain, they've got a jammer!"
Narethi stared at the rod.
Of course they did. They had caught her far from the shipping lanes, damaged her sails, and forced her to spend her magic defending the vessel. Now they could take their time killing everyone aboard.
"Keep trying. Please. Even a location would be enough."
The gnome bent over her instrument again.

Narethi looked toward the pirate deck, where Garron was wrenching his wings free of the water surrounding him. Her gargoyle drove his forehead into the captain's face, breaking the Fomorian's concentration with a spray of blood.
"Yes!" her first mate shouted, hauling the wounded sailor toward the hatch. "Garron! Get the bastard!"
The captain staggered. His shield caught the gargoyle's next punch, bending inward, while his sword opened a dark wound across Garron's abdomen.
Before her defender could strike again, the pirates beside the mounted bow thrust their lower palms toward him.
"[Tidal Hammer]!"
Their spells hammered Garron from both sides, crushing him between converging masses of water.
His roar reached Narethi through the crash. She saw a wing fold at an awful angle as the spells hurled him back toward her ship.

"[Rising Tide]!" Narethi lifted her free hand while keeping the other against the crystal. Her wave caught Garron and guided his fall onto the deck. Even slowed, his impact broke the planks beneath him.
"Garron!"
The gargoyle pushed himself up on one elbow. Dark blood poured between his fingers where he clutched his stomach.
"Still... here."
Narethi wanted to get to him. He was trying to stand, and she could see the crack widening across his middle every time he moved.
But the barrier was dimming beneath her hand.
The pirate captain tore the crushed shield off his arm and reached for another. His men were laughing as they passed it to him.

The bounty notices put him and his spear-carrier close to their hundredth levels. Garron could fight either of them, but the rest of the raiders kept joining in, and her own crew could barely keep them off the ship.
A deep crack sounded beneath Narethi's coils.
The deck dropped.
"They're in the water!" someone screamed from below. "The hull!"
Narethi unwound herself from the stern helm and drove her tail against the boards, racing toward the open cargo hatch in the middle of the main deck.
She remained above it, leaning over the frame to see into the hold. Below her, seawater burst through the shattered side of the hull.
Their kobold carpenter was pinned beneath a sliding crate.
"[Water Wall]!"
She spread her fingers toward the breach below, catching the incoming water with her spell. The flow slowed, trembling against her resistance, and the carpenter dragged his trapped leg clear.
"Can you brace it?" she asked him. "I'll hold the water."
He looked at the gap where the sea should have been outside his workplace.
"I'll need timber!"
Her first mate was already shouting for it. A lynxkin sailor shoved a length down through the hatch, then dropped after it with a hammer between her teeth.
Narethi poured more mana into the breach. Her chest hurt with every breath, and the pressure against her spell kept growing.
Through the suspended water, she saw the spear-carrier watching her.
He grinned, gills spreading along his sides, and drew his lower palms together before thrusting them toward the opening.
"[Crushing Current]!"
The sea surged inward under his spell, forcing Narethi's water wall back toward the carpenter.
"Ngh!"
Narethi slid backward across the deck. She wrapped her tail around the hatch frame and strained against his magic, feeling the wood splinter beneath her coils.
Above her, the barrier failed.
"Oh no..."
Hooks bit into the rail. The remaining arch of seawater collapsed over the deck, knocking sailors from their feet as the pirates began hauling their ship closer.
Garron got in front of the first boarder. His fist shattered the Fomorian's shield, but another pirate landed behind him and buried an axe between his wing and shoulder.
"Garron, behind you!"
He turned, dragging the axe-wielder with him, and struck the man against the mast.
The spear-carrier forced another surge through the hole below.
Narethi's spell gave a little farther. Water slammed into the carpenter's knees, knocking him down before the lynxkin grabbed his collar.
They were going to die down there because she couldn't hold it.
Her first mate was calling her name. He had blood all over his face, and he was pointing toward the stern, toward the boat they could still lower.
She looked at the sea full of Fomorians.
There was nowhere she could send her people. Even if she abandoned the cargo and somehow got them over the side, the pirates would catch them in the water.
Fear made her breath catch painfully. She had brought them out here. They were still answering her, still trying to save her ship, and she couldn't even give them a direction to run.
"Captain!"
"I know!" she cried. "I know, just..."
The pressure suddenly vanished.
"What happened?!"

Across the water, violet light pulsed from a forked metal rod fixed beneath the pirates' flag.
The artifact on the gnome's knees answered with another screech.
"They're blocking us!
Captain, they've got a jammer!"
Narethi stared at the rod.
Of course they did.
They had caught her far from the shipping lanes, damaged her sails, and forced her to spend her magic defending the vessel.
Now they could take their time killing everyone aboard.
"Keep trying.
Please.
Even a location would be enough."
The gnome bent over her instrument again.
Narethi looked toward the pirate deck, where Garron was wrenching his wings free of the water surrounding him.
Her gargoyle drove his forehead into the captain's face, breaking the Fomorian's concentration with a spray of blood.
"Yes!" her first mate shouted, hauling the wounded sailor toward the hatch.
"Garron!
Get the bastard!"
The captain staggered.
His shield caught the gargoyle's next punch, bending inward, while his sword opened a dark wound across Garron's abdomen.
Before her defender could strike again, the pirates beside the mounted bow thrust their lower palms toward him.
"[Tidal Hammer]!"
Their spells hammered Garron from both sides, crushing him between converging masses of water.
His roar reached Narethi through the crash.
She saw a wing fold at an awful angle as the spells hurled him back toward her ship.
"[Rising Tide]!" Narethi lifted her free hand while keeping the other against the crystal.
Her wave caught Garron and guided his fall onto the deck.
Even slowed, his impact broke the planks beneath him.
"Garron!"
The gargoyle pushed himself up on one elbow.
Dark blood poured between his fingers where he clutched his stomach.
"Still... here."
Narethi wanted to get to him.
He was trying to stand, and she could see the crack widening across his middle every time he moved.
But the barrier was dimming beneath her hand.
The pirate captain tore the crushed shield off his arm and reached for another.
His men were laughing as they passed it to him.
The bounty notices put him and his spear-carrier close to their hundredth levels.
Garron could fight either of them, but the rest of the raiders kept joining in, and her own crew could barely keep them off the ship.
A deep crack sounded beneath Narethi's coils.
The deck dropped.
"They're in the water!" someone screamed from below.
"The hull!"
Narethi unwound herself from the stern helm and drove her tail against the boards, racing toward the open cargo hatch in the middle of the main deck.
She remained above it, leaning over the frame to see into the hold.
Below her, seawater burst through the shattered side of the hull.
Their kobold carpenter was pinned beneath a sliding crate.
"[Water Wall]!"
She spread her fingers toward the breach below, catching the incoming water with her spell.
The flow slowed, trembling against her resistance, and the carpenter dragged his trapped leg clear.
"Can you brace it?" she asked him.
"I'll hold the water."
He looked at the gap where the sea should have been outside his workplace.
"I'll need timber!"
Her first mate was already shouting for it.
A lynxkin sailor shoved a length down through the hatch, then dropped after it with a hammer between her teeth.
Narethi poured more mana into the breach.
Her chest hurt with every breath, and the pressure against her spell kept growing.
Through the suspended water, she saw the spear-carrier watching her.
He grinned, gills spreading along his sides, and drew his lower palms together before thrusting them toward the opening.
"[Crushing Current]!"
The sea surged inward under his spell, forcing Narethi's water wall back toward the carpenter.
"Ngh!"
Narethi slid backward across the deck.
She wrapped her tail around the hatch frame and strained against his magic, feeling the wood splinter beneath her coils.
Above her, the barrier failed.
"Oh no..."
Hooks bit into the rail.
The remaining arch of seawater collapsed over the deck, knocking sailors from their feet as the pirates began hauling their ship closer.
Garron got in front of the first boarder.
His fist shattered the Fomorian's shield, but another pirate landed behind him and buried an axe between his wing and shoulder.
"Garron, behind you!"
He turned, dragging the axe-wielder with him, and struck the man against the mast.
The spear-carrier forced another surge through the hole below.
Narethi's spell gave a little farther.
Water slammed into the carpenter's knees, knocking him down before the lynxkin grabbed his collar.
They were going to die down there because she couldn't hold it.
Her first mate was calling her name.
He had blood all over his face, and he was pointing toward the stern, toward the boat they could still lower.
She looked at the sea full of Fomorians.
There was nowhere she could send her people.
Even if she abandoned the cargo and somehow got them over the side, the pirates would catch them in the water.
Fear made her breath catch painfully.
She had brought them out here.
They were still answering her, still trying to save her ship, and she couldn't even give them a direction to run.
"Captain!"
"I know!" she cried.
"I know, just..."
The pressure suddenly vanished.
"What happened?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1955 A Strange Man
paragraphs: Narethi lurched over the hatch as her spell burst through the breach. Outside, the spear-carrier was hurled away from the hull, his lower arms wrenching sideways against a current she hadn't made.
The water inside her hold began flowing backward.
It streamed around the carpenter's legs, carrying loose nails and splinters through the hole. A separate current lifted the crate off the floor and set it against the opposite wall.
The kobold stared down at his feet.
"Captain...?"
Narethi reached into the water with her magic and felt a broad, rising flow beneath the keel. Some weird phenomenon was supporting her ship while drawing the sea out of it.
Her own exhausted spell slipped from the breach. The foreign current took its place, holding the ocean outside a hole wider than her spread arms.
She could let go.
The realization left her trembling. Her fingers had cramped around the hatch frame, and she had to pull them free before she could straighten.
Wind swept her wet hair from her face. Narethi raised her head from the cargo hatch, looking along the main deck toward the stern.

A man stood on the stern rail in full black armor, a pitch-black saber lowered beside his leg. Crimson light burned through the seams of his plates and gathered beneath his helmet in a pair of red eyes.
The pirate nearest him turned, raising an axe with both upper hands.
"Who the fuck are you?"
The man turned his free palm toward him.
"Just a wanderer. [Gust]."
The man turned his free palm toward him.
"Just a wanderer. [Gust]."
Wind slammed into the pirate's chest and flung him off the ship. "H-hah?! Wind magic!" His scream followed him across the gap before he struck his own vessel's mast.
Narethi stared up at the stranger.
He was looking at her while he held the water back, her damaged ship cradled in his magic.
"Can your people close that hole if I keep the sea out?"
She opened her mouth to answer, but the mounted bow fired at his chest. The man raised his forearm, fingers spread.
"[Fortress Wall]."
Stone grew across the bolt's path, layer forming behind layer as the enchanted shaft tore into it.
*BOOOOM!*
The impact shattered the mass above the rail. Narethi flinched, but the stranger stopped the fragments with his wind before they could fall on her crew.
They hung around him, spinning slowly, their broken edges turning toward the pirates.
He swept his hand toward the pirate deck.
"[Boulder Throw]."
His wind hurled the fragments along the line of his fingers.
The largest fragment drove the bow's loader beneath its mounting with a scream. The captain drew a broad arc with his lower hands.
"[Water Wall]! Get behind it!"
His barrier caught the remaining fragments before they could smash into the crew.
"Water, wind, earth?!" Narethi gasped.
Their rescuer lifted off the rail. His wind carried him across the gap, and Narethi felt his current beneath her hull change direction.
He was moving her vessel away.
"H-he's doing so many things at once!"
The boarding chains snapped taut. A petite black-haired woman appeared beside them, her katana flashing through the links before they could tear out the rail.
The armored man lifted his free hand, palm upward.
"[Tidal Wave]."
Across the widening gap, the pirates' ship began climbing an enormous swell.
"Hold her!" their captain bellowed. "He's turning us over!"
"[Tidal Brace]!" The captain pressed his lower palms downward. His casters echoed the spell beside him, forcing the rising water down beneath their bow.
Their combined magic could resist the stranger's. Narethi felt the clash through the sea, saw the Fomorian captain bare his tusks as he began forcing his ship level.
"This is my sea, you bastard!" the pirate captain shouted. "I'll drag you to the bottom and feast on your heart!"
The red eyes remained on him as the stranger turned his raised wrist, closing his fingers one by one.
"Good luck."
His wind twisted through their rigging.
"[Inferno Blast]."
Fire followed the turning current into their sails.
Flames climbed the sails in a howling rush, wrapping canvas around the mast as the wind twisted it. One of the casters released [Tidal Brace] and swept his lower hands over his burning crewmates.
"[Water Shield]!"
The bow lurched upward again.
"Stay on the water!" the captain roared.
"We're fucking burning!"
Narethi clutched the broken hatch frame. The pirate shielding his crewmates had stopped helping hold the bow down.
Their rescuer pushed more water beneath it while the remaining casters struggled to make up for him.
The armored man raised his closed hand above his head.
"[Magma Rain]."
Molten rock gathered over their burning mast as he slowly opened his fingers.
The glowing mass spread until its red light covered the foredeck. Narethi could feel its heat across the water, and her first mate stumbled back from the rail.
"Just what in the Goddess's name is he?"
"...I don't know. But he's on our side!"
Her attention had gone to the carpenter, who was getting to his feet on a drained floor.
Their rescuer was still holding that gentle current against the breach. He had room to keep one frightened kobold dry while trying to break a ship full of savage pirate mages.
Narethi could follow his currents, but trying to imagine shaping them all herself made her head swim. He had spoken to her while doing it.
"Get below the rail!" she cried.
The stranger brought his hand down, and his wind hurled the molten rock after it.
*BOOOOM!*
"[Rising Tide]!" The pirate captain thrust his lower hands upward. Seawater crashed into the descending mass, bursting into steam while molten fragments punched through onto the deck.

Men screamed beneath glowing shields. Burning rock struck one Fomorian between the shoulders, folding him over the rail, while another crawled through the embers with a blackened lower arm dragging behind him.

Their captain spread his water into a sloping roof, carrying the molten wreckage off his crew. He kept them alive through the downpour, blood running from his broken nose as he fought the stranger for every opening.
The armored man poured fresh magma into the steam, forcing them to keep their shields raised while their vessel burned beneath them.
"Into the sea!" the pirate captain roared. "Under the merchantman! Make him come down here!"
"Excuse me. Could you move your tail?"
"!!" Narethi recoiled, drawing her coils away from the short-haired elf beside the hatch. Armed women were appearing across her deck, close enough to touch her sailors.
Her first mate raised his spear halfway before a golden-haired elf held up an empty hand.
"We're his wives," she beamed, indicating the armored man. She gestured between herself and the smith. "We're here to help."
"His..." Narethi looked from them to the man above the sea. "Why? You don't even know us."
"We saw you in distress. Isn't that reason enough?"
Seraphiel smiled at her, then looked toward Garron as he groaned beside the mast. Her expression changed immediately.
"What's his name?"
"Garron."
"Garron, I'm coming to help you. I've never healed anyone of your race. Is there anything specific I should know?"
"...It's hard to heal someone like me-"
"The patient shouldn't decide how difficult the procedure is."
"...Okay."
"Good~"
The elf passed Narethi and knelt beside her defender, tracing a shining pattern above his wound as she murmured, "[Healing Light]."

Narethi watched the dark blood slow beneath Seraphiel's hands. These people had found them out here and decided they were worth saving. She had spent the last moments of her life expecting nobody to come.
"Captain?" Kaelira asked softly. "I can reinforce the patch. Could your carpenter get it into place?"
"Yes! Yes, he can."
Narethi called down to him. The lynxkin braced their timber against the breach while the smith drew runes along its supports.
"[Runeweaver's Armory]."
Behind Kaelira, a blonde dogkin crossed her clawed gauntlets.
"[Umbral Step]!"
She vanished and reappeared behind a boarder. His lower hand seized her wrist before her claws reached his throat, twisting it until she cried out.
"[Veil of the Hollow]!"
Her body dissolved in his grip. She reappeared beside the katana-wielder, cradling her wrist against her chest.
"They're very fast!!"
The swordswoman met the pursuing pirate's axe. Steel screamed against steel, and the force drove her backward across the wet planks.
She turned the axe aside before he could force her katana into her chest. His free upper fist passed close enough to her cheek to tear a strand of hair away.
"Yeah. Everyone watch out! The stats of their elites seem to be around level 100, but their classes aren't very strong!"
"What did you say, bitch?!"
"That you are simple brutes."
"I'll make you mine and teach you how women should behave!"
His lower fingers hooked toward her.
"[Water Lash]!"
Seawater whipped over the rail toward her ankles. She touched her katana's flat with two fingers and cast, "[Stormstride]!"
The swordswoman burst past the first lash. The next caught her calf, dragging her off balance before the axe descended.
A serpent-patterned blade slid beneath its edge.
