chapters.title: Chapter 1956 Fighting Against Overwhelming Stats
paragraphs: Black Fang slid her serpent-patterned blade beneath the axe descending toward Ayame on Narethi's deck.
She gave ground as the weapons met, turning the heavier strike into the deck. Her sword left a shallow cut across the pirate's casting forearm as she passed.
"Don't stop," she muttered to Ayame with a perfectly flat voice.
Narethi recognized the difference at once. Black Fang was watching all four hands, stepping into the spaces between their attacks while Ayame recovered.
The Fomorian dragged his axe free. Blue light coated its edge as he traced a sign with his lower fingers.
"[Aqua Edge]!"
"[Viper's Coil]."
Black Fang drew her fingers along the serpent markings on her arm. A cord of violet venom lashed from them and wound around the axe's haft.
She hooked her fingers toward the deck, tightening the coil to drag his next swing low.
The Fomorian tore his axe free and slammed it against her sword. Her heels cut grooves in the planks before she slipped past his upper fist and opened the same forearm farther.
"Big sis!"
Ayame cut the water binding her calf and moved alongside her. Across the hatch, Aurora raised her staff.
"[Ethereal Empowerment]!"
Light spread over the fighters. Ayame's next step carried her under the axe, and she traced her fingertips down the flat of her blade.
"[Heavenscar Blade]!"
Her katana bit through the bracer on his wounded arm. The Fomorian wrenched it away before she could sever the limb, but his other lower hand came up to catch her sword.
"[Null Rend]!"
Blossom appeared on that side, one gauntlet shining with void energy. Her claws sank into the reaching palm, and lightning burst from them as she tore it open.
He screamed, still strong enough to swing the axe toward her head.
"Cunts with such classes?! Everyone, help overwhelm these sows!"
Ayame caught its haft on her katana. Her arms shook under the weight while Black Fang thrust her poisoned blade into the cut beneath his bracer.
Dark veins spread from the wounded arm toward his chest. "P-poison!" He tried to pull away, but his shoulder spasmed as the venom reached it, loosening his grip on the axe.
Black Fang stepped inside his failing guard and drove her blade into his throat.
"I won't die to fucking belly dancers!" He caught her wrist with his uninjured upper hand. She twisted through his grip, tearing the wound wide before he could crush the bones.
Blood sprayed across the hatch cover as he fell.
Ayame was breathing hard.
"Sexist pieces of shit... But damn are their stats insane."
Blossom kept her damaged wrist against her body, and Black Fang flexed the hand he had caught before facing the next boarder.
"To be the slower one again..." she whispered, her eyes dancing.
"I know, right?" Lilith laughed from the rail. "Bronnya, with me!"
Bronnya intercepted an axe aimed at Blossom. The impact drove the shield back against her shoulder, and she laughed through a grunt of pain.
"Bahahaha! Boss, these bastards hit hard!"
"I'm noticing! [Rift Cleaver]!"
Lilith tapped the flat of her sword with her free hand before swinging. White light tore through the water ward on the pirate's weapon, leaving him to catch her steel on its bare haft.
Beyond them, Lucille called, "[Bloodmonger's Fury]!" and struck another boarder's breastplate with her magma-coated axe.
It cut a glowing groove. He punched her in the ribs hard enough to fold her over the weapon, but Iris stepped into his next blow.
"You slut!"
Ayame caught its haft on her katana. Her arms shook under the weight while Black Fang thrust her poisoned blade into the cut beneath his bracer.
Iris staggered against the hatch frame, blood on her lips, then drew a shaking hand down her sword.
"[Torment Cycle]!"
Iris swung at his head, releasing the force stored from his blow through her sword. He caught it on his raised bracer, but the impact drove his arm back against his tusks.
"Gah!"
Lucille straightened, teeth bared, and drove the hammer in her other hand into the knee beneath his guard.

He remained standing, but they had stopped him reaching the workers. Narethi turned back to the hold, spread her fingers, and cast [Water Wall] again to hold the timber steady as the carpenter hammered its brace home.
The hull jumped beneath Narethi and threw her off her coils as the spear-carrier rammed his weapon into it from below.
*CRACK!*
The new runes flared. Kaelira braced both hands against the frame, blood welling beneath her fingernails as she kept the patch whole.
"I can't keep doing that!"

Through the gap above the timber, Narethi glimpsed the spear-carrier drawing back for another blow. Green light ran along his weapon as his lower fingers traced a sign beside it, while the other swimmers were reaching the hull behind him.
"[Aqua Lance]!"
"They're here!"
Quinlan faced Narethi's ship. He stopped feeding the magma above the pirates and swept his open hand toward the bow.
"I've heard enough remarks about my women for one day. Begone, filth. [Tsunami Surge]."
His current drove beneath her keel, forcing the approaching swimmers outward.
They fought it with cries of "[Crushing Current]!" Their lower hands pulled against his sweep, and Narethi felt the pressure on the patch ease before their combined magic began gaining ground again.
The pirates' burning mast fell between the vessels. Steam and smoke hid the water as the gunner and loaders turned the mounted bow toward her hull.
"They'll shoot while the hero is occupied!"
Kitsara detached two of her white tails and sent them over the rail. Narethi watched them slip beneath the smoke drifting between the ships.
The tails reappeared beside the pirate vessel, each carrying the likeness of a bloodied Fomorian. They vaulted the broken rail and staggered into the mounted bow's line of fire.
"Don't shoot! We're wounded!"
One clutched a dangling lower arm while the other stumbled against him, both keeping clear of the real pirates reaching toward them.
"Get out of the fucking way!" the gunner roared, lifting his hand off the firing lever.
"My leg! I can't!"
Quinlan swept his saber toward the gunner and loaders crowded behind Kitsara's decoys.
"I half expected you to shoot your comrades. But alas, those aren't your friends. [Wind Blade]."
A crescent of wind tore through the false pirates and swept across the crew at neck height.
"Wai-!"
His head flew off with his mouth still open. The loaders lost theirs in the same sweep, blood spraying across the mounted bow as their bodies collapsed over its handles.
Kitsara's shattered disguises exposed the white tails beneath them. She called both back across the gap as the severed heads spun toward the merchant ship, their eyes still moving.
The foxkin bent forward and shook her butt from side to side as the two tails reattached, her returning fluff bouncing with each shameless wiggle.
Kitsara stuck her tongue out at the flying heads.
"Keep calling my friends ugly names now, you stinky bastards!"
The gunner's mouth worked soundlessly before his head splashed into the sea with the others.
Quinlan turned back toward the swimmers approaching Narethi's hull and flattened his palm over the sea.
"A formidable race of water warriors. But what happens if you have no water? [Frozen Sea]."
Ice spread around Narethi's vessel, sealing the surface over the Fomorians pressing toward it. Then it kept rushing downward, deeper and deeper, freezing the pirates themselves.
Quinlan raised his open hand, and the trapped Fomorians strained against the ice locking their limbs apart. "Nothing much, I see."
He closed his fingers into a fist.
Narethi saw the ice crush inward around each captive. Ribs collapsed under the pressure and torsos burst as the frozen jaws ground shut, flooding the cracks beneath her ship with blood.
"You fucking butcher!"
Beyond the frozen shelf, the surviving swimmers watched their comrades come apart. "How dare you?!"
They drove their axes into its outer edge and hauled themselves out of the water with their free hands.
"I'll rip your head off!"

The first survivors scrambled across the ice toward the ship, then buried their axe blades in its wooden side to climb to the deck. Their lower hands gripped the planks while their upper arms dragged them higher.
"How utterly terrifying," Quinlan replied, voice emotionless.
Black Fang caught the first axe swinging over the rail on her sword, and Ayame cut the fingers reaching up beside it.
The pirate kept climbing. Bronnya struck him with her shield, knocking him back onto the ice while Blossom caught a sailor he had dragged off his feet.
Narethi's first mate brought his guards behind the women. They hauled their wounded clear and kept the route to the hatch open while the armed women fought for the rail.
Across the gap, Quinlan's current was still forcing the pirate vessel's bow upward. Beside its burning mast, the red-coated captain pressed his lower hands toward the sea.
"[Tidal Brace]! Hold the fucking ship!"
His remaining casters joined him, straining to force the bow down while the hull creaked beneath their feet.
Near Narethi's bow, the spear-carrier hauled himself over the ice's outer edge and charged toward the hull, lowering his weapon for another strike.
"There!" Narethi pointed at the spear-carrier. "Their second-in-command! He's the one breaking the hull!"
"Sink them!" the pirate captain bellowed across the water to his lieutenant. "Make him save his own ship!"
The lieutenant pointed his spear toward the exposed planks above the ice.
"Keep those bitches at the rail! I'll open it myself!"
The raiders nearest him spread along the hull, climbing toward the defenders while he drew back for a thrust.
"Orc Boss..." Void offered her hand. "Ready?"
Lilith caught it. "Always!"

sentences.text: Black Fang slid her serpent-patterned blade beneath the axe descending toward Ayame on Narethi's deck.
She gave ground as the weapons met, turning the heavier strike into the deck.
Her sword left a shallow cut across the pirate's casting forearm as she passed.
"Don't stop," she muttered to Ayame with a perfectly flat voice.
Narethi recognized the difference at once.
Black Fang was watching all four hands, stepping into the spaces between their attacks while Ayame recovered.
The Fomorian dragged his axe free.
Blue light coated its edge as he traced a sign with his lower fingers.
"[Aqua Edge]!"
"[Viper's Coil]."
Black Fang drew her fingers along the serpent markings on her arm.
A cord of violet venom lashed from them and wound around the axe's haft.
She hooked her fingers toward the deck, tightening the coil to drag his next swing low.
The Fomorian tore his axe free and slammed it against her sword.
Her heels cut grooves in the planks before she slipped past his upper fist and opened the same forearm farther.
"Big sis!"
Ayame cut the water binding her calf and moved alongside her.
Across the hatch, Aurora raised her staff.
"[Ethereal Empowerment]!"
Light spread over the fighters.
Ayame's next step carried her under the axe, and she traced her fingertips down the flat of her blade.
"[Heavenscar Blade]!"
Her katana bit through the bracer on his wounded arm.
The Fomorian wrenched it away before she could sever the limb, but his other lower hand came up to catch her sword.
"[Null Rend]!"
Blossom appeared on that side, one gauntlet shining with void energy.
Her claws sank into the reaching palm, and lightning burst from them as she tore it open.
He screamed, still strong enough to swing the axe toward her head.
"Cunts with such classes?!
Everyone, help overwhelm these sows!"
Ayame caught its haft on her katana.
Her arms shook under the weight while Black Fang thrust her poisoned blade into the cut beneath his bracer.
Dark veins spread from the wounded arm toward his chest.
"P-poison!" He tried to pull away, but his shoulder spasmed as the venom reached it, loosening his grip on the axe.
Black Fang stepped inside his failing guard and drove her blade into his throat.
"I won't die to fucking belly dancers!" He caught her wrist with his uninjured upper hand.
She twisted through his grip, tearing the wound wide before he could crush the bones.
Blood sprayed across the hatch cover as he fell.
Ayame was breathing hard.
"Sexist pieces of shit...
But damn are their stats insane."
Blossom kept her damaged wrist against her body, and Black Fang flexed the hand he had caught before facing the next boarder.
"To be the slower one again..." she whispered, her eyes dancing.
"I know, right?" Lilith laughed from the rail.
"Bronnya, with me!"
Bronnya intercepted an axe aimed at Blossom.
The impact drove the shield back against her shoulder, and she laughed through a grunt of pain.
"Bahahaha!
Boss, these bastards hit hard!"
"I'm noticing!
[Rift Cleaver]!"
Lilith tapped the flat of her sword with her free hand before swinging.
White light tore through the water ward on the pirate's weapon, leaving him to catch her steel on its bare haft.
Beyond them, Lucille called, "[Bloodmonger's Fury]!" and struck another boarder's breastplate with her magma-coated axe.
It cut a glowing groove.
He punched her in the ribs hard enough to fold her over the weapon, but Iris stepped into his next blow.
"You slut!"
Ayame caught its haft on her katana.
Her arms shook under the weight while Black Fang thrust her poisoned blade into the cut beneath his bracer.
Iris staggered against the hatch frame, blood on her lips, then drew a shaking hand down her sword.
"[Torment Cycle]!"
Iris swung at his head, releasing the force stored from his blow through her sword.
He caught it on his raised bracer, but the impact drove his arm back against his tusks.
"Gah!"
Lucille straightened, teeth bared, and drove the hammer in her other hand into the knee beneath his guard.
He remained standing, but they had stopped him reaching the workers.
Narethi turned back to the hold, spread her fingers, and cast [Water Wall] again to hold the timber steady as the carpenter hammered its brace home.
The hull jumped beneath Narethi and threw her off her coils as the spear-carrier rammed his weapon into it from below.
*CRACK!*
The new runes flared.
Kaelira braced both hands against the frame, blood welling beneath her fingernails as she kept the patch whole.
"I can't keep doing that!"
Through the gap above the timber, Narethi glimpsed the spear-carrier drawing back for another blow.
Green light ran along his weapon as his lower fingers traced a sign beside it, while the other swimmers were reaching the hull behind him.
"[Aqua Lance]!"
"They're here!"
Quinlan faced Narethi's ship.
He stopped feeding the magma above the pirates and swept his open hand toward the bow.
"I've heard enough remarks about my women for one day.
Begone, filth.
[Tsunami Surge]."
His current drove beneath her keel, forcing the approaching swimmers outward.
They fought it with cries of "[Crushing Current]!" Their lower hands pulled against his sweep, and Narethi felt the pressure on the patch ease before their combined magic began gaining ground again.
The pirates' burning mast fell between the vessels.
Steam and smoke hid the water as the gunner and loaders turned the mounted bow toward her hull.
"They'll shoot while the hero is occupied!"
Kitsara detached two of her white tails and sent them over the rail.
Narethi watched them slip beneath the smoke drifting between the ships.
The tails reappeared beside the pirate vessel, each carrying the likeness of a bloodied Fomorian.
They vaulted the broken rail and staggered into the mounted bow's line of fire.
"Don't shoot!
We're wounded!"
One clutched a dangling lower arm while the other stumbled against him, both keeping clear of the real pirates reaching toward them.
"Get out of the fucking way!" the gunner roared, lifting his hand off the firing lever.
"My leg!
I can't!"
Quinlan swept his saber toward the gunner and loaders crowded behind Kitsara's decoys.
"I half expected you to shoot your comrades.
But alas, those aren't your friends.
[Wind Blade]."
A crescent of wind tore through the false pirates and swept across the crew at neck height.
"Wai-!"
His head flew off with his mouth still open.
The loaders lost theirs in the same sweep, blood spraying across the mounted bow as their bodies collapsed over its handles.
Kitsara's shattered disguises exposed the white tails beneath them.
She called both back across the gap as the severed heads spun toward the merchant ship, their eyes still moving.
The foxkin bent forward and shook her butt from side to side as the two tails reattached, her returning fluff bouncing with each shameless wiggle.
Kitsara stuck her tongue out at the flying heads.
"Keep calling my friends ugly names now, you stinky bastards!"
The gunner's mouth worked soundlessly before his head splashed into the sea with the others.
Quinlan turned back toward the swimmers approaching Narethi's hull and flattened his palm over the sea.
"A formidable race of water warriors.
But what happens if you have no water?
[Frozen Sea]."
Ice spread around Narethi's vessel, sealing the surface over the Fomorians pressing toward it.
Then it kept rushing downward, deeper and deeper, freezing the pirates themselves.
Quinlan raised his open hand, and the trapped Fomorians strained against the ice locking their limbs apart.
"Nothing much, I see."
He closed his fingers into a fist.
Narethi saw the ice crush inward around each captive.
Ribs collapsed under the pressure and torsos burst as the frozen jaws ground shut, flooding the cracks beneath her ship with blood.
"You fucking butcher!"
Beyond the frozen shelf, the surviving swimmers watched their comrades come apart.
"How dare you?!"
They drove their axes into its outer edge and hauled themselves out of the water with their free hands.
"I'll rip your head off!"
The first survivors scrambled across the ice toward the ship, then buried their axe blades in its wooden side to climb to the deck.
Their lower hands gripped the planks while their upper arms dragged them higher.
"How utterly terrifying," Quinlan replied, voice emotionless.
Black Fang caught the first axe swinging over the rail on her sword, and Ayame cut the fingers reaching up beside it.
The pirate kept climbing.
Bronnya struck him with her shield, knocking him back onto the ice while Blossom caught a sailor he had dragged off his feet.
Narethi's first mate brought his guards behind the women.
They hauled their wounded clear and kept the route to the hatch open while the armed women fought for the rail.
Across the gap, Quinlan's current was still forcing the pirate vessel's bow upward.
Beside its burning mast, the red-coated captain pressed his lower hands toward the sea.
"[Tidal Brace]!
Hold the fucking ship!"
His remaining casters joined him, straining to force the bow down while the hull creaked beneath their feet.
Near Narethi's bow, the spear-carrier hauled himself over the ice's outer edge and charged toward the hull, lowering his weapon for another strike.
"There!" Narethi pointed at the spear-carrier.
"Their second-in-command!
He's the one breaking the hull!"
"Sink them!" the pirate captain bellowed across the water to his lieutenant.
"Make him save his own ship!"
The lieutenant pointed his spear toward the exposed planks above the ice.
"Keep those bitches at the rail!
I'll open it myself!"
The raiders nearest him spread along the hull, climbing toward the defenders while he drew back for a thrust.
"Orc Boss..." Void offered her hand.
"Ready?"
Lilith caught it.
"Always!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1957 Grand Sea Battle
paragraphs: Bronnya and Jallen closed around them. Scar stepped beside Lilith with a dagger in each hand as Void's violet eyes opened fully.
"[Void Step]."
Void drew her free fingers across the space before them. Darkness swallowed the group and delivered them onto the ice beside the Fomorian.
The raiders clinging to the hull released their axes and turned on the Lilies, rushing across the ice to surround them.
The void mage raised one palm and folded compressed nothing around every Fomorian except the lieutenant, sealing his reinforcements inside a single pocket of emptiness.
"[Void Push]..."

She pushed her hand toward the sky, and the pocket launched with it. She stripped the air from its path as it climbed, giving the trapped pirates no wind resistance to slow them. The raiders became blue-gray specks in a heartbeat before her magic punched them through the clouds and carried them out of sight.
*CLAAANG!*
"Damned wenches!" The powerful pirate's spear caught Lilith's white-burning sword. He drove her backward, striking her beneath the ribs with his lower fist before Bronnya forced herself between them.
"Lilith!"
"I'm fine!" Lilith spat, blood on her teeth. "This filthy thing is amazing!"
The pirate drove his spear into Bronnya's shield. Its edge bent against her shoulder, and her feet slid backward until Jallen braced behind her.

"[Mend Flesh]!" Jallen cast, touching two fingers to her weapon. Light closed the cut opening across Bronnya's shoulder, but the tanker still had to turn the next thrust aside to keep it from impaling them both.
Scar slipped around Bronnya's shield and thrust at the lieutenant's ribs. "Stop getting excited over the strength of your enemies, orc..."
He dropped his shield to catch her dagger, but her second blade cut across a lower wrist.
"Another one?!"
He kicked Scar in the stomach before she could withdraw. She skidded across the ice on one knee, then rose with both daggers still in her hands.
"Scar!" Lilith lunged at the arm lifting his spear, forcing him to turn back toward her.
"It's okay." Scar was already circling toward his shield side again.
The Fomorian hooked his lower fingers downward.
"[Crushing Current]!"
Narethi watched the ice sink beneath them. He was trying to drag them underwater, where he could breathe and they couldn't.
"[Cyclone]." Quinlan circled his free hand, driving wind beneath the frozen slab to lift it against the Fomorian's pull.
The pirate threw more magic against it. His upper arms held his weapons while both lower hands strained to overturn the ice.
"[Aqua Lance]!" the pirate captain roared from his deck.
His water jet shot toward Quinlan's head while the remaining casters held their vessel level. Quinlan raised his saber hand across its path.
"[Ice Wall]."
The jet shattered the barrier beside his helmet, spraying him with ice. His other hand kept the wind beneath the Lilies' feet as he turned his saber toward the captain.
"[Inferno Blast]."
Fire swept across the pirate deck, and the captain threw up a water shield with a furious bellow. His men stumbled beneath it, fighting to keep their hands aimed at the sea.
Serika folded her fingers over her palms and crossed her fists.
"[Solar Drive]!"
Flame drove her from Narethi's rail toward the lieutenant on the ice. Her foot struck his shield, but he heaved it upward, throwing her over his head.
She twisted in the air and landed behind him, sliding toward the edge of the ice. He reversed his spear and thrust at her stomach before she could get upright.
Bronnya caught the shaft on her shield. The pirate dragged her forward with it, and Lilith struck his exposed back.
Her white-burning edge cut through his coat and opened the flesh beneath. "Argh!" He roared and tore one lower hand away from his current, sweeping it toward Serika.
"[Water Shield]!"
Seawater rose between them.
"[Blazing Fist]!" Serika drove her fist into it. Fire burst across the water, but her punch stopped before it reached him, and the recoil split the skin over her knuckles.
Narethi saw Serika keep her bleeding fist against the shield. Heat spread from her body, boiling the water around her arm while Lilith forced the pirate's spear away from her throat.
"Come on!" Serika growled. "[Solar Eruption]!"
She slammed her other fist beside the first. The second blast tore through the thinning shield and struck his lower arms, leaving him screaming with his casting hands spread apart.
His spell broke, and the ice surged upward beneath his feet.
Jallen plunged her spear through his thigh as he stumbled, pinning his leg to the slab. "I feel like we're back in our early days, trying to bring down a war troll..." the spearwoman reminisced.
"Silence, cunt!" The pirate pulled against it, tearing the wound wider.

"Now that you mention it, it's true! How long has it been since we had such an uphill battle against a single enemy?" Bronnya rammed her shield into his chest while Lilith cut into the arm lifting his spear.
He still caught her blade on its shaft.

"Centuries." Scar ducked beneath his shield arm and buried a dagger in his armpit. He seized her wrist with a lower hand, wrenching her off her feet, but she forced her other blade into the same wound.
"Get off me, bitch!"
Serika planted her burning fist in the cut across his back. His grip faltered, and Lilith tore the spear aside before swinging through his neck.
His head struck the hull before dropping out of sight.
Scar landed beside his collapsing body and pulled her daggers free.
"Hah... Fuck..." Lilith stared at the body, breathing heavily. Then she began laughing. "Did you see that?!"
"Hell yeah!" Bronnya bellowed back, biceps flexing. "What a battle! Let's find more of them!"
Narethi looked down. The patch was in place, its runes glowing beneath Kaelira's bloodied hands, and the incoming water had narrowed to a trickle.
Relief hurt enough that she had to close her eyes. Her people could stand in that hold without being swept out to sea.

At the mast, Seraphiel was finishing Garron's healing, light pouring from her palm into his wounded abdomen. Kaelira joined her to bind his damaged wing against his back with a chain, reinforcing its links with [Runeweaver's Armory].
"The little ones," he rasped, looking toward the hatch. "Are they..."
"They're safe," Narethi answered, her voice breaking. "They're still here."
He eased himself upright beneath Seraphiel's hand. Narethi wanted to go to him, but the man holding her ship needed to know he could let go.
"The hull is closed!" she shouted to Quinlan. "Thank you, nameless hero! You can go all out now!"
His red eyes turned toward her. The supporting current left her vessel, and Narethi hurried back to the helm as her ship settled deeper.
"Is that so?"
Across the gap, he drew his hand toward himself and repeated, "[Tidal Wave]." The sea pulled away from the pirate vessel's stern.
Its bow rose on a steepening swell. The rear dropped, bending the hull across the ridge of water beneath its middle, and the captain roared for his remaining casters to help him.
"[Tidal Brace]!" Their hands pressed upward, lifting the stern with their magic. Quinlan turned his palm down, driving wind against it while the burning rigging fell around them.
"[Lightning Strike]."
How is the first outsider confrontation? Do you enjoy it or is it boring?

chapters.title: Chapter 1958 Epic Showdown
paragraphs: Quinlan's lightning tore through the water shielding the pirate deck, striking the casters trying to save their ship.
Narethi flinched at the thunder. A caster fell with smoke rising from his open mouth, and the others lost their hold on the sea.
The ship broke across Quinlan's rising wave.
*KRAAACK!*
Its stern dropped into the water. The mounted bow tore free of its base, spilling over the side as the captain pressed his lower hands beneath himself.
"[Rising Tide]!"
A column of seawater launched him from the wreck toward Quinlan, his upper right hand drawing back his sword. He held his shield in the upper left, leaving both lower hands free for magic.
Quinlan caught the descending sword on his saber. The blow drove his blade back toward his helmet, and the captain rammed his shield into the crossed weapons before he could recover.
The shield knocked Quinlan's saber arm wide. With his guard open, the Fomorian brought his lower palms together and aimed them at Quinlan's stomach.
"[Aqua Lance]!"
"[Ice Wall]."
Quinlan's barrier shattered under the concentrated jet. He twisted away, but the water struck his armored thigh and hurled him down onto the ice beside Narethi's ship.

Crimson light flared across Synchra as her ward blunted the hit. Her leg plates thickened beneath the water, taking the force until its narrow point scored through the metal and grazed the skin beneath.
Quinlan landed on both feet, wind bracing him against the ice. A bead of blood escaped the shallow cut before the living armor flowed shut over it.
"Just one attack..."
His red eyes lifted toward the Fomorian descending after him.
"It really is a dangerous world out here."
The captain landed farther out on the frozen shelf, facing Quinlan. Open sea lay behind the pirate; the merchantman stood behind Quinlan.
"Hubby!"
Vex vaulted the rail with Lucille beside her. Quinlan caught them with wind and set them down on either side of him, their boots scraping across the ice.
Lucille carried her magma-coated axe in her right hand and the blacksteel warhammer in her left. She had enjoyed using both against the dwarves enough to bring the combination on their journey.
Blood stained her lips from the fight on deck. Every blow she had dealt or taken there had strengthened [Bloodmonger's Fury], and she was smiling as she faced the captain.
"[Hex of Decay]!"
Vex's dark markings shattered against the Fomorian's skin. He laughed and lunged at her, shoving his shield toward Quinlan to block his saber.
"You can die with him!"
"[Gust]." Quinlan drove wind beneath the shield, wrenching it upward. Lucille stepped into the opening and smashed her hammer into the ribs beneath the captain's raised left arm.
"Guh!"
The blow turned his body, carrying his sword past Vex. She cut his right forearm as the weapon passed, then withdrew beside Quinlan before the pirate could grab her with a lower hand.
"No one gets to hurt my husband on my watch, you filthy pig."
"Silence!"
The captain backed toward the seaward edge of the shelf. He spread his lower hands toward the open water on either side of the ice, then swept both palms inward.
"[Crushing Depths]!"
Seawater rose between him and the three fighters, forming a wall taller than their heads. He thrust his hands forward, driving it across the ice toward them.
"[Water Shield]." Quinlan braced his free palm against the approaching wave with his magic. Its advance slowed, but the pressure drove his boots backward toward the merchantman's hull.
Narethi saw what the pirate intended. He would crush the fighters against her ship and break through its repaired side with the same wave.
"[Rising Tide]!"

She sent a current beneath her keel, carrying the merchantman clear of the ice. Ayame helped Lilith and Bronnya back aboard the merchantman while Black Fang kept the remaining boarders away from them.
"Where's your fucking fire now?!" the pirate roared. "You ran out of mana, huh? Spamming so many expensive spells was a rookie mistake you'll pay for by watching me ravage your women, bastard!"
Quinlan's helmet turned toward him through the churning water.
"[Fortress Wall]."
A broad ramp of earth grew across the ice in front of Quinlan and his women. Its lower end faced the incoming wave; its upper edge rose above their heads and curled back toward the captain.
Quinlan released his water shield. The wave struck the ramp and rushed up its face, throwing spray high above the fighters.
"[Gust]."
He swept his hand toward the pirate, blowing the rising water back across the gap. The captain looked up as his own wave fell toward him.
"[Tidal Brace]!"
He raised his shield overhead and pointed his lower right palm upward. A barrier of seawater formed above the metal, catching the returning torrent before it could crush him.
His lower left hand was still driving fresh water toward Quinlan's ramp.
"What the fuck?!"
The harder he pushed with that hand, the more water climbed the ramp and came crashing back onto his head. His knees bent beneath the weight.
Narethi stared at the path of the wave. Quinlan was letting the pirate supply its force, using earth to lift it and wind to throw it back at him.
The captain wrenched his lower left hand away from the sea, canceling his attack. Water stopped pouring onto the ice, and the wave already at the ramp began draining away.
Quinlan spread his fingers toward it.
"[Water Shield]."
He gathered the retreating water into a suspended mass above the ramp, catching it before it could return to the ocean.
"You brought all this water over for me," he said. "I won't waste it."
Quinlan swept his hand down. The captured mass poured onto the captain's overhead barrier, driving him onto one knee.
"[Tidal Brace]!" The Fomorian raised his lower left palm beside his right. "[Tidal Brace]!!"
With both hands supporting his defense, he forced the falling water upward long enough to begin standing. Quinlan drove wind down through the torrent, and the captain's knee struck the ice again.
Blood ran from his nose onto his bared teeth.
"Ngh! You..."
Quinlan lowered the earthen ramp into the ice, opening the path between them. Vex and Lucille advanced with him while he kept the captured water pressing down on the pirate's barrier.
Vex moved toward the captain's right, facing his sword. Lucille went left, where he was holding his shield above his head.
"Get away from me!"
The pirate slashed at Vex.
"Over my dead body." Quinlan flicked two fingers sideways, pushing wind against the sword, and she caught the weakened swing on her own blade.
She turned his sword outward and cut deeper into his wounded forearm. He screamed and tried to pull away from her, leaving his other side exposed to Lucille.
His lower left arm was still extended upward, palm supporting the water barrier. Lucille planted her foot beside him and swung her axe at the elbow beneath it.
"Got you~"
The magma-coated blade tore through flesh and bone in one blow. His severed arm struck the ice with its fingers still spread.
"AAAAAGH!"
Lucille completed the swing with blood spraying across her coat, her hammer ready in her other hand.
"You should've kept your men off my ship," Narethi whispered.
The captain's water barrier sagged with only his lower right hand supporting it. Before the torrent could fall on Lucille, Quinlan swept it sideways against the pirate's raised shield.
"Why do you still have mana?! What is your class?!" The captain howled, lurching over his words.

The impact ripped the shield free, tearing its straps and wrenching the pirate's upper left shoulder out of its socket. The shield spun out to sea while Quinlan lifted the water over the fighters again.
"Never heard of Elemental Sovereign?"
"Hahaha!" The captain broke into ugly laughter. "An Elemental Sovereign, you?! A shitty fucking Epic-tier class?! Doing all this to my men? Stop lying!"
Vex stepped back from the sword's reach, and Lucille withdrew beside her. The pirate lurched upright, blood pumping from his missing arm.
He turned toward the open sea behind him. His lower right hand swept upward, drawing a wave toward the edge of the shelf to carry him away.
"[Rising Tide]!"
Quinlan pointed past the pirate's shoulder.
"[Frozen Sea]."
The escape wave froze as it rose, forming an ice wall across the pirate's path. He struck it shoulder-first and staggered back, his sword shaking in his wounded right arm.
"Stay back! I'll fucking kill you!"
Narethi knew that voice. She had heard the same desperate fury in her own throat when she told the pirate captain he could drown.
Watching him search for a way out filled her with vicious satisfaction. Then her gaze rose to the water hanging above the ice, enough to bury every fighter beneath it.
Quinlan held it there while Vex wiped spray from her eyes beside him. Lucille stood within reach of his free hand, her weapons dripping.
Both women kept their eyes on the pirate, trusting Quinlan to keep the water above them.
'Such trust...'
The sight frightened Narethi.
'Such powers...'
He had kept her carpenter dry through a shattered hull with that same control, and now he was using it to take a man apart.
The captain lunged at Quinlan with his sword, thrusting his lower right palm forward beneath the blade.
"[Aqua Lance]!"
Quinlan turned the sword aside with his saber and swept his free hand across the forming jet.
"[Frozen Sea]."
The water froze against the pirate's palm. Quinlan grew the ice down to the shelf, trapping that last spellcasting hand in a solid column before the Fomorian could pull it back.
His lunge carried his body past the anchored arm, wrenching the elbow backward.
*CRACK!*
"AAAAAGH!"

Narethi flinched at the thunder.
A caster fell with smoke rising from his open mouth, and the others lost their hold on the sea.
The ship broke across Quinlan's rising wave.
*KRAAACK!*
Its stern dropped into the water.
The mounted bow tore free of its base, spilling over the side as the captain pressed his lower hands beneath himself.
"[Rising Tide]!"
A column of seawater launched him from the wreck toward Quinlan, his upper right hand drawing back his sword.
He held his shield in the upper left, leaving both lower hands free for magic.
Quinlan caught the descending sword on his saber.
The blow drove his blade back toward his helmet, and the captain rammed his shield into the crossed weapons before he could recover.
The shield knocked Quinlan's saber arm wide.
With his guard open, the Fomorian brought his lower palms together and aimed them at Quinlan's stomach.
"[Aqua Lance]!"
"[Ice Wall]."
Quinlan's barrier shattered under the concentrated jet.
He twisted away, but the water struck his armored thigh and hurled him down onto the ice beside Narethi's ship.
Crimson light flared across Synchra as her ward blunted the hit.
Her leg plates thickened beneath the water, taking the force until its narrow point scored through the metal and grazed the skin beneath.
Quinlan landed on both feet, wind bracing him against the ice.
A bead of blood escaped the shallow cut before the living armor flowed shut over it.
"Just one attack..."
His red eyes lifted toward the Fomorian descending after him.
"It really is a dangerous world out here."
The captain landed farther out on the frozen shelf, facing Quinlan.
Open sea lay behind the pirate; the merchantman stood behind Quinlan.
"Hubby!"
Vex vaulted the rail with Lucille beside her.
Quinlan caught them with wind and set them down on either side of him, their boots scraping across the ice.
Lucille carried her magma-coated axe in her right hand and the blacksteel warhammer in her left.
She had enjoyed using both against the dwarves enough to bring the combination on their journey.
Blood stained her lips from the fight on deck.
Every blow she had dealt or taken there had strengthened [Bloodmonger's Fury], and she was smiling as she faced the captain.
"[Hex of Decay]!"
Vex's dark markings shattered against the Fomorian's skin.
He laughed and lunged at her, shoving his shield toward Quinlan to block his saber.
"You can die with him!"
"[Gust]." Quinlan drove wind beneath the shield, wrenching it upward.
Lucille stepped into the opening and smashed her hammer into the ribs beneath the captain's raised left arm.
"Guh!"
The blow turned his body, carrying his sword past Vex.
She cut his right forearm as the weapon passed, then withdrew beside Quinlan before the pirate could grab her with a lower hand.
"No one gets to hurt my husband on my watch, you filthy pig."
"Silence!"
The captain backed toward the seaward edge of the shelf.
He spread his lower hands toward the open water on either side of the ice, then swept both palms inward.
"[Crushing Depths]!"
Seawater rose between him and the three fighters, forming a wall taller than their heads.
He thrust his hands forward, driving it across the ice toward them.
"[Water Shield]." Quinlan braced his free palm against the approaching wave with his magic.
Its advance slowed, but the pressure drove his boots backward toward the merchantman's hull.
Narethi saw what the pirate intended.
He would crush the fighters against her ship and break through its repaired side with the same wave.
"[Rising Tide]!"
She sent a current beneath her keel, carrying the merchantman clear of the ice.
Ayame helped Lilith and Bronnya back aboard the merchantman while Black Fang kept the remaining boarders away from them.
"Where's your fucking fire now?!" the pirate roared.
"You ran out of mana, huh?
Spamming so many expensive spells was a rookie mistake you'll pay for by watching me ravage your women, bastard!"
Quinlan's helmet turned toward him through the churning water.
"[Fortress Wall]."
A broad ramp of earth grew across the ice in front of Quinlan and his women.
Its lower end faced the incoming wave; its upper edge rose above their heads and curled back toward the captain.
Quinlan released his water shield.
The wave struck the ramp and rushed up its face, throwing spray high above the fighters.
"[Gust]."
He swept his hand toward the pirate, blowing the rising water back across the gap.
The captain looked up as his own wave fell toward him.
"[Tidal Brace]!"
He raised his shield overhead and pointed his lower right palm upward.
A barrier of seawater formed above the metal, catching the returning torrent before it could crush him.
His lower left hand was still driving fresh water toward Quinlan's ramp.
"What the fuck?!"
The harder he pushed with that hand, the more water climbed the ramp and came crashing back onto his head.
His knees bent beneath the weight.
Narethi stared at the path of the wave.
Quinlan was letting the pirate supply its force, using earth to lift it and wind to throw it back at him.
The captain wrenched his lower left hand away from the sea, canceling his attack.
Water stopped pouring onto the ice, and the wave already at the ramp began draining away.
Quinlan spread his fingers toward it.

"[Tidal Brace]!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1959 Married Man From Afar
paragraphs: "AAAAAGH!"
Quinlan caught the pirate's sword wrist in his free hand. Earth grew over the Fomorian's knuckles, pinning his fingers against the hilt.
The captain tried to release the weapon. His trapped fingers strained against the rock as Quinlan tightened it around them.
"Wait-!"
Quinlan squeezed, crushing them until they burst.
He crumbled the rock and released the mangled hand, letting the sword fall.
Quinlan melted the ice holding the broken lower arm, then swept his hand toward the pirate's legs. An earthen slab rose behind his knees and knocked him onto his back.
Narethi recoiled at the impact. The pirate's tusks snapped together, spraying broken teeth across his chest.
"Stop!" he choked. "Stop, I yield!"
Quinlan held his saber against the Fomorian's throat. Stone closed around his three remaining arms and both legs, pinning him to the ice.
He broke the water suspended above them into rain.
"Thanks," Quinlan said. "You taught me a lot."
He lifted his saber and brought it down across the pirate's neck. The black blade cut through flesh and bone, striking the ice beneath with a sharp crack.
The severed head rolled onto its cheek. Blood poured from the stump as the captain's body jerked against the stone bindings.
Vex wiped her sword on the pirate's coat while Lucille rested her hammer against her shoulder.
"What an epic first battle~" the Bloodmonger purred.
Around the ship, the surviving raiders began dropping their weapons onto the ice.
None were spared.
After the last pirate died, Narethi's first mate began counting the crew aloud.
Each answer let her breathe a little easier. The kobold limped out of the cargo hatch with the lynxkin's arm around his shoulders, and the gnome raised a shaking hand from beside the companionway.
Some names received no answer.
Narethi kept looking toward the water after each one, searching the floating wreckage even when her mate had moved on.
"[Gust]." Quinlan lifted a sailor out of the sea with a sweep of his hand. Narethi reached for the body as he brought it over the rail, but Seraphiel was already shaking her head.
Narethi lowered the dead man onto the deck.
She stayed beside him for a moment, her palm pressed against his wet shoulder. Then another survivor called from below, and she turned toward the sound.
There were still people who needed her.
Quinlan lifted his companions from the ice with wind, bringing them aboard in groups.
They were hurt too. Lilith sat on a broken crate while Jallen traced a sign over her ribs and cast [Mend Flesh], the captain still grinning despite the blood on her teeth.
Serika had a burned sleeve and trembling hands. Blossom was holding her own injured wrist while Aurora helped her drink a potion.
'We got the drop on them, and they clearly aren't the final bosses of some epic organization, yet it was still a close call...' Quinlan thought.
Quinlan landed beside the mast, realizing that the world of Thalorind truly wasn't going to be a walk in the park. Vex took his arm and steered him toward an empty crate.
"Could you sit down for a moment, Hubby? I want Sera to look at your leg."
"It's barely a scratch."
"Wonderful. Then she'll be quick."
He sat, and Seraphiel knelt beside him. Synchra parted over his thigh, exposing a thin scrape that Seraphiel closed with a brief touch of [Healing Light].
Narethi approached them with Garron beside her. Her defender leaned against the mast, his good wing drooping with exhaustion.
"I don't know who you are," she began. "Hero..."
Quinlan's red eyes lifted toward her.
She tried to introduce herself properly. Then she looked at her crew behind him and couldn't get past the fact that they were alive because these strangers had stopped to help.
"We were going to die," she said. "All of us. I couldn't..."
Her voice failed, and she pressed a hand against her mouth until she could trust it again.
"Thank you."
Garron bowed his head to Quinlan.
"And your companions. Thank you."
"You're welcome." Quinlan glanced toward the cargo hatch. "You kept your ship afloat long enough for us to reach it."
Narethi looked back at the carpenter, who was sitting against the mast with his hammer clutched in both hands.
"Barely."
"It was enough."
She wanted to say something worthy of what they had done. Instead she found herself wiping her face with the heel of her hand.
Quinlan waited while she composed herself.
Behind him, Kaelira was watching the broken bow turret floating in the wreckage of the pirate ship. He followed her gaze, then raised it out of the water with a current of air.
"Some assembly required," he told her.
Kaelira let out a surprised laugh.
"I can work with that."
He lowered it onto an undamaged section of deck, keeping its loaded bolt pointed out to sea until the first mate helped Kaelira remove it.
Narethi watched them start examining the weapon that had nearly sunk her.
"You can have anything we recover from their vessel," she said. "I'll have my people help once we've seen to the wounded."
"I'd appreciate that. There are some things I'd like to ask you, too."
"Of course."
His helmet turned toward the Fomorian captain's headless body, still lying on the ice.
"Was he someone important?"
Narethi followed his gaze.
"A coastal raider. There are notices for him at the port. He was rumored to have reached his hundredth level."
"A coastal raider," Lilith repeated from her crate.
"He was well equipped," Narethi said. "But he didn't command a fleet or hold a port. Men like him prey on ships that stray too far from protection."
Serika looked at Lilith. Both were smiling again.
"Oh, I'm going to enjoy this adventure far too much," Lilith decreed.
Narethi couldn't understand it. They had fought hard enough to leave blood across her deck, and hearing that there were more enemies like these seemed to please them.
Her curiosity was becoming unbearable. She wanted to know where people like these came from and what had brought them across her ship's path.
"May I ask who you are?" she ventured. "You don't owe me an explanation. I just... I've never seen anyone fight like that."
Quinlan rested his hand over Vex's on his arm.
"My wives and I are on our honeymoon."
"Your... honeymoon?"
"Yes." He looked toward Lilith and the women gathered around her crate. "And these are our bodyguards."
Lilith stared at him before giving him a grin.
It was much better than having to pretend to be his lover.

Vex leaned against his shoulder, smiling into his armor. Narethi looked between the married couple and their battered escorts, trying to fit the explanation to the battle she had just witnessed. "W-where do you hail from?"

"We come from a distant, secluded land," Quinlan replied. "It's customary for a newlywed lord to take his wives out into the wider world for a while. See unfamiliar places, learn how other people live."
"Before taking charge at home?" Narethi asked.
"Exactly. We're expected to return wiser than we left, ready to lead our people. I'd like to have a few adventures with my wives along the way."
Lucille smiled softly, leaning back to let Seraphiel examine her ribs.
"We're enjoying ourselves a lot."
Narethi glanced at the blood drying on her coat. That much she had gathered.
The explanation did account for their questions about the pirates. They were strangers to this coast, and she could finally offer them something useful in return for her crew's lives.
"Then perhaps I can help, my lord. Once we've seen to everyone, I'd be happy to tell you what I know of the region."
"Then I'll take you up on your offer."
Kaelira crouched to examine the salvaged weapon's mounting.
"The bow and the jammer cost money," Narethi added. "Someone ashore will know where he got them. We may learn more about these raiders at the port."
The gnome approached with the distress artifact held against her chest. Its copper rings were turning smoothly now, the crystal glowing clear between them.
"Captain... The jammer went down with their mast. I can send again. What should I tell the harbour?"
Narethi looked around her ruined deck. Her crew were alive to work on it, Garron was standing beside her, and Lucille was laughing while Seraphiel tended her bruised ribs.
"That we survived," she said, her voice trembling. "And that we're bringing home the people who saved us."

chapters.title: Chapter 1960 Preposterous Man
paragraphs: Narethi turned toward the helm as her gnome began speaking into the distress artifact. Beside the merchantman's mast, Quinlan finally opened the rewards he had put aside during the battle.
[You've slain Fomorian Pirate (Level 85). You've gained 8,400,000 XP.]
His gaze stayed on the number.
That had been one of the Fomorians beneath the hull, crushed inside his ice while the others tried to force their way through.
Eight million four hundred thousand.
'Goddess's Sexy Lacy Panties... Am I under an illusion attack?'
He brought up the next notification.
[You've slain Fomorian Pirate (Level 79). You've gained 6,900,000 XP.]
Then another.
[You've slain Fomorian Elite (Level 91). You've gained 11,200,000 XP.]
'Holy fuck.'
Vex stood beside his crate, one hand resting on his shoulder. To Narethi's crew, the white-haired woman seemed entirely occupied with watching the sailors clear a fallen spar.
<Hubby.>
<Yes?>
<Have you looked?>
<I'm looking.>
<I want to kiss you so badly right now.>
Quinlan kept his face composed beneath his helmet. His women were scattered across the damaged deck, helping where they could while rewards appeared before their eyes.
Lucille accepted a strip of clean cloth from a sailor and began wiping her axe.
<Quin, baby... We really should travel more often.>
<Blossom sees so many numbers!! Her head is spinning!!>
The dogkin remained seated beside Aurora, her tail lying carefully along the crate instead of beating it to pieces.
He wanted to laugh. His gorgeous dogkin had enough excitement in her voice to fill the whole harbour they were headed toward.
Quinlan continued through the notifications, reaching the reward for the pirate captain.
[You've slain Fomorian Captain (Level 102). You've gained 50,000,000 XP.]
For a moment, he forgot the voices in the link.
Fifty million.
The pirate captain who had grazed his thigh was level 102 and had paid him fifty million XP.

Quinlan read it again, remembering the captain's furious face when his own wave came crashing back down on him. Fighting the Fomorian had already been immensely satisfying. Now the system was giving him this for the pleasure.
He was already addicted to progressing through the levels, but this...
'Injected straight into the veins,' he chuckled inwardly.
Vex kept her hand on his shoulder while he called up his status.
He checked the difference, including the smaller rewards and the additions from the family's Bond Pool.
A hundred million XP from the battle.
His bar had advanced by more than five percent. He could see the gain plainly, an entire stretch filled in where the serpent's reward had made a much smaller change.
All from stopping beside two ships.
<How much, Quin?> Ayame asked.
<A hundred million altogether.>
Her blue eyes remained on the sailor demonstrating how to secure a replacement line. She listened with the polite interest of a visiting noblewoman.
<...We need to find more pirates.>
<My thoughts exactly.>
Quinlan let himself enjoy the number while the crew hauled their remaining sail into position. The strained canvas caught a little wind, and the merchantman began moving away from the wreckage.
They had barely begun exploring Thalorind. Less than one hour's fighting had given him progress he would otherwise need to spend sleepless days grinding in the labyrinths on Iskaris to earn.
Then his attention returned to the first reward: eight million four hundred thousand.
His pleasure remained, but he found himself studying that figure for a different reason.

General Hargrieve had given him eighty-four thousand five hundred. Quinlan had been considerably weaker then, killing a level-sixty-eight commander while arrows and spells came at him from every direction.
He remembered the notification. At the time, he had been perfectly happy with it.
One level 85 pirate had just paid close to a hundred times as much.
'Well, these bastards were stronger.'
They had been. He had watched them injure his women despite their ambush, and the captain had forced him to work for his openings.
The boss had reached level 102. That put him thirty-seven levels above Quinlan, a gap deserving a substantial reward.
But Quinlan had spent most of his life fighting people who should have killed him.

He had fought with weaker abilities, worse equipment, and far less room to make a mistake. Some victories had left him in pieces. Being outmatched in stats, experience, and numbers was familiar enough that it had stopped feeling remarkable long ago.
Yet the rewards had never looked like this.
His gaze moved toward the sea beyond the rail, where the last patches of blood were thinning behind the ship.
The serpent had only been level seventy.

He had suggested that fighting underwater explained its generous payout. Perhaps the creature itself was rare. Black Fang had listened to both possibilities with the same unconvinced expression before asking for a larger sample.
Now they had killed an entire crew of pirates.
Different enemies, different conditions, and millions kept appearing.
Quinlan looked down at his restored thigh. The captain's attack had drawn blood, but Seraphiel had closed the scrape with one touch.
He had endured far worse for far less.
'...Strange.'
Beneath the edge of Quinlan's frozen sea, Black Fang watched the merchantman's keel pass overhead.

She held the Soul Reaper against her chest, its pale fire dimmed along the pitch-black blade. Her other hand gripped the underside of the ice, keeping her below the surface while the ship's wake tugged at her hair.
Cold water crept beneath her black combat robes whenever she moved. Her fingers ached against the ice, and she drew the saber closer while remembering the look that had put her here.
Quinlan had been standing on the merchant ship, sending the others up to the ship's rail with his wind. Black Fang had watched him glance across the corpses between each group.
His red eyes had lingered on the captain, then followed the bodies drifting among the wreckage.
She knew that hunger. The pirates had stopped being useful as opponents, but their souls were still there, waiting to become his soldiers.
He wanted them badly enough that his gaze returned to the dead even while a sailor called over to thank him.
Quinlan had looked at the man, then at the other survivors gathered along the rail. They were watching their rescuer with exhausted gratitude.
Having him rip souls out of the corpses surrounding their ship would give them rather a lot to discuss on the journey home and afterward.
Then his eyes had found hers.
Black Fang remembered how they brightened. He glanced once more at the dead before looking back at her, his head tilting a little as he waited.
Oh, she knew that face.

Synchra covered his mouth, but she could see the smile perfectly in those shameless red eyes. He had found someone who could collect every soul he wanted while he stayed aboard with their new acquaintances.
And now he was looking at her so sweetly, asking her to do it for him without saying a word.
Black Fang had stared back.
His eyes creased with the grin beneath his helmet.
*Splash.*
She had turned toward the sound behind her. The Soul Reaper had flown around her back and dipped its point into the sea beside the ice, its hilt hovering within reach of her hand.
When she looked at Quinlan again, he was still waiting, his gaze warm with the confidence that she understood him.
She did.
The warmth with which he looked at her was making it very difficult to resent how thoroughly he intended to put her to work.
Black Fang had reached down and caught the hilt. His eyes followed her hand, then returned to her face with such open pleasure that she felt it beneath her ribs.
She held his gaze for another moment before slipping into the water. Vex's [Hex of Null Presence] covered her descent, and Quinlan turned his attention to the people waiting for him aboard.
They had exchanged no words at all.
Now the wake washed cold seawater down Black Fang's neck while she clung beneath the ice with his precious saber pressed against her.
'The audacity...'
The man was aboard with his wives while she hid in freezing water to keep his necromancy secret from a ship full of strangers.
Black Fang looked down at the weapon in her hand, then up at the departing hull.
Through the clear edge of the ice, she watched the ship's repaired side rise and fall with the swell as it moved away.
She waited until the stern disappeared beyond the broken mast lying across her view, then lifted herself far enough to breathe behind the wreckage.

chapters.title: Chapter 1961 The Villain's Fang
paragraphs: Water streamed from her hair. She drew air into her lungs without exposing herself above the mast, watching the distant figures working along the merchantman's rail.
The vessel grew smaller as she watched from behind the broken mast.
At last, the curve of the sea hid its hull, leaving only a ragged sail above the horizon.
Black Fang planted her palm on the ice and pulled herself out.
Her boots found the frozen shelf Quinlan left behind beside a dead Fomorian. She straightened, water pouring from the hem of her clothes and pattering onto the blood beneath her feet.

She pushed her wet hair behind one shoulder. Her combat robes usually concealed her figure, but the soaked black silk now clung to her breasts and waist. Cold water trickled down her leg beneath the torn hem.
Quinlan would have dried and warmed her already.
The thought came so readily that she looked toward the distant sail again.
Now she stood alone with a sea full of corpses and a freezing body.
Black Fang glanced down at the saber, its hilt warm beneath her cold fingers. She remembered the pleasure in Quinlan's eyes when she had accepted his wordless request.
That smile brought another of his remarks back with perfect clarity.
"The Villain's Fang cannot be an indecisive woman."
She could hear the smug bastard saying it.
Back then, she had told him to shut his mouth.
Her lips parted now, but the remembered grin made her heart warm before she could find anything contemptuous to say about it.
His fang.
"Preposterous."
Black Fang lowered her gaze to the Fomorian at her feet. His lower hand had frozen around the axe that brought him up the ship's side.
Remembering the fight sent a delicious thrill through her.
His death had moved her toward level seventy-five.
More than a century of killing had failed to give her that next level.
She looked across the bodies littering the ice, remembering the wealth of XP that had appeared in her vision.
Her mouth slowly curved.
"My heart won't calm down."
The dead pirate stared upward with the terror of his last moment still fixed on his face.
Black Fang stepped over his arm and raised the Soul Reaper. Violet light shone through the wet silk over her mark, spreading along her wrist into the saber.
"[Soul Collection]."
Her spell sent violet threads from the saber into the dead scattered across the ice and beneath the water, catching their souls and drawing them toward the blade.
A cold pull caught beneath Quinlan's ribs while Narethi spread a chart across a crate beside him.
He recognized Black Fang drawing on his necromancy channel through the saber he had left in her hands. Pale-blue light ran between Synchra's breastplates as her collection spell took hold.
Narethi stopped smoothing the chart.
"My lord? Are you alright?"
Quinlan glanced down at the glow. Synchra's crimson seams had acquired a ghostly blue edge, bright enough to reflect on the naga's scales.
His helmet parted over his face, and he gave her an easy smile.
"Quite alright. Just cooling down."
"Oh." Her gaze lingered on his chest before she returned to the chart. "Please tell us if there's anything you need."
"I will. Thank you."
Vex stood beside him, studying the unfamiliar coastline drawn across the parchment. Her expression remained politely curious while another cold surge passed through his body.
<She started.>
<Yep.>
Quinlan rested his hand on the crate as Narethi indicated their position.
Far behind the merchantman, blue fire lit the frozen sea.
Blue fire burst from the Fomorian at Black Fang's feet.

His soul tore free as a writhing wisp, and the Reaper swallowed it with a deep hum. Across the shelf, violet threads pulled more souls through the ice and water, gathering them into streams of pale light.
Black Fang raised the saber into the converging fire. Its glow washed over her wet skin as the captain's soul surged from his headless body, straining upward against her spell.
"There's no escape."
She turned the blade toward the captain's rising soul. Power flowed from her violet mark into the Reaper, dragging it down into its hungry flames.
Black Fang watched it disappear, her unhinged smile widening as the remaining souls poured into the saber. Through the necromancy channel Quinlan had shared with her, she claimed them all for him.
These men had thought they could rape his women, speaking of hideous acts even in their last moments.
Now he owned their souls for the rest of eternity.
The last wisp vanished into the black steel, and the flames withdrew. Water dripped from Black Fang's hair as she lowered the saber, still smiling.
Sunlight returned to the ice and the bodies lying across it.
She looked at the blade in her hand.
"Satisfied?"
The Soul Reaper tugged toward the distant ship.
"Okay."
She released it from her hand. Beside her knees, the saber turned flat in the air, its point aimed along the merchantman's wake.
Black Fang stepped onto the flat of the blade, one boot near the guard and the other farther along its length. The Reaper held her weight without dipping.
"Go."
The saber accelerated toward its master, carrying her low over the waves. Black Fang bent her knees as it banked around floating wreckage, her wet hair streaming behind her.
When a swell rose ahead, the Reaper lifted her over it and dipped toward the water again. The merchantman's ragged sail grew above the horizon.
Quinlan felt the Reaper skimming above the water, rapidly closing the distance.
<She's coming up behind us. Could you cover her?>
<Of course, Hubby.>
Narethi rolled up the chart as Vex moved to the stern rail. "I'm so hungry!! Is there anyone who can fish here?"
Many sailors flexed their biceps in response as if personally insulted and got to work.
Kitsara approached the first mate beside the steps to the helm.
"Could you show us how you steer with that? It looks fun~"
The man looked toward Narethi, who gave him permission to demonstrate. Kitsara leaned over the mechanism with an interest that soon had him pointing out its parts.

Blossom meanwhile squatted and jumped straight into the spotter's basket. She asked for tips on how to spot things better while pointedly aiming in the opposite direction from which Black Fang was approaching.
The Soul Reaper carried Black Fang over the rail behind the distracted sailors.
She stepped off the blade onto an empty stretch of deck. The Reaper slid back to his side while she passed behind the mast, emerging among the women gathered there.
Quinlan met her before she reached the crates.
"I forgot to warm you up all this time? My bad."
His hand came to rest against her back, warm through the drenched silk. He smiled at her while water lifted from her clothes in clear ribbons, gathering above his free palm.
Black Fang stopped beside him.
The cold weight left her robes. Her hair loosened against her shoulders as his magic drew the seawater from each strand, and the cloth at her waist softened beneath his hand.
He sent the water over the rail, watching her face.
"Better?"
She looked up at him and narrowed her eyes.
He had done exactly what she had imagined out on the ice, reaching for her as soon as he saw the water dripping from her clothes.
His attention stayed on her while the crew worked around them. He seemed far too pleased to have her beside him.
Across the deck, Ayame looked up from her conversation with Lucille. Her blue eyes found her sister staying beside Quinlan even after being dried, and her mouth began to curve.
Black Fang saw it.
For once, she let her sister smile.
With the battle loot collected, it was finally time to enter civilization!

chapters.title: Chapter 1962 Gathering Information
paragraphs: Quinlan stayed beside the merchantman's mast with Black Fang as Narethi passed them with the chart she had rolled up earlier.
"Captain, do you have time to tell us more about the region?"
"Of course, my lord."
Narethi brought the chart back to the crates. She glanced between him and the women gathering around him, then pressed a hand to her chest.
"Ah. How terribly rude of me. I haven't even given you my name. Narethi, my lord. Captain and owner of this vessel."
Her gaze moved toward the broken rail.
"Most of it, anyway."
"Your carpenter seems determined to keep the rest," Quinlan said.
Hammering answered from below. Narethi smiled at the sound, although her eyes were still sore from crying.
"I'd never hear the end of it if I let her sink after all his work."
She spread the chart across the crate, holding its corners down with pieces of broken timber. Quinlan took his hand from Black Fang's back and leaned over it.
"Where do you sail from?"

"Sarthal. Here, on the coast." Her finger found a harbour marked beside a broad stretch of land. "I carry goods between the coastal ports. Cloth on this journey, mostly, with tools and some medicines. Assuming the water hasn't ruined everything below..."
She stopped herself and smoothed a crease in the parchment.
"My apologies. You're hardly interested in my cargo."
"You have nothing to apologize for. I understand the value these goods hold for you and your crew."
After all, Quinlan was once a dejected salaryman himself.
Narethi looked up at him before a grateful smile returned to her face.
"Thank you."
Quinlan sat on the crate behind him, and Ayame settled beside him with her shoulder brushing his arm. Vex stood on his other side, while Lucille faced them with a cup a sailor had brought her.
Black Fang remained beside the mast, close enough to examine the chart over Narethi's shoulder.

"Would you recommend Sarthal for a longer visit?" Quinlan asked. "We'd like somewhere comfortable to stay while we explore the region. We're looking for a safe base location with good food, interesting places, and opportunities to keep ourselves occupied."
"With your wives? Certainly. You could spend a great deal of money enjoying yourselves there."
"That sounds promising already," Ayame approved.
Narethi's smile grew easier.
"There are merchants from all over, my lady. Whatever you're accustomed to at home, someone will probably sell it. And if you're looking for something unfamiliar, you can find that too."
"Blossom wants the unfamiliar food!! Master needs to take her on another food adventure!"
The dogkin called down from the spotter's basket, her blonde head appearing over its edge.
"I'll recommend places with generous portions," Narethi promised her, getting energetic tail wagging in return.
Quinlan chuckled, then followed the roads drawn inland from the harbour.
"And beyond the city? We'd rather do some travelling on land after this crossing."

"Then Sarthal is a good place to begin. These roads serve the farming settlements and the caravans coming down to the coast. Farther inland, you have hunting grounds, old ruins, mines... Though I'd recommend a local guide before you go wandering."
She moved her finger away from the roads.
"Some places are dangerous to enter. Others are dangerous to be caught entering."
"Whose permission would we need?" Aurora asked. "We aren't familiar with your borders. I'd hate to discover we'd offended someone after arriving at their gates."
"That depends where you travel, my lady. Sarthal governs the city and its surrounding lands. Beyond them, you begin crossing into our neighbours' territories."
Narethi indicated the boundaries in turn, letting them follow each one before continuing.

"These are the ones the caravans supplying us deal with. I can tell you where the usual crossings are, but farther inland I'd ask someone who actually travels there. I wouldn't trust my own advice with your safety."
Quinlan appreciated that answer considerably more than he would have appreciated a confident guess.
"Who governs Sarthal itself?"
"Queen Zorvanna. The dragonkin ruler."
Quinlan's eyes left the chart. Across it, Lucille was looking at him, her cup held halfway to her lips.
Dragonkin existed. They had a city, a ruler, and a merchant captain who mentioned them as casually as she mentioned her cargo.

<Dragonkin?!> Seraphiel's voice rang through the link. <We're going to a city full of dragonkin?>
<Apparently. Let's try to get as much info from her as we can without blowing our cover.>
<Got it.> Serika came around the mast and leaned over the map, resting her hands on her knees.
"I've heard of them, but haven't had the pleasure of meeting any. What are they like?"
"Terrifying warriors, my lady. Strong, and very skilled at using that strength. They're proud of it, too. If you want their respect, being able to fight is the best place to start."
"That sounds manageable," Serika said, smiling.
Narethi looked at the dried blood on her sleeve.
"After what I saw today, I imagine you'll get their attention. Though I'd be careful about accepting challenges before you know who you're dealing with."
"And Zorvanna is their queen?" Ayame asked. "Does she hold lands beyond the territory you've shown us? I only see a large city-state."
"No, my lady. The city and its surrounding lands are the only thing she rules."
Ayame glanced at the boundaries again.
"Queen is an unusual title for that holding... How did she come by it?"
"Don't let her hear you say such a thing," the naga captain whispered under her breath. Then, slyly, she added, "She crowned herself queen. Nobody objected. That's all there is to it."
Quinlan pressed his lips together. He could appreciate the simplicity of that arrangement.
Vex rested her forearm against his, studying the city mark.
"Is it mostly dragonkin in Sarthal, then?"
"Oh, no. You'd see far more people like my crew. Humans, naga, gnomes, and more... The dragonkin are few, and they have children rarely. They couldn't fill a city that size themselves."
She caught the chart's corner as the breeze lifted it.

"The dragonkin only want to fight. Farming, making clothes, buying cargo and carrying it across the sea... They'd rather leave that to the rest of us. So they let people settle in their city, provided we accept their rule."
"And people came," Lucille said.
"From all over. You can walk past a naga's shop, buy bread from a human, then take your tools to a kobold for repairs. The port keeps growing because there's work for all of us."
Narethi glanced toward her first mate, who was helping a sailor secure the damaged rail.
"My mate was born there. So were his parents. He complains every time I take him away from it."
"A family of settlers?" Quinlan asked.
"Originally from the north, he says. Seafarers. Though if you asked where he's from, he'd tell you Sarthal before you finished the question."
Quinlan looked at the human leaning over the rail.
The man was arguing about how much rope they needed. His home waited ahead of them, on a continent where humans hadn't even originated.
His ancestors had simply sailed away and made a life somewhere else.
<They could just up and leave their home continent whenever they so desired...> Ayame whispered. <It's so obvious, yet...>
Her shoulder pressed more firmly against Quinlan's.
<Yeah.>

They had known there was a world beyond Iskaris. But this man's family had crossed the world from what must've been the northern fjords, home to Dragnar's and Thyra's descendants. Seeing him here made their own confinement feel uglier.

'Like our vikings, traveling the world in their boats...' Quinlan mused inwardly at the image his mind created, then returned his attention to the chart before Narethi could wonder what interested him so much about a sailor tying knots.

"If you pay for what you buy and don't cause trouble, you can live very well. I own my ship. Other families own warehouses, workshops, houses. There's money to be made, and the city needs people willing to work."

"It earns me customers. Respect is harder." Narethi's mouth tightened. "Their soldiers need what we bring in, but being a merchant is still a lesser occupation to them. I'm grateful when they defend our walls... But I'd appreciate it if they could respect the work that keeps their soldiers fed just a bit more."

Narethi checked the helm, then looked back at Quinlan.

"I hope I haven't made the city sound unwelcoming. I've made a home there and many consider it the center of the world, the port city of freedom. But it's not perfect. "And I'd like you to keep answering that honestly," Quinlan nodded. "We're coming from far away. I'd rather learn the unpleasant parts here than discover them with my wives standing beside me in a street."
"Then... don't expect your title at home to settle an argument with a dragonkin. They'll be interested in your strength. Your ancestry may interest them considerably less."
"I see."
Ayame glanced up at him, her smile widening.
<We might've just found your people, my arrogant primordial~>
<I'm remarkably humble.>
<Yes, of course. And I'm an ugly goblin.>
<Took you long enough. Acceptance is the first step toward growth,> Iris spoke wisely.

Ayame and Iris nearly got into a catfight then and there, but a sailor approaching Narethi with a sodden strip of cloth interrupted them. She took it, rubbed the weave between her fingers, and asked him to bring the unopened bales above deck once the carpenter gave permission.

Narethi followed his gesture. The weapon lay where he had set it, its mounting broken and its bolt removed.

"Someone who benefits when your ships don't return."
"There are plenty of those. Our neighbouring nations would very much like our harbour, my lord. Until they can take it, making our trade more expensive seems to satisfy them."
She touched the coastal route on the chart.

"Hence the need for people like Garron," Quinlan said.
Narethi looked toward the gargoyle resting beside the companionway. His repaired wing was folded close to his body, and a sailor had placed a drink within reach of his good hand.
"Yes. He earned far more than I paid him today."
For a moment, her attention stayed on her wounded defender. Quinlan let her have it.
Then Ayame traced the edge of the city's territory without touching the ink.

<She did,> Aurora replied. <Whether she means that literally...>
Quinlan wanted that distinction settled very badly. He lifted his eyes to Narethi, keeping his question on the arrangements a visiting noble might reasonably care about.
