chapters.title: Chapter 1963 The Everclaiming
paragraphs: "No, my lord. The queen rules from Sarthal. Her Sovereign is a true dragon, with holdings far beyond our city. You won't be expected to present yourselves to her."
Ayame's fingers tightened against his sleeve beneath the edge of the crate.
An actual dragon owned the continent ahead of them.

Quinlan stared at the sprawling land on Narethi's chart, trying to imagine the being who could claim all of it. He wanted to see her. The desire arrived so strongly that he had to remind himself they were discussing someone whose attention might be extraordinarily dangerous.
They had met primordials. He had a demon living inside him. Even so, hearing that a dragon lived across this sea filled him with an excitement he couldn't dismiss as childish.
This was part of what he had wanted from coming here. Creatures he had only imagined, places he couldn't predict, a world that could still leave him staring in wonder.
<A real dragon...> Serika said. <Fuck. I'd like to see that.>
<From a sensible distance, please,> Aurora replied.
<At least until Quinnie is strong enough to confidently ravage her into submission!> Kitsara corrected.
<We can't be careless now...> Quinlan sighed. <If we mess up here we'll have a literal dragon matriarch on our asses.>
Vex looked down at him. For once, her excitement had left her without an immediate answer, and she tucked her hand around his arm while Narethi moved the timber covering an inland border.
Beside the mast, Black Fang was watching the captain intently.
"How does her rule affect travellers? Would we owe anything beyond the local fees?"

"Your ordinary business is with the local authorities. Their rulers, like Queen Zorvanna, pay her tribute. Unless you intend to involve yourselves with her possessions, I'd recommend learning the laws of the places you're visiting."
Quinlan looked across the borders Narethi had shown them. Every hostile neighbour she had mentioned occupied land belonging to this same dragon.
"She permits these conflicts in her sovereign territory?" he asked aloud.

"They've been happening for as long as I've traded here. Whoever holds the land still owes her tribute afterward. I couldn't tell you what she thinks of them, but she seems to not care much about the inner workings of her territory."
Narethi hesitated, then added, "Our queen is her daughter. That hasn't stopped anyone from trying to take Sarthal."
Lucille lowered her cup.
"Her daughter?"
"Yes, my lady."
"And that makes no difference?"
"We still hire guards. We still lose ships. When an army comes, it's the queen and her warriors who have to meet it. I've never seen her mother come to help."
Lucille stared down at the cup in her hands.
<That's foul.>

Quinlan agreed. He thought of Rosie at home, of her little hands catching his before he left. The idea of hearing that someone wanted to take her home from her and caring only whether they paid him afterward was as alien as possible to him.

"People talk, of course. But I carry cloth, my lord. I don't attend the Sovereign's court. I can tell you what it costs to bring goods through the harbour. What passes between her and her daughter..."
She shook her head.
"I won't pretend to know."
"Fair enough," Quinlan said.
Beside the mast, Black Fang shifted her gaze from the map to Narethi.
"The pirate captain. How would he compare to your queen and her strongest fighters?"
Narethi looked at the black-haired woman, then toward the sea behind them.
"He wouldn't have come near us if one of them had been aboard. Or if he had, he and his men would've died within moments."
Black Fang waited for her to continue.
"I don't know their exact levels," Narethi admitted. "The great figures keep that information close. They certainly don't share it with merchants asking about escort fees."
"Rumours?" Quinlan asked. "I'd like some idea of whose toes we should avoid stepping on."
"The strongest in the region are said to have passed level two hundred. Whether all the people claiming that know anything... I couldn't say."
Ayame's hand paused against the crate.
Two hundred.
The captain had been level 102. He had cut Quinlan through Synchra, and his men had hurt the women even with their surprise attack.
There were people here rumoured to be another hundred levels beyond him.

Quinlan felt excitement rising alongside his caution. He wanted to reach that strength, to discover what his classes would become with so many levels behind them. The world had finally given him fights worth seeking.
It could also kill the people he loved if he became careless.
<Let's be picky about who we annoy,> he told his women.
<For now,> Vex agreed.
"Does that include the Sovereign?" he asked Narethi.
"I couldn't even offer you a useful rumour about her, my lord."
"Then we'll start with something more approachable. Where would you recommend looking for work that involves travelling inland? Hunting, perhaps. Exploring somewhere worth seeing."
Narethi looked between him and his wives.
"Adventuring?"
"We're rather well equipped for it."
Her eyes went to the blood drying around the salvaged bow.
"Yes. I suppose you are."
Ayame squeezed his arm.
<We did register as adventurers once. Before someone decided he'd rather become a criminal.>
<It was fun, wasn't it?>
<No comment. But perhaps we could try completing a few more quests this time~>
He covered her hand with his while Narethi pointed inland again.
"The Adventurer's Guild has a branch in Sarthal. Merchants need escorts, people need creatures driven away, expeditions need fighters. You'd have plenty to choose from.

"I'm not sure how it is in your distant lands, but here, the Guild is a power in its own right, recognized across most continents. Its adventurers aren't sworn to the nation where they happen to be staying."
Narethi traced a road crossing the city's border.

"A neighbouring kingdom can go to war with Sarthal and still welcome adventurers from our branch. Its people need monsters killed too, lands charted, and other problems solved. Taking a contract here doesn't make you one of the queen's soldiers."
Ayame leaned forward to follow the road beneath the captain's finger.
"And the border guards accept that?"

"Generally. Though if nobody knows you and you arrive during a war, they may wonder whether you're a spy. A reputation helps. Someone whose deeds are known has an easier time explaining why they're travelling with weapons."
"Understandable," Quinlan said.
He liked the prospect considerably. They could make a home in the city, travel beyond it, and return without having to take its rulers' side in every dispute.
<We could actually see the continent,> Ayame said. <Without having to conquer our way across it.>
<What an alien concept,> Quinlan chuckled.
<...> The girls found it a bit less amusing.
"Why don't the dragonkin take that work themselves?" Vex asked. "There must be fights worth having."

"There are, but the dragonkin take pride in serving their queen. Most consider wandering off to fight for whoever offers a contract disloyal. They'll call adventurers wandering mercenaries, then tell you what a true dragonkin warrior ought to be."
"Even if the adventurer is stronger?" Serika asked.
Narethi smiled at her.
"That would make for an unpleasant argument, my lady. I'd prefer to be elsewhere when it happened."
The captain moved a piece of timber off the chart, uncovering the neighbouring territory.
"Their leaders still hire adventurers, though. That independence adventurers enjoy is very useful when they want something done across a border."
Aurora understood instantly. "If the queen sends soldiers and they're caught, her neighbour can point to them as proof that Sarthal acted against it. That gives them grounds to declare war."
Ayame looked from the border to Narethi.
"But if adventurers are caught, the queen can deny sending them."
"Exactly. They were pursuing a private contract. Whatever they did, she can say it had nothing to do with her. Unless the neighbour can prove otherwise, it loses that justification for war."
Lucille lowered her cup to the crate.
"And the people who accepted the contract are still across the border."
"Yes, my lady. I'd want to know very clearly what I was being paid to do before accepting that sort of work."
Quinlan studied the inland routes. There was enough land beyond them to keep the family occupied for a very long time, and enough trouble to make choosing their work worthwhile.
"We'd be more interested in the place and the challenge than the fee. Someone who knows the region would be useful company."
"Then I can introduce you to people who arrange expeditions. And help you find somewhere to stay while you choose. Somewhere suitable for your family."
"With a bath," Vex added immediately.
"A good one," Ayame agreed.
Narethi laughed, looking at the two women pressed against their armored husband.
"I'll make certain of it."
Above them, Blossom leaned over the basket again.
"And tasty local food!"
"And the food," the captain promised.
Quinlan caught the chart's edge as the wind lifted it, keeping the inland roads exposed beneath his hand.
"It's time to adventure, huh, ladies?"

Whoever holds the land still owes her tribute afterward.
I couldn't tell you what she thinks of them, but she seems to not care much about the inner workings of her territory."
Narethi hesitated, then added, "Our queen is her daughter.
That hasn't stopped anyone from trying to take Sarthal."
Lucille lowered her cup.
"Her daughter?"
"Yes, my lady."
"And that makes no difference?"
"We still hire guards.
We still lose ships.
When an army comes, it's the queen and her warriors who have to meet it.
I've never seen her mother come to help."
Lucille stared down at the cup in her hands.
<That's foul.>
Quinlan agreed.
He thought of Rosie at home, of her little hands catching his before he left.
The idea of hearing that someone wanted to take her home from her and caring only whether they paid him afterward was as alien as possible to him.
"People talk, of course.
But I carry cloth, my lord.
I don't attend the Sovereign's court.
I can tell you what it costs to bring goods through the harbour.
What passes between her and her daughter..."
She shook her head.
"I won't pretend to know."
"Fair enough," Quinlan said.
Beside the mast, Black Fang shifted her gaze from the map to Narethi.
"The pirate captain.
How would he compare to your queen and her strongest fighters?"
Narethi looked at the black-haired woman, then toward the sea behind them.
"He wouldn't have come near us if one of them had been aboard.
Or if he had, he and his men would've died within moments."
Black Fang waited for her to continue.
"I don't know their exact levels," Narethi admitted.
"The great figures keep that information close.
They certainly don't share it with merchants asking about escort fees."
"Rumours?" Quinlan asked.
"I'd like some idea of whose toes we should avoid stepping on."
"The strongest in the region are said to have passed level two hundred.
Whether all the people claiming that know anything...
I couldn't say."
Ayame's hand paused against the crate.
Two hundred.
The captain had been level 102.
He had cut Quinlan through Synchra, and his men had hurt the women even with their surprise attack.
There were people here rumoured to be another hundred levels beyond him.
Quinlan felt excitement rising alongside his caution.
He wanted to reach that strength, to discover what his classes would become with so many levels behind them.
The world had finally given him fights worth seeking.
It could also kill the people he loved if he became careless.
<Let's be picky about who we annoy,> he told his women.
<For now,> Vex agreed.
"Does that include the Sovereign?" he asked Narethi.
"I couldn't even offer you a useful rumour about her, my lord."
"Then we'll start with something more approachable.
Where would you recommend looking for work that involves travelling inland?
Hunting, perhaps.
Exploring somewhere worth seeing."
Narethi looked between him and his wives.
"Adventuring?"
"We're rather well equipped for it."
Her eyes went to the blood drying around the salvaged bow.
"Yes.
I suppose you are."
Ayame squeezed his arm.
<We did register as adventurers once.
Before someone decided he'd rather become a criminal.>
<It was fun, wasn't it?>
<No comment.
But perhaps we could try completing a few more quests this time~>
He covered her hand with his while Narethi pointed inland again.
"The Adventurer's Guild has a branch in Sarthal.
Merchants need escorts, people need creatures driven away, expeditions need fighters.
You'd have plenty to choose from.
"I'm not sure how it is in your distant lands, but here, the Guild is a power in its own right, recognized across most continents.
Its adventurers aren't sworn to the nation where they happen to be staying."
Narethi traced a road crossing the city's border.
"A neighbouring kingdom can go to war with Sarthal and still welcome adventurers from our branch.
Its people need monsters killed too, lands charted, and other problems solved.
Taking a contract here doesn't make you one of the queen's soldiers."
Ayame leaned forward to follow the road beneath the captain's finger.
"And the border guards accept that?"
"Generally.
Though if nobody knows you and you arrive during a war, they may wonder whether you're a spy.
A reputation helps.
Someone whose deeds are known has an easier time explaining why they're travelling with weapons."
"Understandable," Quinlan said.
He liked the prospect considerably.
They could make a home in the city, travel beyond it, and return without having to take its rulers' side in every dispute.
<We could actually see the continent,> Ayame said.
<Without having to conquer our way across it.>
<What an alien concept,> Quinlan chuckled.
<...> The girls found it a bit less amusing.
"Why don't the dragonkin take that work themselves?" Vex asked.
"There must be fights worth having."
"There are, but the dragonkin take pride in serving their queen.
Most consider wandering off to fight for whoever offers a contract disloyal.
They'll call adventurers wandering mercenaries, then tell you what a true dragonkin warrior ought to be."
"Even if the adventurer is stronger?" Serika asked.
Narethi smiled at her.
"That would make for an unpleasant argument, my lady.
I'd prefer to be elsewhere when it happened."
The captain moved a piece of timber off the chart, uncovering the neighbouring territory.
"Their leaders still hire adventurers, though.
That independence adventurers enjoy is very useful when they want something done across a border."
Aurora understood instantly.
"If the queen sends soldiers and they're caught, her neighbour can point to them as proof that Sarthal acted against it.
That gives them grounds to declare war."
Ayame looked from the border to Narethi.
"But if adventurers are caught, the queen can deny sending them."
"Exactly.
They were pursuing a private contract.
Whatever they did, she can say it had nothing to do with her.
Unless the neighbour can prove otherwise, it loses that justification for war."
Lucille lowered her cup to the crate.
"And the people who accepted the contract are still across the border."
"Yes, my lady.
I'd want to know very clearly what I was being paid to do before accepting that sort of work."
Quinlan studied the inland routes.
There was enough land beyond them to keep the family occupied for a very long time, and enough trouble to make choosing their work worthwhile.
"We'd be more interested in the place and the challenge than the fee.
Someone who knows the region would be useful company."
"Then I can introduce you to people who arrange expeditions.
And help you find somewhere to stay while you choose.
Somewhere suitable for your family."
"With a bath," Vex added immediately.
"A good one," Ayame agreed.
Narethi laughed, looking at the two women pressed against their armored husband.
"I'll make certain of it."
Above them, Blossom leaned over the basket again.
"And tasty local food!"
"And the food," the captain promised.
Quinlan caught the chart's edge as the wind lifted it, keeping the inland roads exposed beneath his hand.
"It's time to adventure, huh, ladies?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1964 Meeting the Dragonkin
paragraphs: Quinlan stood at the merchantman's repaired rail as Narethi's crew brought them toward Sarthal, watching ships emerge from behind the harbour walls.
There were so many of them.

A broad cargo vessel passed close enough for Blossom to wave at the children peering over its side. Beyond it, masts crowded the waterfront, where cranes swung loads onto quays packed with wagons and shouting workers.
The city climbed inland behind them. Quinlan followed its roofs toward distant walls, then lost the streets among towers and rising smoke.
"We could stay here for a while," he finally commented.
"We could get lost here for a while," Aurora replied, leaning beside him.
"Blossom can find everyone!"
His dogkin lifted her nose, sniffed enthusiastically, and turned toward a passing boat carrying baskets beneath damp cloth.
"Master, Blossom doesn't know that smell!!"
"It's exciting, huh? There's so much to discover."
"Yes!"
Quinlan watched the little boat disappear behind a larger hull while Seraphiel pulled her hood forward against the breeze.
Her long ears remained concealed beneath it. Kaelira wore hers up too, the cloth falling around her violet hair.
They had covered their ears before meeting Narethi, at Quinlan's request.
He knew how readily people on Iskaris had treated elven women as things to capture, buy, and fuck. Until he understood these people, he wanted that particular attention kept away from his lovers.
More importantly, he wasn't even certain elves lived outside Iskaris.

He knew of only two elven primordials. Humans had their distant homelands, and beastkin were certainly curious and brave enough to venture out before Iskaris faced the Suppression, but he could easily imagine elves remaining content in their forests while the other races spread across the world.
Perhaps their ears would draw ordinary curiosity here. Perhaps someone would look at his women and begin calculating a selling price or worse.
The uncertainty was enough to keep the hoods in place.
Seraphiel caught him checking hers and smiled beneath its edge.
<Perhaps I can pretend to be your sex slave again? I much prefer my belly dancer attire to this...>
<Please bear with it for me.>
<Hmm~ I suppose I shall consider it for just a little bit~>
<And you call me slutty? Look at this bitch trying to show off her body to the whole world...> Kitsara muttered with obvious dissatisfaction.
<Oi, foxy.> Seraphiel's tone lost its purr.
Kaelira was looking past them at a crane lifting a loaded wagon bodily off a ship. Her hood turned with the swinging load until Seraphiel caught her sleeve before she leaned too far over the rail.
"We can investigate once we're ashore."
"I can see how it works. I want to know what they're using for the joints."
Narethi came down from the helm as sailors began calling to the quay. People gathered opposite the damaged rail, pointing toward the replacement timbers.
"Narethi! What happened?!"
The captain called back, but a woman on the dock was already shouting a sailor's name. He appeared beside Quinlan, waving both arms until she saw him.
Her hands covered her face.
Quinlan moved aside to give the man room. Across the deck, other crew members were hurrying toward familiar voices, smiling through the exhaustion.
Narethi watched them while the gangplank was lowered.
Then she saw someone still searching the faces along the rail, and her smile faltered.
"Excuse me, my lord."
"Of course."
She went down first.
Quinlan stayed with his women while the captain took the waiting man's hands. He couldn't hear what she said over the workers calling for ropes.
He saw the man shake his head, then try to look past her toward the ship.
Lucille's hand found Quinlan's.
They waited until Narethi turned back to them.
The soldiers stopped Quinlan at the foot of the gangplank.

Quinlan noticed the woman first. Around a metre seventy-five, she had long auburn hair spilling between swept-back horns, with copper scales framing a beautiful face. Her full lips curved as her golden, slit-pupilled eyes met his.

Fitted armour hugged her bust and waist, leaving patches of scales visible along her muscular arms and outer thighs. A thick copper tail curled beside her leg, its pale underside exposed as she lifted the tip.
Her tail, however, was nothing like a demon's or a beastkin's; it was full of muscle, weighty, meant as a fifth limb for physical warfare.
'So this is it... A dragonkin.'
The man beside her stood around two metres ten, broad-shouldered and more heavily scaled. Charcoal plates climbed his neck toward his golden eyes, and a dark, ridged tail curved behind his boots.
Quinlan felt a thrill at the sight of them. With natural armour over powerful bodies, they looked like a race bred for war. He wanted badly to see them fight.
'And they're only the port guards...'
The man was already examining Synchra before moving his attention to the women descending behind Quinlan.
"These are the passengers you reported?" he asked Narethi, his voice resonating in his chest with a low growl beneath the words.
"The people who saved us."
"They weren't aboard when you departed."
"We met them at sea."
His eyes returned to Quinlan's helmet.
"On what vessel?"
"We travelled by magic," Quinlan answered.
"You carried this many across the sea?" The dragonkin's nostrils widened as he looked Quinlan over. "You?"
"Yes. I have an artifact that lets us rest when I run out of mana."
"What artifact?"
"I'd rather that stayed private until I know I can trust this city with personal information."
The growl deepened in the soldier's throat. His pointed nails pressed against his belt, but he let the refusal pass while looking toward Lilith's sword, then Black Fang's blade.
"And what business brings you here?"
"My wives and I are travelling the world. Your captain recommended Sarthal. We'd like somewhere to stay and a chance to see the region."
"His honeymoon," Narethi supplied. "He took his wives on an adventure to celebrate their marriage."

The female dragonkin released an amused huff, her gaze travelling from Quinlan's shoulders down to his saber. The prospect of a man taking his mates into dangerous foreign lands plainly appealed to her.
"Taking your women out to see what you can kill?" Her voice had a throaty rasp, rough even through her amusement. "That is a marriage custom I can appreciate. Which land do you hail from?"
"A long way from here."
"How informative," the man rumbled. "Take off the helmet."
Quinlan remained where he was.
"I'll keep it on."
The woman's nails tapped against her sword's pommel as she watched him refuse. Behind Quinlan, Ayame stepped off the gangplank and came to his side.
"That will not stand," the man growled, baring the points of his teeth. "Whatever your servants tolerate at home, foreigner, you stand before dragonkin here. You don't set the terms."
Quinlan looked at the pair of guards, then simply shrugged. "Okay. If we're unwelcome, we'll go elsewhere. Thank you for your time."
He turned toward his companions.
"Shall we? We can look farther along the coast."
"Certainly," Vex smiled. "I don't like how they look at you, Hubby. Let's find more hospitable people."
Quinlan was disappointed. He had wanted to explore the enormous city beyond the warehouses, and Blossom was still trying to locate whatever scents had caught her nose.
But they had an entire world ahead of them. He could find another harbour, another inn, another place worth visiting with his family.
He certainly wasn't going to argue with hostile guards or reveal his cards just to gain entrance.
Vex slipped her arm through his while the Lilies began turning away from the gangplank. The male guard watched them, his mouth closing before he could find another accusation.
"They're leaving Sarthal so readily...?" he muttered, his bafflement carrying through the rumble. "The center of the world?"

As a prideful dragonkin, he struggled to understand such a concept. His city was the best because it was ruled by dragonkin. The lesser races arriving every day to live beneath their protection only confirmed that belief.
He had expected resistance, followed by an excuse to comply. The foreigner was leaving with the same easy confidence with which he had approached.
"Hmm~" The female dragonkin's interest only grew. This tall, masked man had finally given her something worth watching during a boring guard duty.
Quinlan glanced back at the pleased sound. Her lips parted, and a long, dark tongue curled over her upper lip, reaching past the corner of her mouth before slipping between her teeth again.
She held Quinlan's gaze through the entire movement as she muttered, "I want to see what's beneath that armor..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1965 Curiosity
paragraphs: Vex pressed closer to him, her red eyes narrowing at the dragonkin.
"Wait, please!" Narethi spoke up suddenly.
She moved between Quinlan and the guards, her tail curling clear of a porter carrying a coil of rope.
"I vouch for them. Put it against my name. You know where I berth, where I trade, and where I live."
"You met them today," the female dragonkin said.
"Yes. While they were saving my crew. Without them, I'd be dead... or worse."
Her voice shook. She steadied it before continuing.

"I watched them fight the men who were killing us. I watched them heal Garron and pull my sailors from the sea. They asked me for directions afterward. That's what these suspicious strangers wanted from me."
The woman glanced past her at the crew unloading their dead.
Narethi kept her eyes on the man blocking their way.
"Will you accept my guarantee?"
He studied the captain before looking at Quinlan again.
"Any trouble you cause comes back to her."
"..." Quinlan didn't reply instantly. He didn't like being indebted, especially because with his rowdy girls, he couldn't be sure they'd not cause trouble.
The female dragonkin watched his hesitation, then grinned, showing the sharp points of her canines between full lips.
"Worry not, man from far away. 'Trouble' for us dragonkin means grave crimes against the crown."
She chuckled, a rough sound deep in her throat.
"Starting a fight, especially one you win, will not get this merchant punished."
Now that, Quinlan could accept much more readily. "I understand. Thank you for the explanation."
"You're welcome~" she purred, looking him over again.
The male guard moved aside and curled his tail behind his boots, clearing the passage beside the stacked cargo.
"Don't make her regret it."
Narethi released a breath and led them through. Quinlan inclined his head to her as they passed the first warehouse.
"Thank you for putting your name behind us. I'll not forget your kindness."
"Of course, my lord."
She looked at her crew again, then pointed them toward the street beyond the docks.
"Now. I promised you a bath."
Lucille moved closer to Quinlan as Narethi led them into the inn. A server was carrying used dishes out of the dining room, and Lucille drew Quinlan aside to leave the passage clear.
"Perhaps we could wait here while the captain arranges things?" she suggested to the others, indicating the space beside the stairs.
Narethi approached the counter and began discussing rooms with the innkeeper. Lucille watched a maid hurry upstairs with folded linen, then smiled at Quinlan.
<We've just ruined someone's peaceful afternoon.>
<We haven't done anything yet.>
<Baby, look how many of us there are. Rooms to prepare, baths to fill, everyone wanting to eat at once... I'd be sending someone into the kitchen already.>
The innkeeper turned and called through an open doorway behind the counter. Lucille's smile widened.
<There she goes.>
Quinlan chuckled beneath his helmet. His Bloodmonger was at home when it came to the topic of innkeeping, visibly perking up at the opportunity to finally be the most knowledgeable about something.
"Could we have rooms facing the courtyard?" Lucille asked when the innkeeper returned. "And whatever the kitchen can comfortably manage for lunch. We're happy to wait until after we've washed."
"That would help considerably, my lady."
"How lovely. Perhaps someone could help us, too?"

The voice came from a woman seated beside a pair of travelling trunks. Chestnut curls framed a pretty face pinched with exhaustion, and her gloved fingers drummed against her knee as she looked over Quinlan's company.
"We arrived first."
Her husband stood beside the luggage in a fine coat dusty from travel. He leaned toward the counter immediately.
"My partner has had a very tiring journey. Surely our room takes precedence over accommodating an entire procession?"
Lucille glanced at the innkeeper.
"Are we holding up their room?"
"No, my lady. Their linen is being changed."
"Still?" The woman puffed out a breath. "You said this was a respectable establishment."
"It came highly recommended," he assured her, then inspected the others with obvious distaste. "Though apparently they aren't particular about their clientele."
Lucille's smile remained pleasant.
"Clean sheets take a little time. I'm sure you'd prefer them."
"I would prefer to sleep."
"Then we'll try to leave the staff free to finish your room."
"Damned plebeians can't even clean clothes quickly..." The woman scoffed and looked away. "I can't stand this any longer. Andre, do something."
The man hurried to lift her cloak from the neighbouring chair before she could reach for it herself.
"You'll be upstairs soon. I'll speak to someone."
"Now."
Lucille returned her attention to the counter, her hand resting comfortably on Quinlan's arm.
<Someone never had her parents say no...>

<Pampered brats exist all over the world, huh?> Quinlan chuckled, more amused than offended. As far as he was concerned, this was just a bitch throwing a tantrum, nothing more. Though that could change rapidly if she kept talking to Lucille in such a manner.
The innkeeper nodded at their naga friend.
"I'll have someone show you upstairs."
Narethi asked for the total, including the baths and food. Quinlan listened as the woman quoted a sum in crowns, then watched the captain count dark coins onto the counter.
'Different currency.'
Pale lines gleamed inside the metal as the innkeeper turned them beneath the light. She counted them into a drawer and returned smaller coins, which Narethi tucked into her purse.
Quinlan compared the payment with the symbols on the price board behind her. The currency was unfamiliar, but he could learn what people called it and how they spent it by watching.
Narethi came back to them.
"Your stay is my treat, my lord. Please enjoy yourselves."
"I'm grateful."
"And an excellent choice of inn," Lucille added. "I think we'll be comfortable here."
Narethi looked pleased. She gave them directions to the Adventurer's Guild before returning to her people at the harbour.

Upstairs, the promised bath occupied a sunlit room overlooking an inner courtyard. Lucille tested the water while the others came in, then reached automatically for the towels a maid was setting down.
"I'll take those, thank you."
She distributed them before noticing Quinlan watching her.
"What?"
"Are you staying here or working here?"
Lucille looked down at the last towel in her hands and laughed.
"Oh, shush. She had her hands full."

He closed the door after the maid left. Once the family was alone, and they ascertained the absence of spying artifacts or spells, Synchra withdrew from his face and Lucille laid the towel aside to cup his cheek.
"There you are. I was beginning to miss that face."
Quinlan smiled and drew Lucille against him. She settled comfortably beneath his arm, looking out at the unfamiliar roofs beyond their window.
"I'd like to earn our spending money here," he told her and the others. "Using our valuables to trade is too risky when we know so little."
"Then we'll find something worth doing," Lucille hugged him tight. "Though perhaps we should learn what dinner costs before promising to pay for it with our earnings."
"We have gold if we need it. None of you will starve on my watch."
For now, he liked the prospect of earning local money and spending it on whatever caught their interest.
Lucille kissed his cheek before slipping out from beneath his arm.
"First, a bath." Her clothes began dropping with concerning speed.
"Then, the Adventurer's Guild," Ayame grinned, shedding her own clothes quickly. "I can't wait."

"She'll hear you..." Lucille buried her face against the edge of the bath while Ayame disappeared beneath the water again, bubbles escaping around her as she failed to contain herself.
Marielle began hammering against the other side.
"They're laughing at me!
Andre!!!"
"The innkeeper promised me the walls aren't thin enough to hear normal conversation..."
"Do not take their side!
I know these cunts heard us!"
Sera pressed both hands over her mouth.
Her long ears trembled with the effort of keeping the next laugh inside.
Blossom's nose twitched against Quinlan's cheek.
She paused halfway into another kiss and turned toward the open window.
The afternoon breeze carried the harbour's salt into the room, mixed with smoke, unfamiliar spices, and food being cooked somewhere in the streets below.
"Master...
Blossom still doesn't know that smell."
Quinlan followed her gaze past the courtyard roofs.
They had seen the harbour and walked through the city, yet hearing the wonder in her voice made the distance they had crossed settle over the room.
Ayame rose from the water and pushed her hair away from her face.
"We're really here, huh...?"
The laughter softened.
They were naked together in a bath belonging to an inn on another continent.
Outside that window lived races they had never encountered, food they had never tasted, cities and ruins that had never appeared on any map they knew.
An actual dragon claimed the land beneath them, and people stronger than anyone born beneath the Heavenly Restriction treated this enormous world as their home.
For their entire lives, leaving Iskaris was not even a concept they entertained.
It was just that outlandish of an idea.
Now the sea lay behind them.
Quinlan looked around at his women.
Their bodies were tired and bruised beneath the clean skin, but excitement was already returning to their faces.
"A different continent," Lucille murmured.
Her green eyes moved toward the window.
"We actually crossed the sea."
"And met dragonkin on our first day," Seraphiel added, abandoning Marielle to hurry back to the bath, snuggling between Serika and Kaelira.
"Real dragonkin!
Did you see that woman's tongue?!"
"I saw where she was looking while she used it," Vex replied.
Her arms tightened possessively around Quinlan's neck.
Ayame drifted closer and rested her arms across his knees.
"An Adventurer's Guild is waiting for us.
We can take contracts, travel wherever we please, explore whatever interesting things we find." Her smile widened with every word.
"Quin, there is so much to see."
"And eat!" Blossom remembered, bouncing on his thigh.
"Master promised Blossom a food adventure!"
Kitsara lifted one limp tail from the towels.
"Foreign food, foreign monsters, foreign beds...
Best honeymoon ever~"
The room erupted around Quinlan as his women began talking over one another.
Exhaustion had delayed their excitement until they finally felt safe enough to relax, and now every possibility seemed to arrive at once.
Quinlan listened with Vex and Blossom warm against him, surrounded by the women he had brought across the sea.
"We'll see all of it," he promised.
By the time the inn's staff brought food upstairs, the family had reluctantly left the bath and dressed.
Quinlan sat beside the open window with a plate while Blossom discovered which of the unfamiliar dishes she wanted again.
All of them, apparently.
The Lilies had taken rooms farther down the corridor.
They joined the family after bathing, Lilith arriving with her silver hair still damp and Void, for once, walking on her own two feet.
"Ready?" the captain asked.
"I want to see how the Guild differs here."
Quinlan set his empty plate down.
Synchra closed over his face as he stood, and Seraphiel checked Kaelira's hood before pulling up her own.
"Let's find out."
Following Narethi's directions through the afternoon traffic, they found the Adventurer's Guild by a square crowded with wagons.
Quinlan could hear an argument about a damaged wheel before he reached the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 1969 Registering as Adventurers
paragraphs: He pushed open the door and stepped into a hall lined with contract boards. Counters occupied the far wall, with drinking tables filling the space to his right.
"I'm telling you, the wheel was already-"
The speaker stopped as Vex entered beside Quinlan.
"Damn! Anyone know her name?"
"They look like seasoned veterans but I never heard of them... What's their rank?"
Such questions sounded as Ayame followed, then Lucille and the others. A man carrying a tray turned to watch them until the mugs slid against one another.
"Careful!"
He caught the tray against his chest, spilling beer down his shirt.
Quinlan surveyed the hall through Synchra. Men were staring openly at Serika's tanned legs, at the curves beneath Seraphiel's travelling cloak, at Blossom's tail brushing through the doorway.

The attention spread as his companions kept entering. Lilith walked past the staring tables with her sword at her hip, Bronnya beside her, and more than one mouth closed at the sight of their weapons.
<Quite an entrance,> Aurora observed.
<Blossom doesn't like how they smell.>
<We won't ask you to sit with them,> Ayame promised.
Quinlan approached a registration counter while the women gathered around him. Serika and Kitsara took the open space to his right, facing the clerk with their backs toward the drinking tables.
The human clerk looked over Quinlan's shoulder at the crowd before setting a stack of forms on her desk. Quinlan glanced at the questions on the top sheet, leaving the pen where it was.
"New registrations?"
"We're considering it. We know the basics, but could you give us a general overview before we sign up for anything?"
"Certainly. Are you all registering together?"
"Two parties," Lilith answered, coming to his left.
Quinlan indicated his own companions.
"There are twelve of us in mine. Is that a problem?"
"Not a problem. Though depending on what quest you accept, you might find yourselves sharing a very modest reward among a great many people."
She pointed toward the boards nearest the entrance.
"If someone needs herbs collected or a stretch of road inspected, they pay for that task. Bringing twelve people won't make them pay twelve times as much."
"Could we take several jobs and divide the work?" Serika asked.
"Depending on your rank, yes. For starters, we do not allow such a thing to protect our members from their own ambition.

"But if you're permitted to split up, you'd tell us who's going on each quest so we can check that the people actually doing the work meet its requirements. You can remain one party in our register while completing separate contracts."
Ayame leaned against his arm. <They're protecting you against your own ambition~ Who knew Sarthal would be so prepared to house our arrogant primordial?>
Quinlan's mouth twitched, especially as he heard a certain petite samurai's delicate giggling in his mind.

"Your numbers can also be an advantage," the clerk continued. "Big contracts have a minimum headcount that surpasses your average team's numbers. We won't authorize a departure until enough qualified adventurers have signed on.
"Clearing a large infestation, for example. You need people watching the exits while others go inside. An expedition might need guards for its camp as well as fighters accompanying the explorers."
She turned a notice lying beside her ledger so they could see the requirements beneath its description.
"Usually several parties join together to fill those places. A large enough party can take the whole contract itself, provided it meets the other conditions too."

Now that sounded even better. His women knew how to fight together, and he trusted them with his life. Getting to explore a ruin with them without some stranger deciding he ought to lead the expedition sounded excellent.
Quinlan read farther down the sheet. Alongside the headcount, a minimum grade was listed.
"My partners and I are quite a bit more powerful than your hopefuls with pitchforks. Can our starting rank reflect that?"
"I'm afraid not..." The clerk carefully shook her head. It was clear to all that she had to fight a great number of arrogant people demanding to be given a higher rank.

"Your rank reflects your standing with the Guild. A new registration starts at Grade One, no matter how individually powerful. Completed contracts build your record, and we review that record for promotion. The higher the grade, the more demanding the work we'll entrust to you."
'Grade One? Their system is different.'
On Iskaris, ranks went from Iron to Adamantite.
The ladies were pondering the same thing, creating a moment of silence.

The clerk took it as them being dissatisfied with her answer, quickly adding, "Being able to kill a monster doesn't tell me whether you'll abandon a caravan halfway to its destination, or if you know how to proceed in other delicate situations.
"As adventurers you represent our organization, so we need to know that you'll finish what you agree to do."
"...Fair enough. What information do you need from us?"

"The name you'll work under and a way to contact you while you're staying in the city. If you use a working name, please keep using it. Your completed jobs need to remain attached to the same person."
Quinlan wrote Black, then passed the remaining forms along the counter. The women used their usual names, leaving surnames and titles off the sheets.
Their names were never announced universally by the Soul Records; thus, only Quinlan had to use an alias.
Ayame read his entry and smiled. <Lord Black again?>
<Just Black this time.>
Behind them, a chair scraped across the floor.
"Grade One," a man repeated. "Fuck me. I thought someone important had walked in."
Quinlan glanced toward the nearest drinking table. It stood beside the passage along the counters, with three men seated around a collection of empty mugs.
The speaker wore a padded coat with grease darkening its collar. He had turned his chair to face the women, his legs spread across half the passage.
"That's a lot of protection for a nobody. Your daddy pay for all that?"
Quinlan returned his attention to the form. Beside him, Vex laid her completed sheet on the counter.
"Daddy paid for the women too," the blond man across the table suggested. "Look at them. You think they're following him around for his charming personality?"
"What personality? He hasn't got a face!"
The third man, whose nose bent sharply to one side, slapped his friend's shoulder and barked a laugh.
"Hasn't got a face! Hah! Probably scared they'll all run off if he takes that thing off."
"I'd keep it on too if I had that lot. Fucking hell, look at the redhead..."
The greasy man's eyes travelled up Serika's legs and stopped at her chest. He leaned sideways in his chair when Kitsara stepped between him and his view.
Then he noticed the foxkin's ass.
"Oh, come on. That's just unfair."
"Sharing is caring, you know?"
His friends laughed again. The blond lifted his mug toward Kitsara, sloshing beer across his fingers.
"Oi, foxy! We've got a spare chair here. Or you can sit on my lap if you prefer."
Kitsara passed a pen to Serika without looking at him.
"She prefers the lap," his crooked-nosed friend announced. "Look at her. That's a woman who appreciates a comfortable seat."
"Mine's fucking comfortable."
"You'll have to move your gut first."
The blond shoved him, laughing hard enough to spill more beer. He wiped his hand down his trousers before calling after Kitsara again.
"Don't listen to this prick, sweetheart. Come over here and I'll buy you something better than whatever your Grade One nobody lets you drink."
"Yeah! We're Grade Two bigshots about to enter Grade Three!"
Quinlan heard every word. Anger was growing beneath his armour, made uglier by the ease with which these bastards discussed his women as things to borrow for an evening.
"It's them again..." a woman muttered under her breath, face scrunched in visible disgust. "There are ten grades. Why are they so boastful about picking herbs for a hundred years?"
Quinlan aligned Vex's finished form beside his own while the clerk checked their entries. Ayame's fingers had stopped moving over her pen, and Vex was glaring at the men.
The blond saw her looking.
"There we go. That one's interested."
"In you? She's looking at me."
"Keep dreaming. You've got a wife."
"Bah! Don't remind me of that ancient harlot. I've been thinking of changing her anyhow."
Their table erupted. The crooked-nosed man leaned back, delighted with himself.
The clerk returned a sheet that needed their team name declared. Quinlan accepted it.
"How much is he paying you, then?" the greasy man called. "Must be a fortune to keep you all smiling at him."
Serika collected the finished sheets from the far end of the counter. Carrying them back to Quinlan took her along the narrow passage beside the men's table.
"Here comes one," the blond muttered loudly. "Told you."
"Not to you, she isn't."
The greasy man sat forward, smoothing a hand over his stained coat as Serika approached.
"You getting bored over there, gorgeous? Come have a drink with men who've actually done something. We could show you around. Get you out of that armour for a bit."
"Give her a proper welcome," his friend added, grinning up at her.
Serika walked past them, her expression empty as if she didn't even realize they existed. The greasy man seemingly mistook her refusal to stop for an invitation to lean farther out of his chair.
"Aw, don't be like that. I can afford you."
He reached for her hip.
And just like that, the room erupted.

chapters.title: Chapter 1970 Proper Introduction
paragraphs: Quinlan remained facing the registration counter in the Adventurer's Guild as the drunk behind him reached for Serika's hip.
"[Wind Blade]."
His magic compressed the air above the outstretched arm into a thin cutting edge. He drove it down through the padded sleeve, flesh, and bone just above the elbow.
*Shhk!*
The man's arm struck the floor with a wet slap, its open hand bouncing against Serika's boot. Blood spurted from the severed upper arm and splashed across the mugs on his table.
He stared at the stump, his mouth working soundlessly until another pulse of blood struck his friend's face.
"MY ARM! AAAAH!"
Quinlan dipped his pen in the ink.

The drunk began to rise from his chair. Blossom flashed across from the counter and appeared behind the man. She caught his hair, wrenching his head back while her claw gauntlet aimed its sharp edges against his exposed throat.
He tried to bend over his bleeding stump, but she pulled his head back until he felt the metal against his throat.
A single droplet of blood ran from beneath Blossom's claw toward his chest.
"W-why are you bastards just staring? Help!" he cried toward his table.
"H-how dare you?!" The blond dropped his mug and reached for the sword at his belt, finally finding his voice. The mug struck the floor with a clang, spilling beer into the blood.

Ayame drew her katana as she crossed from the counter in the blink of an eye, sliding it beneath his chin before he could pull his sword free. She lifted the edge, forcing him upright with a thin red cut opening across his neck.
"I wouldn't draw that if I were you."
"M-mercy...!"
His hand sprang away from the hilt. Scar slipped behind the crooked-nosed man's chair with both daggers drawn, bringing their points against his back just as he shoved his seat away from the table.
"Aagh! Fuck!"
He had driven himself onto both blades. When he lurched forward, Scar followed, keeping their points buried beneath his shoulder blades.
"Sit still."
Around them, adventurers scrambled out of their seats, overturning a bench in their haste to get clear of the blood spreading beneath the table.
"A healer! Someone get a fucking healer!"
The wounded man's plea broke into another scream as his remaining hand closed around the stump. Blood squeezed between his fingers and ran down his wrist.
Blossom held him by the hair while he writhed. She wanted to open his throat for what he had tried to do to Serika, and the frightened eyes straining upward toward her found no mercy in her face.
"To appreciate the beauty of my wives is natural," Quinlan finally spoke, still facing the counter. "After all, they are the most amazing women in existence."
His pen moved across the returned form, spelling out the inn's name in the space for their address.
"But to make crude remarks about them, to suggest their love can be bought, and then presume to touch them..."
"Please! I'm sorry! Please, my arm..."
Quinlan finished the final letter while the man choked on his own pleading. Serika laid the remaining forms beside his elbow, her fingers hot against his wrist when she touched him.
"...is nothing but suicidal," he finished.
Quinlan set the pen down and covered Serika's fingers with his free hand.
"We're new in Sarthal, unaware of your customs. That's why I only took your arm, not your head. But if grabbing women like that is a part of your culture..."
"It fucking isn't! Harl, you know damn well it isn't!"
The woman who had mocked their herb-picking stood beside the overturned bench. Her face had gone red with fury, and she pointed straight at the bleeding man in the greasy padded coat.
"Don't let these disgusting bastards paint the picture of this wonderful city! They think being close to Grade Three means they can do whatever they want to anyone beneath them!"
"We were only having a laugh," the crooked-nosed man protested.

"Were you, Dask?" A short-haired woman pushed away from the wall to confront him. "Was it funny when you caught my ass at this counter? When I told you to let go and you asked whether I'd like to lose my teeth?"
Dask's eyes flicked to the clerk.
"That wasn't... You walked into me!"

"There!" She threw a hand toward him, disgust twisting her mouth. "That's what he does. Grabs a lower-grade woman, threatens her, then claims she imagined it. Apparently we all keep walking into his fucking hands!"
"Every woman detests them. Just one look is enough to paint the full picture, even if they haven't tried grabbing you personally..." the first woman said.
"Their poor wives are so miserable..." another whispered, dejected. "When these sons of bitches are out 'working,' we tend to visit them to lift their spirits."
Similarly angry voices answered from farther back. Women who had moved out of the fight's path were coming closer again, staring at the men trapped in their chairs.
"Go on, then," the short-haired woman challenged. "Tell her she'll lose her teeth too."
She pointed at Serika. Dask stared at the floor, trembling against Scar's daggers.
Harl sucked in a ragged breath. The blond had begun crying, blood from his friend's stump freckling his cheeks.

Serika looked down at the gloved hand covering hers, then squeezed it before turning back toward the table. Heat rolled from her body, driving the adventurer at the neighbouring counter away from her.
Vex clapped her hands.

"Alright, every detestable pig, please listen up!" Vex stepped into the blond's line of sight, drawing her sword. "I'll only say this once. The next time you'll have to face my husband's full fury. And let me tell you..."
Her red eyes gleamed with immense sadism. "Death is a mercy."
The blond tried to speak up, but Vex wasn't done with her announcement just yet.
"We love our husband. Every one of us chose to be with him of our free will, said yes at the altar, and have been overjoyed ever since."
"We didn't... I wasn't..."
Vex leaned closer, her red pentagrams burning.
"You weren't what?"
He stared at her with his mouth open. Beside him, Harl was making wet, breathless sounds as he struggled to hold the ragged sleeve over his wound.

"If you ever insult our devotion to him again, or speak of us as loose women..." she licked her blade's edge. Suddenly, all of Quinlan's wives looked utterly ferocious, their eyes burning with pure malice. "We might just not wait for him to set things right."
"Yes! Yes, I understand!"
Dask hurried to agree, his voice shaking. Harl could only sob his answer, still clutching the stump against his chest.
The clerk's breathing came in shallow catches as she looked past Quinlan at the armed women surrounding him.
Her gaze caught on the arm beneath the table. She swallowed hard and looked at the forms instead.
The blond followed her gaze, then raised his eyes to her with desperate hope.
"You're going to do something, right? We're loyal members, working hard every day for a century! They attacked us inside the Guild!"
Ayame's katana touched his neck when he tried to lean toward the counter. He swallowed and stayed where he was.
"Look at him! They cut his fucking arm off! Over a bit of rookie hazing!"
"Hazing?!" the short-haired woman spat. "He tried to grab her! We all saw it!"
"You told him to give her a proper welcome, Brennic!" another woman called from the tables, pointing at the blond. "You were laughing until the arm came off!"
Brennic's mouth trembled. "We didn't know they were... We only..."
"Didn't know they could fight back?"
The question brought a furious murmur from the women around him. Brennic turned toward the clerk again, tears running down his blood-spattered face.
"Please! You can't let them do this!"
Quinlan gathered the registration sheets, then let them fall back onto the counter.
The clerk looked from the papers to his helmet.
"If you consider what just happened innocent hazing, this isn't an organization I will be a part of."
Her eyes widened, and then she began stammering. "I- we-"
"It was not hazing."
The answer came from above. A grey-haired man stood on the landing overlooking the hall, one hand gripping the stair rail. His eyes moved across the bloody table before fixing on Brennic.
"Guildmaster!" Brennic tried to rise, then remembered Ayame's blade. "Sir, thank the Goddess. We were just..."
"I heard what you said."
The Guildmaster descended the stairs beside the contract boards. He stopped at the bottom, glaring at the three captives with such open anger that Brennic's appeal died in his throat.
"You admitted it in front of this entire hall. Your friend tried to grab a woman who wanted nothing to do with him, and now you expect the Guild to protect you from her companions?"
"It wasn't me who tried to touch her!"
"You encouraged him."
The short-haired woman folded her arms, watching Brennic try to find an answer beneath the katana raised against his chin.
"All three of you are coming upstairs," the Guildmaster continued. "We will discuss what you think your badges entitle you to."
Harl lifted his blood-soaked hand far enough to expose the stump. Fresh blood ran over the severed bone.
"I need a healer! Please!"
"I'm here."
A man carrying a healer's bag had edged through the crowd. He stopped beside the chair, looking at Blossom's claw beneath Harl's chin.
"Could you let me get to the wound? He's bleeding out."
Blossom glanced toward Quinlan.

sentences.text: Quinlan remained facing the registration counter in the Adventurer's Guild as the drunk behind him reached for Serika's hip.
"[Wind Blade]."
His magic compressed the air above the outstretched arm into a thin cutting edge.
He drove it down through the padded sleeve, flesh, and bone just above the elbow.
*Shhk!*
The man's arm struck the floor with a wet slap, its open hand bouncing against Serika's boot.
Blood spurted from the severed upper arm and splashed across the mugs on his table.
He stared at the stump, his mouth working soundlessly until another pulse of blood struck his friend's face.
"MY ARM!
AAAAH!"
Quinlan dipped his pen in the ink.
The drunk began to rise from his chair.
Blossom flashed across from the counter and appeared behind the man.
She caught his hair, wrenching his head back while her claw gauntlet aimed its sharp edges against his exposed throat.
He tried to bend over his bleeding stump, but she pulled his head back until he felt the metal against his throat.
A single droplet of blood ran from beneath Blossom's claw toward his chest.
"W-why are you bastards just staring?
Help!" he cried toward his table.
"H-how dare you?!" The blond dropped his mug and reached for the sword at his belt, finally finding his voice.
The mug struck the floor with a clang, spilling beer into the blood.
Ayame drew her katana as she crossed from the counter in the blink of an eye, sliding it beneath his chin before he could pull his sword free.
She lifted the edge, forcing him upright with a thin red cut opening across his neck.
"I wouldn't draw that if I were you."
"M-mercy...!"
His hand sprang away from the hilt.
Scar slipped behind the crooked-nosed man's chair with both daggers drawn, bringing their points against his back just as he shoved his seat away from the table.
"Aagh!
Fuck!"
He had driven himself onto both blades.
When he lurched forward, Scar followed, keeping their points buried beneath his shoulder blades.
"Sit still."
Around them, adventurers scrambled out of their seats, overturning a bench in their haste to get clear of the blood spreading beneath the table.
"A healer!
Someone get a fucking healer!"
The wounded man's plea broke into another scream as his remaining hand closed around the stump.
Blood squeezed between his fingers and ran down his wrist.
Blossom held him by the hair while he writhed.
She wanted to open his throat for what he had tried to do to Serika, and the frightened eyes straining upward toward her found no mercy in her face.
"To appreciate the beauty of my wives is natural," Quinlan finally spoke, still facing the counter.
"After all, they are the most amazing women in existence."
His pen moved across the returned form, spelling out the inn's name in the space for their address.
"But to make crude remarks about them, to suggest their love can be bought, and then presume to touch them..."
"Please!
I'm sorry!
Please, my arm..."
Quinlan finished the final letter while the man choked on his own pleading.
Serika laid the remaining forms beside his elbow, her fingers hot against his wrist when she touched him.
"...is nothing but suicidal," he finished.
Quinlan set the pen down and covered Serika's fingers with his free hand.
"We're new in Sarthal, unaware of your customs.
That's why I only took your arm, not your head.
But if grabbing women like that is a part of your culture..."
"It fucking isn't!
Harl, you know damn well it isn't!"
The woman who had mocked their herb-picking stood beside the overturned bench.
Her face had gone red with fury, and she pointed straight at the bleeding man in the greasy padded coat.
"Don't let these disgusting bastards paint the picture of this wonderful city!
They think being close to Grade Three means they can do whatever they want to anyone beneath them!"
"We were only having a laugh," the crooked-nosed man protested.
"Were you, Dask?" A short-haired woman pushed away from the wall to confront him.
"Was it funny when you caught my ass at this counter?
When I told you to let go and you asked whether I'd like to lose my teeth?"
Dask's eyes flicked to the clerk.
"That wasn't...
You walked into me!"
"There!" She threw a hand toward him, disgust twisting her mouth.
"That's what he does.
Grabs a lower-grade woman, threatens her, then claims she imagined it.
Apparently we all keep walking into his fucking hands!"
"Every woman detests them.
Just one look is enough to paint the full picture, even if they haven't tried grabbing you personally..." the first woman said.
"Their poor wives are so miserable..." another whispered, dejected.
"When these sons of bitches are out 'working,' we tend to visit them to lift their spirits."
Similarly angry voices answered from farther back.
Women who had moved out of the fight's path were coming closer again, staring at the men trapped in their chairs.
"Go on, then," the short-haired woman challenged.
"Tell her she'll lose her teeth too."
She pointed at Serika.
Dask stared at the floor, trembling against Scar's daggers.
Harl sucked in a ragged breath.
The blond had begun crying, blood from his friend's stump freckling his cheeks.
Serika looked down at the gloved hand covering hers, then squeezed it before turning back toward the table.
Heat rolled from her body, driving the adventurer at the neighbouring counter away from her.
Vex clapped her hands.
"Alright, every detestable pig, please listen up!" Vex stepped into the blond's line of sight, drawing her sword.
"I'll only say this once.
The next time you'll have to face my husband's full fury.
And let me tell you..."
Her red eyes gleamed with immense sadism.
"Death is a mercy."
The blond tried to speak up, but Vex wasn't done with her announcement just yet.
"We love our husband.
Every one of us chose to be with him of our free will, said yes at the altar, and have been overjoyed ever since."
"We didn't...
I wasn't..."
Vex leaned closer, her red pentagrams burning.
"You weren't what?"
He stared at her with his mouth open.
Beside him, Harl was making wet, breathless sounds as he struggled to hold the ragged sleeve over his wound.
"If you ever insult our devotion to him again, or speak of us as loose women..." she licked her blade's edge.
Suddenly, all of Quinlan's wives looked utterly ferocious, their eyes burning with pure malice.
"We might just not wait for him to set things right."
"Yes!
Yes, I understand!"
Dask hurried to agree, his voice shaking.
Harl could only sob his answer, still clutching the stump against his chest.
The clerk's breathing came in shallow catches as she looked past Quinlan at the armed women surrounding him.
Her gaze caught on the arm beneath the table.
She swallowed hard and looked at the forms instead.
The blond followed her gaze, then raised his eyes to her with desperate hope.
"You're going to do something, right?
We're loyal members, working hard every day for a century!
They attacked us inside the Guild!"
Ayame's katana touched his neck when he tried to lean toward the counter.
He swallowed and stayed where he was.
"Look at him!
They cut his fucking arm off!
Over a bit of rookie hazing!"
"Hazing?!" the short-haired woman spat.
"He tried to grab her!
We all saw it!"
"You told him to give her a proper welcome, Brennic!" another woman called from the tables, pointing at the blond.
"You were laughing until the arm came off!"
Brennic's mouth trembled.
"We didn't know they were...
We only..."
"Didn't know they could fight back?"
The question brought a furious murmur from the women around him.
Brennic turned toward the clerk again, tears running down his blood-spattered face.
"Please!
You can't let them do this!"
Quinlan gathered the registration sheets, then let them fall back onto the counter.
The clerk looked from the papers to his helmet.
"If you consider what just happened innocent hazing, this isn't an organization I will be a part of."
Her eyes widened, and then she began stammering.
"I- we-"
"It was not hazing."
The answer came from above.
A grey-haired man stood on the landing overlooking the hall, one hand gripping the stair rail.
His eyes moved across the bloody table before fixing on Brennic.
"Guildmaster!" Brennic tried to rise, then remembered Ayame's blade.
"Sir, thank the Goddess.
We were just..."
"I heard what you said."
The Guildmaster descended the stairs beside the contract boards.
He stopped at the bottom, glaring at the three captives with such open anger that Brennic's appeal died in his throat.
"You admitted it in front of this entire hall.
Your friend tried to grab a woman who wanted nothing to do with him, and now you expect the Guild to protect you from her companions?"
"It wasn't me who tried to touch her!"
"You encouraged him."
The short-haired woman folded her arms, watching Brennic try to find an answer beneath the katana raised against his chin.
"All three of you are coming upstairs," the Guildmaster continued.
"We will discuss what you think your badges entitle you to."
Harl lifted his blood-soaked hand far enough to expose the stump.
Fresh blood ran over the severed bone.
"I need a healer!
Please!"
"I'm here."
A man carrying a healer's bag had edged through the crowd.
He stopped beside the chair, looking at Blossom's claw beneath Harl's chin.
"Could you let me get to the wound?
He's bleeding out."
Blossom glanced toward Quinlan.

chapters.title: Chapter 1971 Just a Joke
paragraphs: "Let him go."

She withdrew her claw and released the fistful of hair. Harl sagged forward with a sob, his greasy collar dragging across the soaked sleeve as the healer knelt beside him and pulled folded cloth from his bag.
"Hold still. Let me put pressure on it."
Harl's scream broke halfway through when the cloth met exposed flesh.
"Treat him here," the Guildmaster told the healer. "Bring him up when he can be moved."
Then he addressed the women gathered behind the table.
"Anyone they have threatened or put their hands on, please stay and give your account."
"Finally doing something..." the short-haired woman muttered, eyes narrowed. "I've got plenty to tell you."
Ayame lowered her katana, and Scar pulled her daggers free of Dask's coat before sheathing them. He lurched out of his chair, flinching when his accuser stepped into his path.
"Mind where you're walking," she said.

"Ugh..." Crooked-nosed Dask went around her with his head down. A sharp laugh followed him toward the stairs, joined by another when Brennic nearly slipped in the beer beneath his seat, blond hair falling across his wet eyes.
"Almost Grade Three!" a woman howled after them. "Make sure you tell him how important you are!"
Quinlan looked down at the remaining empty line. They still needed a party name.
They had crossed the sea together, finally free to go wherever they pleased. He wanted a name that belonged to all of them.
<Unbound?>
Ayame returned to his side, sliding her katana into its sheath. <I like that.>
<So does Blossom!>
The others agreed through the link. Quinlan wrote Unbound on the sheet, signed beneath it, then gathered the forms and offered them across the counter.
"How much do we owe you?"
She stared at the papers.
"Registration."
Although Quinlan wasn't rich by any measure that ignored the entire continent he owned, he had looted the pirates, so he had a few coins to his name.
"Waive their registration fees," the Guildmaster told the clerk while walking up the stairs.
His gaze moved to Quinlan and his companions.
"You should have been able to register here without being harassed. Please accept that much as an apology."
"Oh! Yes, sir." The clerk looked back at Quinlan. "We normally charge each new member, but you and your companions won't owe anything today."
Her voice dwindled while she reached for the stack. Quinlan held it within easy reach until she managed to take it.
"I appreciate the gesture."
The Guildmaster inclined his head to Quinlan before following Brennic and Dask upstairs.
The clerk bent over the forms. Behind Quinlan, the healer asked another adventurer to help hold the dressing in place while he wound a bandage around Harl's injured arm.

She checked the final entries, stamped their sheets, and began setting identification badges on the counter. Her hands shook so badly that one landed face down. She hurriedly turned it over, exposing the numeral marking its owner as Grade One.
"These are yours. Please present them when accepting work or claiming payment. And..."
Her eyes strayed toward the bloody table.
"Congratulations on becoming adventurers!"
The welcome came out painfully bright over Harl's sobbing.
Quinlan chuckled.
"Thank you. You've been very helpful."

Quinlan took his badge, then stepped aside so his companions could reach the counter. The clerk called each name on their forms and handed its owner a Grade One badge, checking them off until every member of Unbound had received one.
Blossom turned hers over between her fingers, her tail wagging as Serika tucked her own away.
Lilith stepped up to the desk with the other Lilies gathering behind her.
"Our turn. We're the Scarlet Lilies, five members. Could we register under that name?"
"Certainly. I'll need a form from each of you."
The clerk passed fresh sheets across the counter. Lilith filled in the party name while Bronnya, Jallen, Scar, and Void began their own entries, sharing the pens between them.
Quinlan finally turned away from the desk.
The healer was still bent over his patient. Farther back, a server had set her tray down to right the overturned bench, and the women who remained were watching Unbound make room for the next party.
Vex stood beside Quinlan with her new badge in one hand, still glaring at the stairs. He settled his hand on her white hair.
"That was quite the speech."
She looked up at him, the fury lingering for a moment before she registered the affection in his touch. His fingers stroked her head, and her lips parted in a delighted little smile.
"Hubby~ It felt so good!"
The murderous hexwitch leaned into his palm. She sheathed her sword and put her badge away, her eyes shining with happiness as she slipped an arm around his and pressed close to her husband.
"Welcome to Sarthal!"
The woman who had first spoken up lifted her mug toward them. Others cheered with her, and someone began clapping hard enough to turn heads at the stairs.
"About fucking time someone put those creeps in their place!"

The relief in their laughter was enormous. Women who had watched the men leer at them across this hall could finally point and laugh back, with Harl whimpering into a bloody dressing a few steps away.
Quinlan found himself surrounded as they came over to greet his family. Vex held his arm firmly while a woman carrying a bow stopped in front of Blossom, staring at her hands.
"How did you get behind him so fast? I was looking straight at you!"
Blossom's tail started wagging even faster.
"Blossom is very fast!"

"Oh my Goddess, you're so adorable!" she giggled, surprised by the speech pattern and violent tail motions. Then she realized what Blossom had just said. "I noticed you're fast! But... he hadn't even stood up."
"He was slow. Fat and drunk!!"
"Ahahaha!" the woman burst into laughter, followed by her comrades.
Beside them, another adventurer was asking Ayame about her draw.
"Did you know he was going for his sword? I only saw your blade when it was already under his chin."
"His eyes moved toward the hilt," Ayame answered, smiling. "After that, it was rather obvious."
"Obvious to you, maybe! Tracking someone's eyes from across the room with such precision in under a moment's time... That's crazy impressive!"
The woman laughed, then turned to Quinlan.
"And you didn't even turn around! That spell... How did you cut only his arm?"
"I aimed for it."
"Oh, well, that explains everything!"
Lucille laughed at the woman's exasperation. The gathering pressed closer, full of questions now that the blades had been put away.
"How strong are those three, actually?" Aurora asked. "Their grades evidently weren't much to boast about."
"Their levels are around seventy," the woman with the mug replied. "They remind us often enough. Especially anyone who hasn't got that far yet."
Quinlan blinked in surprise, and he wasn't alone.
<That high?!> Seraphiel gasped.
"They're too fond of staying alive to take work that might actually test them. Easy jobs, over and over, until the Guild has a mountain of completed contracts to review."
She rolled her eyes toward the stairs.
"Most people their level who actually put some effort into adventuring would reach Grade Three in a few years. Those idiots have spent an entire century trying to get there."
"Then they sit here boasting about it," the archer added. "As though everyone ought to be impressed."
Quinlan heard her, but his attention had gone to Black Fang.
She stood beside the counter with her weapon untouched. The commotion had failed to give her anything worth drawing it for.
Level seventy-four.
Those men were supposed to be close to her. A handful of levels separated them from a woman who could have slaughtered their entire table before any of them realized she had moved.
<Around seventy...?> Ayame repeated through the link. Her gaze had found Black Fang too. <I could barely feel him resisting my blade.>
<The one whose arm I took couldn't even react despite me using a slow attack because I thought these losers were like level 30.>

Their levels gave them the physical attributes their builds entitled them to. Another person with the same Vitality would have been just as sturdy, and the same Agility would have given them the same speed to work with.

Yet Brennic had advertised his intention before moving, Dask had backed straight onto Scar's blades, and Harl had exposed his arm to Quinlan's spell. They had squandered their abilities before the fight even began.
Then the realization filled him. 'Ah. So that's how it is.'
His family had arrived in a world where people could grow far beyond Iskaris's old limit, yet their own levels concealed how dangerous they already were.
They had already fought above their levels at home. Here, where XP seemed to be a lot more abundant, they were able to punch far, far above their supposed weight class.

Black Fang had spent centuries perfecting her killing while her level refused to move. Her judgment, technique, and experience had kept growing. These men could boast of being close to her level all they wanted; put her in a ring with them and they were fodder.

At the counter, the clerk finished registering the Scarlet Lilies and handed each of them a badge. Lilith checked the Grade One numeral on hers while Void slipped her own into a pocket with a sleepy yawn.
The woman with the mug stepped aside to let the healer and his helper ease Harl past her, his bandaged stump held against his chest.

"Sorry for the terrible first impression. We promise Sarthal and the Guild are better than you might think," she told Serika. "And if they give you any trouble after this, there are plenty of us willing to say what happened."
"Much appreciated," Serika gave a grin and a thumbs up.
Quinlan let the last questions run their course before Vex drew him toward the contract boards, the other women following.
