chapters.title: Chapter 1972 Quest Board
paragraphs: Quinlan followed Vex to the contract boards in Sarthal's Adventurer's Guild, where his new badge entitled him to pick weeds.
Quite a selection of weeds, admittedly.
Much of the Grade One board was covered in requests from herbalists and apothecaries. Some wanted roots dug up, others berries or flowers gathered, with drawings showing which plants to look for.
Aurora was studying those illustrations when Quinlan stopped beside a request for leaves.
[FIELDLEAF COLLECTION]
[Issuer: South Quay Apothecary]
[Location: Meadows beside the south road, outside Sarthal]
[Objective: Deliver one basket of fresh, undamaged fieldleaf. Collection baskets supplied.]
[Reward: 3 crowns per accepted basket]
[Suggested party size: 2-3]
[Required grade: One]
"At least they supply the basket," Aurora remarked.
Her eyes moved from the fieldleaf drawing to the roots pictured on the neighbouring notice.
<I don't recognize the plants on these collection quests. I'd like to get some samples while we're here.>
Blossom tapped the drawing of pale leaves beneath the fieldleaf contract.
<Blossom recognizes this one!>

Quinlan glanced past her at the adventurers nearby. Any of those plants might be familiar to every child in Thalorind. They had to conduct most of the conversation using [Master's Link]. But such a large group standing around completely mute would perhaps draw even more attention.
They had to strike a balance.
"That was in Master's lunch!"
Aurora leaned closer to read the apothecary's note beneath the drawing, which described the leaves' uses in cooking and medicine.
<Apparently it also goes into a poultice for swollen feet,> she said through the link, smiling.
"It was a great meal," Quinlan replied, stroking Blossom's long blonde hair.
Kitsara leaned past her to study the reward.
"We could buy a basket of fieldleaf, hand it in for the three crowns, and become accomplished adventurers without leaving the city."
"You could," Lilith replied from the next board. "I wouldn't be shocked if some rich loser tried that."
"You're right!" one of the women who had just cursed the three harassers out of this world said with a smile. "There are some who do stuff like that. But the Guild is quite competent."
Another woman joined the conversation. "The apothecary will pay for good leaves however you got them. But if you claim you gathered them yourself, the Guild might ask where you went."

"They check up on completed jobs," the first added. "Both the clients and the adventurers. Buying a basket of weeds won't convince them you can survive the hills. Rich snobs don't get far on their money alone."
As the women were talking, Lilith grinned. She knew exactly what she was doing, speaking her sentence loud enough for the bored bystander chicks to overhear.
Having these women carry the conversation for them allowed the gang to appear a lot more natural despite speaking less.

Quinlan looked farther along the wall. Road inspections, missing livestock, deliveries to outlying farms... Several sounded pleasant enough, but he had crossed an ocean with women who could tear armies apart.
Mere fetch quests, while potentially ideal for gathering some information, overall felt quite wasteful as their first adventuring job in Thalorind.
But as Grade One adventurers...
Serika had found a notice featuring a sketch of a heavily armoured creature.
"That looks fun," Serika said, pointing at the armoured creature on her notice.
Ayame followed her finger down to the eligibility line.
"Grade Four."
"Aw. Knew it was too good to be true."
Farther down, a sheet bearing an enormous tusked head had caught Blossom's attention.
[RAVENOUS BOARS: ORCHARD CLEARANCE]
[Issuer: South Road Orchard Growers]
[Location: Orchards half a day's walk south of Sarthal]
[Objective: Eliminate the reported boars and locate their nesting grounds. Completion subject to inspection.]
[Reward: 45 crowns]
[Suggested party size: 4-6]
[Required grade: Two]
<We could ask about the larger expeditions,> Aurora suggested. <The clerk said different parties join together. Maybe we can skip the fetch quests that way.>
"How far out is that one?" Lucille asked aloud, leaning toward the board.
The women who didn't seem to have anything better to do than yap all day were more than happy to entertain her, going on and on about their experiences regarding the route.
Quinlan started wondering if adventurers came to the guild on their days off just to show their faces. Not that he had a problem with that.
'They've got quite the colorful community here...' he noted, chuckling.

Ayame followed the route one of the women traced with her finger while the mental conversation continued. <I'd like to research more about the creatures we might face before we volunteer for such a thing. We hardly know any of the creatures on these sheets.>
<Blossom thinks the Ravenous Boar slaying quest is the best!!>
<Let me guess. They sound tasty?> Lucille giggled inwardly.
Blossom's eyes widened, shocked to the core. <Blossom was seen through!!>
Lucille stroked Blossom's wagging tail while answering the woman beside her. "She certainly seems interested in the boars."
<Even after all this time... How can you surprise me with how adorable you are?>
Quinlan was reading a survey contract when someone tugged his coat.
He turned, expecting Ayame.
Black Fang stood beside him with a fold of his clothing held between her fingers.
His gaze travelled from her hand to her face. She stared up at him, violet eyes fixed on his, and gave the cloth another small pull.
"Hmm?"
"My stomach hurts."
'Huh?'
Black Fang glanced toward the women beside the board, then added, rather stiffly, "The meal at the inn. It was troublesome."
And just like that, Quinlan instantly knew something was up.
The fucking queen of poison simply did not get defeated by lunch. It was a possibility his mind could not even begin to entertain.
The same was true for the rest of the gang as well, evidenced by the many gazes sent Black Fang's way.
Ayame followed her sister's hand to Quinlan's coat, then turned back to the women beside the board, instantly activating cover up mode.
"Sorry, where did you say the road branches? I'd hate to take the wrong turning."

The nearest adventurer leaned toward the map again. Quinlan's companions gathered closer to read it, all of them in on it now, their bodies screening Black Fang from the tables without shutting her away from the group.
Lucille made room for Seraphiel and gave the curious woman beside her a reassuring smile.
"Our healer will take care of her. Don't worry. She just can't deal with spicy food."
"Oh, I totally get that! The last time I ate chili beans..." and the yapping went on and on.
"..." Black Fang was nearly growling.
Seraphiel, gang boss of the cover up mission, stepped beside the Venomborne Terror.
"Oh, a stomachache. That's terrible. Let me check. May I?"

Black Fang gave Seraphiel an awkward nod, permitting the elf's hand to settle against her stomach. Sera pressed gently through the fabric, moving her fingers from one side to the other while Quinlan tried very hard to keep his mouth straight.
"[Healing Light]."

Seraphiel traced a shining pattern over Black Fang's stomach, speaking the spell clearly enough for the nearby adventurers to hear. Her light spread beneath her palm as she began the unnecessary treatment.
Quinlan watched her free hand move beside the glowing one. She was making the casting obvious, giving anyone who noticed magic gathering around Black Fang a perfectly ordinary explanation for it.
"Here? Or a little higher?"
"Higher."
Black Fang said it without looking at her. Her violet eyes remained fixed on his, and the fingers holding his coat gave another impatient pull.
She glanced toward Ayame and the rest, who up until her proclamation were deeply engaged in their mental conversation, then returned her attention to Quinlan.
He began to understand her annoyance. His companions were keeping their public conversation harmless, and Black Fang knew them well enough to recognize how much they were leaving unsaid.

Where they wanted to go, what they could handle, which risks were worth taking... She belonged in those discussions. Instead, she was listening to directions from strangers while the people she had crossed an ocean with made their decisions privately.
She could hear a heartbeat through a wall, yet standing beside her own sister apparently entitled her to half a conversation.
Black Fang utterly detested this.
Her eyes narrowed at Quinlan.
She had already heard enough of their remarks about roads and prices. The irritation in her stare demanded access to the conversation they were actually having.
He looked at her hand on his coat again.
She wanted into [Master's Link].
That required [Subjugation].

chapters.title: Chapter 1973 Black Fang's Demand
paragraphs: His gaze snapped back to hers, and Black Fang lifted her chin by the smallest amount. She knew exactly what she was asking for. The surprise in his eyes only seemed to irritate her further.
'Even after all this time, I still have no fucking idea what to expect from this woman,' Quinlan chuckled inwardly. 'Can she be any more random?'
"Does that hurt?" Seraphiel asked, moving her palm.
"Yes. I'm dying."
Quinlan nearly choked.
This woman was not only a walking talking surprise, but also a terrible actor.
Black Fang tightened her grip on his coat, and he swallowed the laugh before it escaped. Her improvised complaint was growing more awkward every time Sera invited her to elaborate.
Yet beneath his amusement, affection filled him with such force that he wanted to pull her into his arms.

She knew what his Subjugation meant. She had seen his enemies obey, seen the authority he could wield through the bond, and she was offering him that power over herself in the middle of a crowded Guild hall.
She wanted to belong in the conversation, and she trusted him enough to ask for this.
He held her gaze until the impatience in her expression eased. For a moment, he let her see his own question plainly: did she truly want to give him that authority?
Black Fang held his eyes and nodded to him.
Seraphiel shifted her palm and traced another bright pattern with her fingers.
"[Healing Light]. There, let's try once more."

As fresh healing mana gathered beneath Sera's hand, Quinlan cast [Subjugation] silently. His magic reached Black Fang amid the elf's conspicuous treatment, and a familiar system prompt appeared before the assassin's eyes.
[The Primordial Subjugator wishes to Subjugate you! Do you accept?]
Black Fang accepted.
The bond took hold, and Quinlan opened [Master's Link] to include her in the family's discussion.
Her fingers loosened on his coat.
"I'm better now."
"Happy to hear. Let me know if it hurts later!" Seraphiel beamed, patting the Venomborne Terror's belly for good measure while her healing light faded.
"..." With immense difficulty, Black Fang moved on from what she had gone through just to enslave herself.
Then, without even needing to calibrate how to use [Master's Link], she joined.
<Only look at contracts with an objective we can finish ourselves,> Black Fang began. <Unless you intend to spend your honeymoon watching a stranger measure a road.>
Ayame finished thanking the woman who had explained the route. Through the link, her voice rose with sheer delight.
<Big sis?!>
<Master?!> Vex's voice burst into their minds. <You're here! Hubby, you finally did it?!>
<She asked,> Quinlan replied. <No, she forced me. Basically I was commanded to enslave her.>
Lucille smoothed a crease in the notice before her, her public expression pleasantly attentive.
<Welcome to the harem chat!!>
<It's good to have you here!> Seraphiel giggled.
Vex remained beside the map, listening while an adventurer described the condition of the south road. She asked whether the wagons had damaged it badly after the last rain.
Inside Quinlan's head, she was beyond overjoyed.
<Now I can talk to you whenever I want! Even when you wander off! Master, you have no idea how many things I've wanted to tell you when you weren't there!>
Her voice was practically beaming, every word spilling over with happiness, while her face remained absorbed in the very ordinary subject of wagon ruts.

She had spent so much of her life looking up to Black Fang. Having her mentor here, sharing the place where Vex laughed, complained, and adored her husband, made the Hexwitch happier than she could possibly keep to herself.
Black Fang turned her violet eyes toward Quinlan. Realization became evident in them as she began to fully understand just what she signed up for.
Vex was already a raving lunatic who could keep yapping about him for hours on end without having unlimited access to her mind.
Now...
Quinlan chuckled softly, leaning closer as though checking whether her stomach had improved.
<I'll try to keep her from harassing you all day.>
<Harassing?! Hubby, I'm going to discuss only the most important of matters with her.>
The look Black Fang gave her became considerably less trusting.
Quinlan kept his amusement inside the link. He would certainly try, but listening to the joy pouring out of Vex, he suspected her mentor's peaceful days were in serious trouble.
He sure as hell wasn't pressing the mute button on his beloved wife.
Black Fang had demanded this. She could enjoy the consequences of her actions alongside the benefits.
Blossom edged closer to Black Fang.
<Can Black Fang hear Blossom too?>
<Yes.>
Her tail began wagging.
<Hello!>
"See anything you like?" the woman beside Lucille asked when she noticed Blossom's wagging tail.
"The boars seem interesting," Lucille answered, giving the dogkin's hair another fond stroke.
Quinlan laughed at that while Black Fang returned her attention to the contracts with immense determination.
<This one,> she said.
Aurora leaned in to read beneath her finger.
[MISSING EXPEDITION: INVESTIGATION AND RECOVERY]
[Issuer: Celia, enquiries through this branch]
[Location: Underground ruins in the southern hills. Expedition route lodged with the Guild.]
[Objective: Establish the expedition's fate and investigate the condition of its sole returned member. Recover belongings and relevant samples where possible.]
[Reward: 300 crowns]
[Provision advance: 30 crowns, deducted from the reward]
[Suggested party size: 10-20]
[Requirement: Grade Three leadership. Lower-grade members may join under the leading party's responsibility.]
[Warning: Cause of the expedition's loss remains unknown.]
Quinlan read the final line again before looking toward the route attached beneath the notice.
<We have the right abilities and the quest has other benefits.>
Seraphiel's eyes began sparkling as she cleared her mental throat. <Ehem. Alright girls, let me enter my Venomborne Translator mode.>
The blonde elf cleared her throat a second time, just to ensure everyone was paying proper attention, then began.

<Blossom can follow tracks and sniff out a great deal of information to help the investigation. Quin can help us through difficult terrain and handle a myriad of other things with his cheat abilities. Then we also have plenty of other unique classes and talents that will help us investigate. Also, it'll give us the background needed to ask around town, collecting valuable information. If we explain we're adventurers preparing to undertake a quest, we'll appear less suspicious if we ask a lot of questions. We're just making sure all our bases are covered.>
Black Fang continued reading, apparently content to let the elf elaborate. It was proof of her translation function working properly.
Quinlan pressed his lips together beneath his helmet.
Ayame's voice was full of amusement.
<Big sis, that's cool and all but is your upset stomach affecting your ability to count? We're Grade One. This requires Grade Three. Three is more than one.>
Black Fang eyed the petite samurai then replied with a tone that sounded as if she was questioning whether her little sister was dropped on her head as a kid.
<We recruit some Grade Three waste of air, send Blossom ahead to bait a large group of monsters, and stage their deaths.>
<The women just told us the Guild checks how contracts are completed,> Aurora reminded her.
Black Fang didn't seem dismayed.

<You can't investigate adventurers who were eaten and then disintegrated inside a monster's stomach. I was just fighting for my life, had to go all out and use my strongest poison. I'll claim their souls for good measure.>
<...Damn.>
The harem chat, for once, was very, very silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1974 New Arrivals
paragraphs: Quinlan stared at Black Fang beside the contract boards in Sarthal's Adventurer's Guild.
She had just proposed murdering whoever agreed to lead their first expedition, and appeared to be waiting for someone to find a flaw in the arrangement.
Ayame recovered first.
<Big sis, could we try completing a single job before we start disposing of our colleagues?>
<Why?>
<...Now I'm afraid to ask you anything else.>
<It was perfectly reasonable.>
Quinlan reached out to rub Black Fang's shoulder in a calming manner.
This woman was always bloodthirsty, but now that she could finally level up again, her lust for violence definitely increased.
Not that he hated it, not at all. But...
<I agree with you, I like that quest as well. But let's not try to kill whoever we choose right off the bat, shall we? Perhaps we can make valuable connections.>
Black Fang didn't react.
<The condition of the survivor...> Seraphiel read. <What happened to him?>
<It doesn't say,> Aurora replied. <We'd have to ask.>
"This one looks worth asking about," Seraphiel said aloud.
"Could you keep hold of it?" Aurora asked. "I'd like to compare the terms with the others."
"Ugh. You weirdos again?"
The voice came from behind Quinlan, carrying a familiar level of scorn.

Marielle stood near the entrance with her staff in one hand. Her chestnut curls had escaped their arrangement around her face, and the flattened patch above one ear suggested her pillow had at least participated in the afternoon.
Rest evidently had not.
Andre stopped beside her with his round shield on his back. He recognized Quinlan's helmet and closed his eyes briefly.
"That's just great..." he murmured.
Marielle looked over the women gathered around the board.
"I hope you've finished disturbing everyone in your vicinity. Some of us intend to work."
"Did you sleep well?" Lucille asked pleasantly.
Andre made a pained noise. "Goddess have mercy."
His wife answered by pushing past him toward the counter. She produced a badge from beneath her collar and laid it in front of the clerk.
"We need our records transferred here. Marielle and Andre. Grade Three."
Quinlan compared the numeral on her badge with the grade required by the investigation notice.
Aurora had made the same connection. She took the notice to the counter while the clerk checked the couple's papers.

Quinlan watched the clerk examine the couple's records. Their grade made them a possibility, although convincing Marielle to work with them would be another matter. He could endure her bitching if it saved them days of picking weeds.
Ayame leaned against his arm while they waited.
<If we're going to ask strangers to take us along, it might be worth showing your face soon. It's harder to get someone to trust you when they can't even see who they're talking to.>
<...Yeah.>
She had a point.
Why hide his face at all?

Unfortunately, he still had no idea whether someone here could recognize a Primordial at a glance. [Masked Seat] concealed his standing as a Sovereign, but his face and whatever it might reveal were separate concerns.
He had arrived in Iskaris knowing practically nothing and made rather a lot of decisions as though he knew everything. His family had paid for some of them alongside him.
Thalorind deserved more care than that. A few drunk adventurers being laughably beneath them did not make this continent safe, especially with an actual dragon somewhere above its rulers.
He wanted to learn enough to take the helmet off comfortably.
However, as Ayame had put it, another long stint behind a mask, like his time in the Consortium, held very little appeal to them all.
It was just a temporary caution until they understood the world better.
<Soon, hopefully,> he replied.
The clerk returned Marielle's papers, and Aurora laid their chosen notice on the counter.
"Could we ask about this contract? You mentioned parties joining together."

"The missing expedition?" Behind the counter, the clerk studied it. "Yes. That one permits additional members under a qualified party's supervision. The leading party must be at least Grade Three, and we need its approval of everyone joining."
"So we'd remain Grade One," Ayame said, coming beside Aurora, "but could participate?"
"On this contract, yes. You couldn't accept it independently. Your completed work would still go on your own records."
Marielle turned toward them.
"Grade One?"
Her gaze travelled over Quinlan's armour with considerable satisfaction.
"Well. That explains a great deal."
Quinlan addressed the couple.
"Would you be interested in leading this one? We can provide the additional fighters."
"Hah?" Marielle gasped then began laughing in his face.
"Hahahahaha!"
"I am serious."
"Yeah, that's what makes this funny. You imbeciles could only dream of working under me." She wiped a tear from her eyes.
At that, a dozen women raised their eyebrows in perfect sync, and the harem chat became quite chaotic.
Unaware of it all, Marielle continued with her chin held high.
"You want me to go with you so you can get yourselves killed and leave us to finish it? Why would I carry a mission all on my own?"
Andre reached for the notice, but his wife put her hand over it. She was already turning away when Quinlan took a cloth-wrapped circlet from his bag and laid it on the counter.
"I see."
He unfolded the cloth to reveal a narrow silver diadem, its fine branches curling around the temples. Tiny runes followed the metalwork along the inner band. Marielle's gaze stopped on it.
"How about this. I'll make a wager with you. This is my collateral."
She looked from the circlet to his helmet before picking it up. Her thumb traced the fine channels worked into the underside.
"This craftsmanship... Who made it?"
"Who knows?" Quinlan offered no information like that freely, prompting the woman to narrow her eyes.
But she couldn't keep the attitude for long, as the crown kept drawing her attention. "What does it do?"
"Would you try it on? It activates when you touch the rune beside your right temple."
"I have nothing against you. Why would I harm you?" Quinlan was quick to shut down this self-centered woman's thoughts. He literally didn't care about her at all.
"...Fine." Marielle settled the circlet among her chestnut curls and touched the indicated rune.
Pale blue light spilled over her shoulders. It gathered into a translucent mantle, then thickened into a flowing outer robe with long sleeves and silver embroidery running down its open front.
She caught a sleeve between her fingers. The conjured fabric slid over her skin like fine silk, cool against the warmth of the Guild hall.

Marielle turned toward the glass-fronted cabinet behind the counter. The robe fell neatly over her battle clothes, drawing in at her waist before flowing down to her ankles. She straightened to study her reflection, then lifted an arm to see the embroidered sleeve drape from it.
It looked damned good on her. The pale blue suited her fair skin, and the silver among her curls gave the sour-faced woman enough elegance to pass for a lady at court.
Seraphiel produced a hand mirror and held it where Marielle could see herself properly.
"Here. The glass makes it difficult to see the embroidery."

chapters.title: Chapter 1975 Cunt Got Caught
paragraphs: Marielle took the mirror without thanking her. She tilted it to admire the silver branches nestled among her curls, then drew a loose strand forward beside her cheek.
"Oh, it looks even prettier with your curls..." Sera murmured, her eyes following the sleeve with open longing.
Marielle smiled at Sera. "Of course it does."
For once, one of his women was looking at her with envy instead of ridicule. She tilted the mirror so she could admire herself with the elf's longing face beside her reflection.
"Perfection."

She wanted this. She wanted the robe, the silver among her curls, and that envious look on such an admittedly gorgeous woman's face. Buying such an indulgence would eat into money she needed for equipment and travel, but here it was, already on her body.
She turned the mirror to catch more of the robe, smoothing its front with her free hand.

Quinlan glanced at Kaelira, who was watching the robe settle around its wearer with undisguised satisfaction. The circlet and its intricate rune structure were her work. His enchantments supplied the silk-like mantle and regulated the temperature within it.

"It keeps you cool in hot weather and warm in the cold," he explained. "The enchantment also shields your skin from harsh sunlight, including your face. The rune at your other temple lets you adjust the warmth."
Marielle didn't even seem to hear those boring words, fully absorbed in the artifact sitting on her scalp.
"I planned to give it to my wives as a honeymoon gift, but I'm ready to part ways with it if you agree to the terms."
Lucille stamped her foot.
"Darling! You promised me that!"
Quinlan faced his wife. Her green eyes shone with indignation as she caught his arm, pulling him closer.
"How cruel..." she whimpered, then inwardly purred, <Giving away my lovely present~ How dare you~>
Quinlan was glad for Synchra's coverage of his lips in this moment.
"It's only until the quest is over, sweetheart."
"Then why does she get to wear it?"
Ayame scoffed beside him, folding her arms with her cheeks puffed out.
"I haven't even tried it on yet."
She pressed against his other side, slipping her fingers between his gloved ones. Through the link came a delighted little giggle.
Quinlan squeezed her fingers. "I'm sorry. We'll get it back."
Marielle turned just enough to let the robe's long sleeve fall between herself and Lucille. She had no intention of taking it off for the sulking woman.

Marielle touched the rune at her other temple to test the cooling. Her fingers stopped pulling at the collar of her battle robe as the heat beneath it eased, and she lifted her chin to inspect how the circlet framed her face.
"How do I put it away?"
"With another touch of the first rune."
At her touch, the blue fabric thinned into light and withdrew into the silver band. Marielle promptly brought it back.
"Where did you buy this?"
"You can hold it until the quest is over. If we fail to do our agreed share of the work, it's yours. Otherwise, you give it back."
"Bastard still won't tell me..." Marielle grumbled as she smoothed the embroidered edge over her hip.
"I've seen nobles pay a great deal for worse."

"Then you understand what I'm offering. If we're as useless as you think and you'll have to carry the quest because we die one after the other, you can keep it. If we prove to be useful, you'll give it back."
Andre rested a hand on the counter between Quinlan and his wife.
"It's a comfort item, Marielle. Mild utility at best. If we're taking on such a responsibility for them, his armour would be better collateral."
Marielle finally lowered the mirror.
"That ugly thing? Don't be ridiculous."
"I could really use a suit of armour of such craftsmanship."
"Then you can buy yourself one when we get paid. If I give this artifact back, one of those useless women will die with it. What if it gets destroyed?"
She raised the mirror again, dismissing him before he could finish drawing breath. "No, Andre. Please use your head next time."

Seraphiel looked toward Quinlan, her mouth curving beneath the edge of her hood. Lucille still clung to his arm, wounded beyond consolation, while Ayame rubbed her cheek against his shoulder with a discontented little huff.
Hook, line, and sinker.
The haughty cunt got caught.
<Quin, I actually do want one now,> the Bloodmonger admitted. <I have an irresistible urge to show this bitch how much better I'd look in them.>
<...Women.>
<Hey! You did not just say that...>
Quinlan made no further comments as Marielle studied the circlet's reflection while addressing him.
"And I can wear it until we finish the quest?"
"Of course."
Lucille tightened her hold on Quinlan's arm at his answer. Marielle smiled at her over the mirror's rim.
"And who decides whether you've done your share?" Andre asked.
Quinlan looked toward the clerk. "Could we put the conditions in the contract?"
"Yes. You'll need to agree on the work first. I can record the item and when it's to be returned. Any disputed claim would go through the branch's review."

Marielle passed the hand mirror back to Seraphiel, then dismissed the robe and took off the circlet so the clerk could inspect it. When Lucille leaned closer to look, Marielle kept her hand beside it on the counter.
"Let's hear what we're being paid to do, then."
"The client is nearby," the clerk offered. "She comes in most afternoons hoping to recruit adventurers for the job herself."
The clerk took a communication artifact from beneath the counter and pressed its rune. When a voice answered, she leaned closer.
"Celia? We have adventurers asking about your expedition contract. Could you come to the Guild?"
A high-pitched, overly feminine voice responded with a squeal. "R-really?! Yes! I'll be right there! Please ask them to wait! No, don't let them leave even if they want to!!"
"...They can hear you."
"AH!!! I-I was just joking, of course!! Wait, I'll be right there!"
The connection ended with a clatter from the other side.
While they waited, the clerk prepared the joining forms and wrote down the circlet's functions. Marielle corrected her when she described the garment as a cloak.
"An outer robe. With embroidery."
Quinlan watched Seraphiel press her lips together. "How lucky..." she murmured.
A few minutes later, hurried footsteps approached from the square.
*Thud!*
"Ouch!"
Everyone at the counter turned toward the entrance. Through the door's glass pane, Quinlan caught a glimpse of a young woman rubbing her forehead before she seized the handle.
The door swung inward, and she rushed through with a bow clutched against her chest.
"I'm here! I'm Ce-"
Her boot caught the raised threshold. She pitched forward, tried to catch herself on her elbows, and landed with her face against the floor and her knees tucked beneath her.
The quiver on her back tipped over her shoulder. Arrows clattered around her head while she remained face down and ass up, her pale brown braid flung across the boards.
"Mmmnh... Ow..."
An arrow rolled to a stop against Quinlan's boot.
He looked from the item to the whimpering young woman's shuddering behind.
"...Seriously?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1976 Clumsy Celia
paragraphs: Quinlan watched Celia push herself off the floor of Sarthal's Adventurer's Guild, one hand clamped over her nose.
"I'm alright! Please don't leave!"

The archer who had been questioning Blossom started forward from beside the counter, but Lucille reached Celia first. The women from the contract boards had stayed to watch the negotiations, their own afternoon plans apparently forgotten.
"We haven't even introduced ourselves yet, sweetheart." Lucille offered her a hand while Quinlan bent down and gathered the scattered arrows using his hands for once instead of magic.
"Look at him," the archer murmured to the woman beside her. "Picking up her arrows after what he did to Harl..."
"Apparently you only need to worry if you're an arsehole," her friend replied over the rim of her mug.
The archer snorted while Quinlan reached for the last arrow.
Celia accepted Lucille's help, then hurried to collect her bow. When she turned back, Quinlan held out the arrows to her.
"Ah... Thank you. The door... I didn't see the..."

She gave up explaining and put them in her quiver before following Lucille to the counter. Her pale brown braid had been tied with a green ribbon, and loose strands clung to her thoroughly reddened cheeks.

Quinlan placed her in her early twenties, at least as far as looks went. She wore a serviceable travelling coat with newly sewn patches at the elbows, and the fingers gripping her bow were wrapped where the string had rubbed them raw.
"Y-you're interested?"
"We have questions," Marielle scowled. Unlike Quinlan and the gang, this woman seemingly did not find Celia's entrance amusing.
"Y-yes, naturally! I'll tell you all I can! Thank you for looking at it."
Her eyes moved over the women before stopping at Quinlan's helmet. She looked back at the clerk, who indicated the notice on the counter.
Seraphiel moved beside the counter, leaving room for Celia to set down her things.
"The notice says someone came back. Are they here in Sarthal?"
"My father. Edric. He's at home."
"Could you tell us what happened to him?"
Celia lowered her satchel onto the counter. Several folded papers protruded from its inner pocket, each marked with notes in a cramped hand.

"He went with an expedition to some ruins beneath the hills. They were surveying the underground passages. There are older maps, but parts of them... parts don't match anymore. They wanted to find out which routes were still usable."
She paused to wet her lips.

"People found him near the approach. He'd been hurt terribly. His legs, and his hands... They brought him back, and the healers repaired everything they could find. He can walk now. He can hold a cup."
Her fingers pressed against the papers.
"But he doesn't know where he is sometimes. He says things, but they don't... I can't understand what he's trying to tell me."
Seraphiel's expression softened.
"Did anyone else return?"
Celia shook her head at the elf.
"They haven't found anybody. I put everything I know in there. The route he took, the names, what he had with him. If something down there did this to him, perhaps..."
She tried to finish the sentence and couldn't.
Lucille touched the satchel beside her hand.
"You want us to find out what it was, so someone can help him."
"Yes. Please."
Aurora began reading the treatment notes with Celia's permission. Marielle pulled the contract toward herself and studied the payment terms instead.
"The funds are deposited?"
"All three hundred crowns," the clerk confirmed. "Thirty can be released for provisions when you sign. That leaves two hundred and seventy payable on completion."
"I borrowed the exact amount," Celia added quickly. "It's all there. I swear."
"Borrowed from whom?" Lucille asked.
"A lender."
"Against what?" The Bloodmonger had a sad little motherly smile, fearing the answer.
Celia's fingers rubbed together as she muttered under her breath. "The house..."
"Sweetheart..." Lucille exhaled. "What's the interest rate?"
"He's my father! I don't care about such a thing!"
"...Understandable," Marielle nodded along, satisfied. "Some things are worth more than any coin."
"Exactly!" Celia nodded vehemently.
However, what she did not notice was the mage's eyes that almost had gold coins replacing the irises.
"So be it," Lucille finally spoke up while glaring daggers into Marielle. "I'd do the same thing in your place."
That brought a smile to their quest giver.
"I know you can't promise to fix him. I just... I don't know what else to try."
Lucille stayed beside her while Andre examined the map.
"Have you been to this approach yourself?"
"As far as the last inhabited road. I asked about hiring a wagon, and I wrote down where we could get water."
She reached into the satchel and found the appropriate page immediately.
"I can come with you. I'll carry things. Food, water, whatever you need. I can cook simple meals, and I'll clean the equipment while you rest."
Celia held her bow a little closer.

"I only started training for this after Father came home, so I'm not very good yet. My level is still low. But I won't get in your way. I want you to stay fresh so you can... so you have the best chance should whatever got him also attack us."
Marielle tapped the reward line.

"Andre and I take half the payment remaining after the advance. Your party takes the other half, however many of you there are. Recovery expenses come from the provision allowance, and any salvage follows the contract."
The woman with the mug looked from Marielle and Andre to the much larger group around Quinlan.
"Half for the two of them?" she whispered.
The archer pursed her lips, watching to see what he would say.

Quinlan read the terms Aurora turned toward him. A hundred and thirty-five crowns for each party, with the provision money covering their shared expenses. Their portion would be split across far more people than the couple's.
Marielle was watching his helmet, waiting for an objection. He glanced at the map instead.

The job would take them into unexplored passages to face a threat nobody had identified, with whatever they accomplished going on their Guild record. He could discover more about Thalorind down there than by spending the day filling a basket with leaves.
Quinlan couldn't care less about negotiating with this greedy vulture now that he got what he wanted, namely the right to go on this expedition itself.

The fact that her future was rather 'uncertain' made him care even less. By not getting into petty squabbles with this bitch, he'd also increase their reputation, or at least not trash it to the very bottom.
Black Fang was already studying the route beside his wives.
Ayame was in agreement with him. "That works for us."
"Just like that?" the archer murmured. "I'd have argued."
"Did you see what he put up as security? I don't think he's worrying about his share of three hundred crowns."
"I don't care how rich you are, that's still a fortune."
"We're like beggars glancing at an emperor. Stop trying to understand."

The clerk drew out a joining form. Aurora went through Unbound's contribution with Andre: fighting, examining the site and its samples, and helping recover whatever they found. The couple would lead them along the expedition route and handle the Guild's reporting requirements.

Beside those duties, the clerk recorded the circlet as security for Unbound's work, to be returned when that work was completed. Marielle read the conditions before signing as expedition leader. Andre signed next, and Quinlan entered Unbound beneath their names.
Marielle put the circlet back on and touched the rune at her temple. The pale blue robe flowed over her shoulders again.
Celia watched the clerk stamp the completed form, then hugged the satchel against herself with her bow trapped awkwardly under one arm.
"Thank you... Thank you so much...."
"Good. Let's go," Marielle said. "You can take us to the approach. We should cover as much ground as possible before dark."
"Before we leave Sarthal, could you take us to your father?" Seraphiel asked Celia.
The young woman's grateful expression faltered as Marielle turned toward the elf.
"She's paid healers to disappoint her already. Must we lose an afternoon so you can have a turn?"
The woman with the mug lowered it without drinking.
"The girl's standing right there," she muttered to the archer, who had stopped smiling too. "Fucking cunt..."

"I'm alright!
Please don't leave!"
The archer who had been questioning Blossom started forward from beside the counter, but Lucille reached Celia first.
The women from the contract boards had stayed to watch the negotiations, their own afternoon plans apparently forgotten.
"We haven't even introduced ourselves yet, sweetheart." Lucille offered her a hand while Quinlan bent down and gathered the scattered arrows using his hands for once instead of magic.
"Look at him," the archer murmured to the woman beside her.
"Picking up her arrows after what he did to Harl..."
"Apparently you only need to worry if you're an arsehole," her friend replied over the rim of her mug.
The archer snorted while Quinlan reached for the last arrow.
Celia accepted Lucille's help, then hurried to collect her bow.
When she turned back, Quinlan held out the arrows to her.
Thank you.
The door...
I didn't see the..."
She gave up explaining and put them in her quiver before following Lucille to the counter.
Her pale brown braid had been tied with a green ribbon, and loose strands clung to her thoroughly reddened cheeks.
Quinlan placed her in her early twenties, at least as far as looks went.
She wore a serviceable travelling coat with newly sewn patches at the elbows, and the fingers gripping her bow were wrapped where the string had rubbed them raw.
"Y-you're interested?"
"We have questions," Marielle scowled.
Unlike Quinlan and the gang, this woman seemingly did not find Celia's entrance amusing.
"Y-yes, naturally!
I'll tell you all I can!
Thank you for looking at it."
Her eyes moved over the women before stopping at Quinlan's helmet.
She looked back at the clerk, who indicated the notice on the counter.
Seraphiel moved beside the counter, leaving room for Celia to set down her things.

Are they here in Sarthal?"
"My father.
Edric.
He's at home."
"Could you tell us what happened to him?"
Celia lowered her satchel onto the counter.

"He went with an expedition to some ruins beneath the hills.

They wanted to find out which routes were still usable."
She paused to wet her lips.
"People found him near the approach.

His legs, and his hands...
They brought him back, and the healers repaired everything they could find.
He can walk now.
He can hold a cup."
Her fingers pressed against the papers.
"But he doesn't know where he is sometimes.
He says things, but they don't...
I can't understand what he's trying to tell me."
Seraphiel's expression softened.
"Did anyone else return?"
Celia shook her head at the elf.
"They haven't found anybody.
I put everything I know in there.
The route he took, the names, what he had with him.
If something down there did this to him, perhaps..."
She tried to finish the sentence and couldn't.
Lucille touched the satchel beside her hand.
"You want us to find out what it was, so someone can help him."
"Yes.
Please."

Marielle pulled the contract toward herself and studied the payment terms instead.
"The funds are deposited?"
"All three hundred crowns," the clerk confirmed.
"Thirty can be released for provisions when you sign.
That leaves two hundred and seventy payable on completion."
"I borrowed the exact amount," Celia added quickly.
"It's all there.
I swear."
"Borrowed from whom?" Lucille asked.
"A lender."
"Against what?" The Bloodmonger had a sad little motherly smile, fearing the answer.
Celia's fingers rubbed together as she muttered under her breath.
"The house..."
"Sweetheart..." Lucille exhaled.
"What's the interest rate?"
"He's my father!
I don't care about such a thing!"
"...Understandable," Marielle nodded along, satisfied.
"Some things are worth more than any coin."
"Exactly!" Celia nodded vehemently.
However, what she did not notice was the mage's eyes that almost had gold coins replacing the irises.
"So be it," Lucille finally spoke up while glaring daggers into Marielle.
"I'd do the same thing in your place."
That brought a smile to their quest giver.
"I know you can't promise to fix him.
I just...
I don't know what else to try."
Lucille stayed beside her while Andre examined the map.
"Have you been to this approach yourself?"
"As far as the last inhabited road.
I asked about hiring a wagon, and I wrote down where we could get water."
She reached into the satchel and found the appropriate page immediately.
"I can come with you.
I'll carry things.
Food, water, whatever you need.
I can cook simple meals, and I'll clean the equipment while you rest."
Celia held her bow a little closer.
"I only started training for this after Father came home, so I'm not very good yet.
My level is still low.
But I won't get in your way.
I want you to stay fresh so you can... so you have the best chance should whatever got him also attack us."

chapters.title: Chapter 1977 Trapped
paragraphs: Celia lowered her eyes. Seraphiel held out a hand for the treatment notes Aurora had finished reading before the girl could begin apologizing.
"I'd like to see him and hear what they tried."
Aurora passed her the papers, and Sera turned them toward Marielle.
"She hired us to investigate what happened to him. His condition is part of that. If we rush out to kill whatever lives there, we might destroy the very thing we need to bring back."
Marielle looked toward Quinlan, evidently expecting the man signing the forms to settle his companion.
He stood beside Seraphiel and rested his hand against her waist.
"We'll do as my wife says so long as Celia lets us see her father."
Marielle stared at him, then raised her chin.
"I am leading this expedition. You signed under my name, so you will fall in line."
"That is true. But I won't agree to ignoring our only witness."
He kept his hand at Seraphiel's waist while the elf leaned against him, the treatment notes still held before her.
"We've barely signed and you're already being insubordinate?" Marielle hissed. "Perhaps I should have expected this from a man who lets his women decide everything for him."
Quinlan chuckled.
"My job is to help complete the quest. That's what we're doing. If you intend to stop us because you don't like my wife's - our party's only healer's - advice, you can give my circlet back."
Her fingers rose to the silver band among her curls.
"You gave me this as security!"

"The deal was that you'd get it if we are so useless we sabotage the quest. Examining the survivor is part of investigating what happened to him. You can't forbid us from doing it, then claim we were useless."
He turned his helmet toward the clerk.
"That's what we agreed, isn't it?"
She pulled the joining form closer, tracing the recorded duties with her finger.
"Yes. The security covers their contribution to the contract. It doesn't make every disagreement grounds for keeping it. If you disputed their work, the branch would review what happened."
Marielle's mouth opened, but her gaze dropped to the papers before she answered. Her name sat beside the very conditions she had checked before signing.
She had imagined watching these fools fail, then taking their lovely artifact home. Now she would have to explain why she had prevented their healer from doing the work written on that same sheet.
The women around Quinlan were enjoying her predicament with undisguised sadism. Lucille's smile grew as Marielle caught her watching the hand still clutching the circlet.
"Well? Give it back, then!" the woman with the mug called.
"Hahaha! He totally played the dumb bitch!"
Laughter burst from the little gathering. The archer caught her friend's sleeve, bending toward her while another woman tried unsuccessfully to smother a snort.
Marielle turned on them.
"Do you have something to say to me?"
Her growl cut through their laughter. The archer straightened, suddenly conscious of the staff in the Grade Three mage's hand, and her friend raised her mug to hide her mouth.
"No, no. Please continue."
Marielle glared at her until she looked down into her drink. Seraphiel made no attempt to hide her own smile.
The mage turned back to him. He waited with his arm around his wife, quite content to let Marielle decide how much longer everyone would be standing here staring at her crown.
Celia stared at the black helmet. She had been afraid to address him, and the air with which he carried himself still made it difficult to find her voice.

Yet the woman beside him had asked to see her father. She had read the notes. She was already treating him as someone worth visiting, and this scary man was backing her up to do so, instead of hurrying to get paid.
Celia wanted that so badly that her eyes began to sting.
"I... I'd like you to come. My home's doors are open to you!"
Marielle's gaze returned to her, and Celia tightened her grip on the bow.
"Please..."
Celia kept her eyes on Marielle, waiting for an answer. If she had to ask again to bring this healer home, she would.
Andre rolled the map closed.
"We need supplies anyway. We can leave properly prepared in the morning."
Marielle smoothed her new sleeve, then picked up her staff.
"At dawn. If you aren't ready, you can hear about your father when we get back."
"I will be," Celia promised at once.
Seraphiel smiled at her.
"Let's meet your father."
While the clerk counted out their thirty-crown provision advance, Lilith returned from the boards with a different notice.
"We're taking a road inspection. My senses are telling me there will be higher-level monsters than advertised," the Spellblade grinned, prepared for bloodshed.
"It's in a different direction. We'll see you back at the inn before you leave," Jallen added.
"Try not to miss us too much," Kitsara winked at Lilith.
"Yeah, yeah. I'll struggle through it somehow."
Scar caught Quinlan's eye while Void murmured against her ear.
<She wants a private word before we split up,> Scar relayed.
Quinlan waited until the clerk had handed Andre the provision money, then followed Celia and the others out of the Guild.

At the edge of the square, Seraphiel stopped with Celia to ask which way her house lay. Quinlan drew Scar and Void into the side street beside them, where his companions screened them from the passing traffic.
Void slipped down from Scar's back and leaned close enough to speak beneath his helmet.
"Mm... Before you go. Could you enslave me?"
Quinlan looked at Black Fang.
She inspected the buildings across the street.
"You too?" Quinlan asked Void.
"Scar can pass things on... but then I have to ask her to ask you." Void yawned. "I'd like to bother you myself."
Scar folded her arms.
"She means whenever she wants."
"Mm. Yes. Also because Miss Rogue over here uses her undead body with reckless abandon sometimes... If she dies, what then...?"
"Makes sense," Quinlan nodded then wryly chuckled under his breath. "The second aloof woman of the day asking for slavery. Thalorind is a wild place."
"I'm not aloof. Also, wait, what?" Her voice rose as her head snapped toward a certain Venomborne Terror. "Don't tell me... So that's what that was about."
A soft smile found Void's lips as she next looked at Seraphiel. "That's why she cast healing spells on a healthy Black Fang... To mask the mana expenditure..."
With Scar standing between them and the square, he cast [Subjugation]. The sleepy mage accepted it with a satisfied little hum, and he opened a conversation with her through [Master's Link].
<Reply by thinking of talking to me mentally. Might take a few tries but->
<Scar is the cutest ever.>
<...That was quick. And yep. Agreed. Not many can rival our cutest ghost girl.>
"Master." Scar spoke with a flat expression. "You're thinking of something weird, aren't you?"
"Me? Never."
"Accepting [Subjugation] tired me out... Please..."
"...Haaah," a weary exhale left Scar's lips as she turned, presenting Void her back.
"Yay!" Void gave a happy little giggle and hopped onto Scar's back, wrapping her arms around the rogue's shoulders.
"It doesn't even take any energy to accept," Scar grumbled as she caught Void beneath the thighs.
"Mentally..."
"Mentally you're challenged, yes."
"Hey... Cruel..."
The two kept bickering as they went after Lilith.
Quinlan watched them leave, then rejoined Seraphiel as Celia pointed out the street leading to her house.
It was time to undertake Unbound's first quest, a quest that would prove worthy of Unbound's introduction!

chapters.title: Chapter 1978 Deep Trauma
paragraphs: Celia led them away from the Guild square through streets that narrowed as they climbed from the harbour.

Quinlan walked beside Seraphiel while she asked whether Edric slept through the night. Ahead of them, Celia kept turning to answer without slowing down, until Lucille gently caught her elbow before she backed into a basket outside a shop.
"We aren't chasing you, sweetheart."
"S-sorry!"
"You don't have to apologize for that either."
Celia gave her a bashful smile and faced forward.
The house stood halfway up a lane behind a baker's courtyard. A neighbour opened the door at Celia's knock, wiping her hands on a cloth.
"He's by the window. Managed most of his soup."
Celia's relief was immediate.
"Thank you. These kind adventurers accepted!"
The older woman looked past her at the gathering in the lane. Her eyes remained on Quinlan for a good few seconds. Finally, she smiled.
"Thank you."
"There's nothing to thank us for," Quinlan replied. It was just work.
"I know. Yet I'm grateful nonetheless."
"Auntie stays with Father when I'm out," Celia explained to Seraphiel. "She's agreed to look after him while we travel too."
"Of course I have. Come in."
Inside, the sitting room had been rearranged around a padded chair by the window. A cup rested on a low stool within its occupant's reach, and a blanket covered his legs despite the afternoon warmth.
Celia set down her bow before approaching him.
"Father? It's me. I've brought some people to meet you."
Edric was a broad man with greying hair and hands that still looked capable of lifting his daughter bodily onto his shoulders. Those hands lay open on the blanket.
His eyes followed her braid.
"You're..."
"Celia."
"Mm."
She knelt beside his chair and waited while he studied her face. Quinlan watched the hope return to her expression, helplessly quick, before Edric looked toward the empty corner behind her.
"No. Can't... can't leave that."
"It's alright, Father. We aren't taking anything away."
He began rubbing his fingertips together.
Seraphiel stopped near the doorway and turned toward the group.
"Could most of us wait outside? I'd like to give him some room."
Ayame guided the others back toward the courtyard. Kaelira remained with Aurora and Lucille, while Quinlan stood beside the open door.
"He's used to me being here," Celia said anxiously.
"Of course you're staying. He's your father." Seraphiel crouched where Edric could see her. "Hello. I'm Sera. Your daughter brought me to meet you. May I sit with you?"
He looked at the space above her shoulder.
"Too... high."
Seraphiel waited, then drew a chair closer and sat beside him.
She offered him the cup from the stool. He took it after Celia touched its handle, drank, and returned it to the same place.
When Sera asked whether his hand hurt, he stared at her without answering.
"He doesn't like people holding his wrists," Celia said. "If you show him what you want first, he sometimes lets you."
Seraphiel thanked her and held out her own hand. She waited for him to place his palm against it before examining his fingers.

Quinlan stayed by the door. He remembered enough from Earth to know that a man could survive something his mind kept living through afterward, but remembering a few accounts hardly made him a physician.

He studied Edric's restless hands. Whatever had happened underground had left this much behind even after the wounds healed. Before taking his family down there, he wanted to get as much information as possible on what they might be exposing themselves to.
Aurora sat at the table with the treatment notes spread before her.
"Celia, are these all the medicines he's been given?"
"I kept the labels. They're in the folded paper at the back."
"And these marks beside the names?"
"Whether he slept. Whether he ate. That one means he knew who I was without being told."
Aurora found only a few of that mark.
Lucille drew another chair beside Celia while Aurora unfolded the medicine labels and compared them with the entries.
"Could I borrow these tonight? You've recorded the changes in his medicine too, so I can check whether any of them helped."
"Yes! Of course."

Celia looked down, blinking hard. After so many evenings recording the same frightened words, she'd begun to wonder why she bothered. Now Aurora was spreading those pages out to study them, and she was terribly glad she hadn't stopped.
"His wounds have closed well," Seraphiel said after Edric withdrew his hand. "Can he move around the house without falling?"
"Yes, if someone stays with him. Sometimes he stops because... because he thinks there's something in front of him. But there isn't."
Seraphiel looked at the clear floor between his chair and the kitchen.
"I wish I could promise you a healing spell would stop that. But I can't."
Celia swallowed. "Yes... I know."
"May we see the things he came back with?" Kaelira asked. "There might be damage that tells us more about where he was."
Celia left her satchel with Lucille and hurried to a cupboard beneath the stairs.
Kaelira helped her bring out a wrapped bundle. Inside lay a torn coat, a damaged armguard, and a knife whose edge had been chipped repeatedly near the tip.
"The people who found him brought these. I cleaned the coat, but I didn't know what to do with the armour."
Kaelira bent over the armguard, examining its crushed plates without trying to force them apart.
"Could you leave the armour with me? I might be able to get something out of this."
She took the bundle to the table while Celia returned to her father's chair.
His gaze had found the bow beside the door.
"Mine..."
Celia followed his stare.
"It's mine, Father. You bought it for me."
"Does he recognize it?" Lucille asked.
"He used to check it before I practised. I only shot at targets in the garden then. He said I pulled it wrong."
For the first time since entering the house, she smiled without forcing it.
"He said it very often."
Lucille fetched the bow and gave it to her. At Seraphiel's invitation, Celia showed her father the grip before resting the unstrung weapon across his knees.
His thumb moved over a worn place in the wood.
"Here."
Celia leaned closer.
He tapped the grip, then reached for her hand. She let him move it, her eyes fixed on his face while he shifted her thumb.
"Too... tight. You'll..."
His hand stopped.
Celia kept hers where he had placed it.
"I'll pull the shot to the side," she whispered. "I remember."
Edric stared at the bow. Whatever he had been trying to say slipped away, and he began rubbing the wood with the same restless motion he had used on the blanket.
His daughter bent her head.
Lucille put an arm around her shoulders while Seraphiel lifted the bow away before Edric could grip it hard enough to hurt himself.
"Was that useful?" Celia asked, her voice painfully small.
"He was trying to teach you again," Sera said softly. "Did you see how he reached for your hand?"
"He remembered how you should hold it. That gives me hope, Celia. There's still something familiar we can reach."
Celia's eyes widened. "R-really?! I thought the same but the healers said..."

"If they told you to give up because their spells didn't work, I disagree." Seraphiel's voice grew firm. "I can't promise I'll heal him either. But I'd like to find out why we can't before deciding there's nothing more to try."

She knew that helplessness far too well. Quinlan's exhaustion after creating Synchra, Iris's class refusing healing... Being able to mend flesh had left her horribly unprepared for some of the things her family endured.
It infuriated her to stand beside someone she loved and have nothing to offer. She had begun studying other ways to help when her magic failed, and wanted badly to put that learning to use here.
"I see..." Celia's fingers curled into a fist. "I'm so glad you were the ones who took my quest..."

sentences.text: Celia led them away from the Guild square through streets that narrowed as they climbed from the harbour.
Quinlan walked beside Seraphiel while she asked whether Edric slept through the night.
Ahead of them, Celia kept turning to answer without slowing down, until Lucille gently caught her elbow before she backed into a basket outside a shop.
"We aren't chasing you, sweetheart."
"S-sorry!"
"You don't have to apologize for that either."
Celia gave her a bashful smile and faced forward.
The house stood halfway up a lane behind a baker's courtyard.
A neighbour opened the door at Celia's knock, wiping her hands on a cloth.
"He's by the window.
Managed most of his soup."
Celia's relief was immediate.
"Thank you.
These kind adventurers accepted!"
The older woman looked past her at the gathering in the lane.
Her eyes remained on Quinlan for a good few seconds.
Finally, she smiled.
"Thank you."
"There's nothing to thank us for," Quinlan replied.
It was just work.
"I know.
Yet I'm grateful nonetheless."
"Auntie stays with Father when I'm out," Celia explained to Seraphiel.
"She's agreed to look after him while we travel too."
"Of course I have.
Come in."
Inside, the sitting room had been rearranged around a padded chair by the window.
A cup rested on a low stool within its occupant's reach, and a blanket covered his legs despite the afternoon warmth.
Celia set down her bow before approaching him.
"Father?
It's me.
I've brought some people to meet you."
Edric was a broad man with greying hair and hands that still looked capable of lifting his daughter bodily onto his shoulders.
Those hands lay open on the blanket.
His eyes followed her braid.
"You're..."
"Celia."
"Mm."
She knelt beside his chair and waited while he studied her face.
Quinlan watched the hope return to her expression, helplessly quick, before Edric looked toward the empty corner behind her.
"No.
Can't... can't leave that."
"It's alright, Father.
We aren't taking anything away."
He began rubbing his fingertips together.
Seraphiel stopped near the doorway and turned toward the group.
"Could most of us wait outside?
I'd like to give him some room."
Ayame guided the others back toward the courtyard.
Kaelira remained with Aurora and Lucille, while Quinlan stood beside the open door.

"Hello.

Your daughter brought me to meet you.
May I sit with you?"
He looked at the space above her shoulder.
"Too... high."

"He doesn't like people holding his wrists," Celia said.
"If you show him what you want first, he sometimes lets you."
Seraphiel thanked her and held out her own hand.
She waited for him to place his palm against it before examining his fingers.

Whatever had happened underground had left this much behind even after the wounds healed.
Before taking his family down there, he wanted to get as much information as possible on what they might be exposing themselves to.
Aurora sat at the table with the treatment notes spread before her.
"Celia, are these all the medicines he's been given?"
"I kept the labels.
They're in the folded paper at the back."
"And these marks beside the names?"
"Whether he slept.
Whether he ate.
That one means he knew who I was without being told."
Aurora found only a few of that mark.

You've recorded the changes in his medicine too, so I can check whether any of them helped."
"Yes!
Of course."

Now Aurora was spreading those pages out to study them, and she was terribly glad she hadn't stopped.

"Can he move around the house without falling?"
"Yes, if someone stays with him.
Sometimes he stops because... because he thinks there's something in front of him.
But there isn't."
Seraphiel looked at the clear floor between his chair and the kitchen.
"I wish I could promise you a healing spell would stop that.
But I can't."
Celia swallowed.
"Yes...
I know."

chapters.title: Chapter 1979 Silk Thread
paragraphs: At the table, Kaelira turned the armguard beneath the window light. One of its overlapping plates had folded into the next, trapping dirt and a wad of pale webbing inside the joint.
She set her small tool beneath the bent edge.
"Quin, could you hold this plate clear while I loosen the strap?"

He came to the table and held the plate up by its edge. Kaelira loosened the leather beneath it and lifted the trapped webbing with her tool. Fine silk threads stretched between the bent pieces of metal.
"Spider silk," Quinlan said. "Or something very much like it."
Kaelira tilted the armguard toward him. "There's quite a bit caught in here."
He looked from the webbing to Edric, who was rubbing his fingertips over the blanket again.
"Celia, I want to test something on your father. He may react strongly."
She looked back at her father. He hadn't followed their conversation, and she smoothed the blanket beneath his restless hands while she considered it.
"As long as it might help him, please try."
Quinlan called Kitsara in.
The foxkin eyed her lover with excitement. "What is it, husband? Did you miss me so much that you couldn't-"
"Please turn into a spider."
"-live a single moment longer without me... Wait, what?"
"Please turn into a spider."
"I heard you!! I don't like spiders..."
"Please?"
"Haaah... What am I to do with you? To think you finally called on me-"
"Today, please," Aurora interjected.
"..." The foxy's eyes narrowed. Then she scoffed. "Fine. What kind?"
"Just an average one. But perhaps make it bigger so he can see clearly."

"What I don't do for my husband..." Kitsara crouched on the clear floor near the doorway, well away from his chair. With [Perfect Form], her body shrank and reshaped into a brown spider no larger than a dinner plate, eight jointed legs spread beneath her.
Edric's eyes fixed on her.
"Off! Get it... get it off her!"
He recoiled into the chair and caught Celia's sleeve, dragging her toward him.
Lucille supported Celia around the waist as Kitsara immediately returned to her foxkin form.
<Yep...> Quinlan sighed. <We're dealing with some kind of spider monster.>

He could hear a lot of wincing on the other side of his link. His girls might've been the most amazing of warrioresses, but that didn't mean they were immune to the shortfalls of womanhood, such as having an unnatural distaste for spiders.
Though, to be fair to them, a few did not care one bit.
"I always knew spiders were freaky as fuck, but isn't this-"
"You can leave now, dear." Lucille addressed Kitsara from beside Celia. Her tone, however, was anything but accommodating. The Slutty Foxy was ordered to abdicate the premises.
"Okay." Kitsara slipped outside before her damned husband could decide to test other spider forms using his loving, utterly adorable, cute and gorgeous, loyal beyond reason, wife.
"She's gone, Father. Look, she's gone."
Celia kept speaking while Seraphiel crouched within his sight.
"You're at home," Sera told him gently. "Your daughter's here with you."
His breath came in gasps. Celia held his hand against her sleeve until his grip began to ease, and nobody asked him another question.
"Had to... cut..."
Celia leaned closer to hear him.
"Couldn't get... her loose. Still... moving."
Her eyes rose to Seraphiel's face. The elf stayed beside them while Edric's fingers loosened, then helped Celia free her sleeve.
"That's enough for today," Sera said softly.
Quinlan agreed. Kaelira wrapped the armguard with the webbing still caught inside it, and Aurora gathered the treatment notes while they gave Celia time with her father.
They spoke in the kitchen while the neighbour took her place beside his chair.
"Does that mean somebody's alive?" Celia asked.
"I don't know, Celia," Seraphiel answered. "Even if some were alive back then, days have passed since."
"I understand..." Celia pressed her hands over her mouth. Lucille drew her against her shoulder, and the young woman finally let herself cry.
Quinlan left them together and stepped into the courtyard. When Seraphiel joined him, he put an arm around her waist, drawing her close.
"You alright?"
"Yeah..." She bit her lips in frustration. "I just wish I could do more."
"You gave a desperate daughter hope where all other healers fed her desperation. You did plenty already."

"...That's one way to look at it, I suppose..." Sera rested against his chest for a moment. Celia had gone back to her father's chair and was telling her neighbour what they had found. Through the open door, Quinlan could see Edric listening quietly beside them.
They walked farther into the courtyard to join the others, leaving the doorway clear for Celia and her neighbour. Once they were away from the house, the elf looked up at Quinlan, her nose wrinkling.
"An entire nest of spiders...? Ugh."
Kitsara edged closer on his other side, rubbing her arms.
"Quinnie... Is it too late to choose another quest?"
"You were just a spider."
"Yes, and I hated every moment of it. I need to scrub myself off."
"Sure. [Water Jet]."
Quinlan pointed at the hissy foxkin, sending a broad gush of water over her head. He kept the pressure gentle enough that she barely swayed, but her indignant squeal carried across the courtyard.
"Kyaah!"
Her white hair fell over her face in wet curtains. Behind her, five magnificent tails sagged into dripping ropes of fur, and water ran from her clothes onto the paving.
Kitsara stood with her mouth open while he lowered his hand.
She slowly parted the hair covering her eyes. The betrayal in those red depths was immense.
"I turned into a fucking spider for you."
Sera pressed a hand over her mouth, but the laugh escaped through her fingers anyway. Ayame leaned against her shoulder, giggling at the drenched foxkin's expression.
"You said you wanted a wash," Quinlan replied.
"You absolute bastard! I'll make you pay!"
Kitsara lunged for his casting hand. In response, he sent another shower for her.
"Pfft! Stop! I'll bite you!"
She swiped wet hair out of her mouth and reached for his wrist again. Quinlan lifted his hand beyond her grasp, grinning as the water followed her across the paving.
"If you don't stop, I'm turning into a man for a whole year!"
The water stopped before she finished drawing breath.
Kitsara blinked up at him. His hand had dropped to his side.
"A year?" Serika laughed. "You wouldn't last a day without climbing into his bed."
Sera looked from the dripping foxkin to Quinlan's suddenly rigid posture.
"Quin... You believed her?"
"No. But I don't want to see her try. Not even for a fucking second."
The sheer disgust in his voice set them laughing again. Kitsara glanced down at herself, then back at his face, her wet ears beginning to lift.
"I'll tell on you when I meet your mothers..."
She stepped forward and wrapped both arms around him. Her soaked hair slapped against his neck while her wet clothes pressed against his front.
"Bastard... Why must I love you so much?"
Quinlan accepted the embrace without a word.
With the check-up done, it was time for Unbound to begin their first proper expedition into Thalorind's new continent!
