chapters.title: Chapter 1980 Rookie Adventurers
paragraphs: Quinlan was still in the courtyard outside Celia's house when the young woman returned with a pack nearly as wide as her shoulders.

They had finished examining her father, and Aurora had written down what they wanted for the expedition. Apparently, Celia had prepared a list of her own. A pot knocked against the doorframe as she squeezed through it.
Serika caught the pack's lower strap before the girl could lose her balance.
"Were you planning to carry the kitchen too?"
"I've been practising every morning!"
"No, this won't do."
"W-what do you mean?"
"What I just said." Serika removed the heaviest pot and held it out to Quinlan while she adjusted Celia's straps. He accepted it with a glance at his former teacher.
Apparently, he had volunteered.
"Sure."
Quinlan channelled mana into his pocket ring, and the pot vanished from his hand in a brief flash.
Celia stopped adjusting her strap.
"Eh?"
Her gaze darted from his empty palm to the place where the pot had been. Serika unfastened another from the pack and passed it to him, and that one disappeared too.
"A... a pocket ring?"
Celia stared up at his helmet. She'd been worrying about how much this man and his companions would have to carry, and he had a pocket ring.
An actual pocket ring, which he was using to store her battered cookware.
These people were really, really rich.
"But those are just my cooking things..."
"They're worth their weight in gold if they'll help feed the misses," Quinlan mused.
"A-ah! I'll do my best!"
Quinlan held out his hand for the lid still strapped to her pack. Celia hurried to unfasten it, watching in fascination as he stored that too.
He was so casual about it. Beside him, Serika was already checking what else they could take off her shoulders, as though making a kitchen disappear was the obvious solution to an overfilled pack.

"I appreciate your eagerness, and I'll do everything I can to help you," Serika told Celia. "But when I look at you, all my danger senses scream at me, telling me I must do something before the worst happens."
"O-oh... I understand..." The girl's lips trembled as her gaze found her feet.

Serika couldn't help but smile at the sight, reaching out to pat the girl's shoulders. "If you listen to me, you'll be an integral part of the mission without forcing us all to take on unnecessary risks to protect you. Will you do that for me? You can have your cooking items back when it's time to feed the 'misses'."
She finished her statement while sending Quinlan an amused sideways glance.
Celia's eyes widened, then she loosened the strap rubbing her hip so Serika could adjust the load. "I'm sorry, I didn't think of it like that."
Serika's smile only deepened as she saw the girl understand how reckless her behavior was. "This is why we're here."
"Are you really rookies...?" the girl couldn't help but ask.
"Rookie adventurers? Yes. But we might have a bit of relevant experience under our belts."
"A bit, huh..." Celia's eyes narrowed, going from one extremely competent woman to the next, before landing on Quinlan himself.

Then she bowed deep, in a perfect ninety-degree motion. "Once again, thank you for accepting my quest, Unbound! If I do something reckless, please tell me! I'll listen to your every word. I'll be in your care!"
The eagerness with which she spoke her declaration softened quite a few women's gazes.
"Celia is a very good girl!!" Blossom finally decreed, petting her lush hair with eager motion.
"Hie..." Celia yelped at the unexpected gesture.
After saying goodbye to her father and checking the evening arrangements with their neighbour, Celia led them toward the shops surrounding the Guild.
Quinlan had their fifteen-crown share of the provision advance tucked away for their purchases. How much that bought was something he intended to find out before spending it.

The signs along the street offered a useful start. An eating house advertised stew, bread, and watered ale for two bits. Bits seemed to be the bronze coins of Sarthal, but their exact exchange rates he didn't know.
Farther along, a harpy set a tray of glazed pastries on her stall, where the little slate beside them also read two bits apiece.

Brown flight feathers fanned along her arms as she lowered the tray. Clawed fingers extended from the ends of her wings, deftly taking up a glazing brush while her taloned feet gripped the wooden perch behind the stall.
Quinlan glanced from those birdlike limbs to her face, framed by loose auburn hair.
'A harpy? Weren't those supposed to be sex fiends too?' Important matters began swirling in the Primordial Villain's head, such as, 'How do they compare to a succubus?'
Nyxara's indignant huff reached him through their bond from his soul realm.
<How dare you, my Ruin! Those are ravenous fiends! They'll descend on a man and drag him off to their nest!>
Quinlan kept walking while she drew herself another offended breath.
<My daughters are gorgeous, exquisitely feminine women! We seduce. We enchant. There is no comparison to be had.>
<Gorgeous, exquisitely feminine women who are ravenous fiends preying on men. And women. Doesn't seem that different to me.>
<...Your wife is unhappy with your behavior.>
<Goddess have mercy.> His voice was perfectly flat.
<...We'll talk about this later, mister.>
Blossom's nose twitched.
Quinlan glanced down at her. The dogkin was watching a tray with immense concentration, her blue eyes following the woman as she brushed glaze over the last bun.
Her tail began wagging so hard that Kitsara moved hers out of its path.
Yet Blossom kept walking beside him. She even managed to face forward, although her nose remained firmly interested in what they were leaving behind.
Quinlan felt a smile spread beneath his helmet.
"Give me a moment," he told Celia, turning toward the stall.
Blossom followed him at once.
"Master?"
"Could I have that one?" He indicated the pastry his dogkin had been staring at, then took a crown from his own money.
The harpy caught a paper bag between her claws. When she saw the coin, the feathers along her arms puffed out.
She looked up at his black helmet, then down at the crown again.
"For one bun?"
"Yes."
"You haven't anything smaller?"
"I'm afraid not."
"Ninety-eight bits in change..." The woman opened her cashbox and peered inside. "You've chosen a fine way to empty my till, sir."
"It's fine." Quinlan was ready to move on, turning, when the woman spoke up again.
"No, no. I can manage."
She counted smaller coins onto the counter with soft clicks of her claws. Quinlan watched her work while the smell of warm pastry drew Blossom closer to his arm.

One hundred bits to a crown, then. A single coin bought fifty of these buns, or fifty meals at the eating house. He could feed someone for quite a while with what he had casually placed on the counter.
And Celia had borrowed three hundred crowns.
The seller pushed his change toward him and slipped the pastry into its bag. Quinlan put the coins away, then offered the treat to Blossom.
"Here."
She stared at it.
"For Blossom?"
"I thought you might like one."
"But Blossom didn't even ask..."
"I saw what I saw."
She glanced behind herself, where the guilty appendage was doing absolutely nothing to conceal her happiness.
"Master...!"
Blossom took the bag and threw her free arm around his waist, pressing her cheek against him. Her delighted little laugh escaped into his armour while he stroked her blonde hair.
Quinlan had conquered a continent, but buying a bun for this girl still made him feel absurdly accomplished. She was hugging him as though he had brought her the whole damned bakery.
"Blossom loves Master so much!"
"I love you too."
*Whoosh!*
Blossom launched herself off the paving in a golden blur, the rush of her movement whipping Celia's braid across her shoulder.
"Eh?"
The dogkin planted her free palm on Quinlan's shoulder and vaulted over it. Her bare legs swept through the air as she arched above him, blonde hair flying behind her.
Quinlan followed the gorgeous curve of her body with considerable interest. His girl was putting on quite a show over a pastry.
With a giggling twist of her hips, Blossom swung a leg over his head and landed astride his shoulders. Her soft thighs hugged either side of his neck, with her calves hanging down his chest.
"Master~!"
He caught her thighs without moving from where he stood. Her tail lashed happily down his back, while the paper bag remained upright in her raised hand.
Celia was still staring at the place where Blossom had been standing.
"H-how did you... Wow..."
Seated above Quinlan's head, the dogkin was already peeking into her bag.
"Comfortable?"
"Very!"
Blossom drew the bun halfway out of its bag, then rested her free hand on top of his helmet. Her first bite earned a blissful little hum above his head.
He wanted to buy her another already.
Celia led them on to an outfitter near the Guild. Blossom took another delighted bite while Quinlan adjusted his hold on her soft thighs.
Quinlan ducked beneath the outfitter's doorframe so Blossom wouldn't hit her head. She folded her ears down anyway, protecting them with the hand holding her pastry.

The Fomorian behind the counter looked up from repairing a pack. Quinlan recognized the blue-gray skin and tusks from the pirates at sea. Here, the man's lower hands held a torn strap while his upper pair worked an awl and thread through the leather.
His eyes travelled from Quinlan's armour to the dogkin happily eating on his shoulders.
"...What can I help you with?"

They had finished examining her father, and Aurora had written down what they wanted for the expedition.
Apparently, Celia had prepared a list of her own.
A pot knocked against the doorframe as she squeezed through it.
Serika caught the pack's lower strap before the girl could lose her balance.
"Were you planning to carry the kitchen too?"
"I've been practising every morning!"
"No, this won't do."
"W-what do you mean?"
"What I just said." Serika removed the heaviest pot and held it out to Quinlan while she adjusted Celia's straps.
He accepted it with a glance at his former teacher.
Apparently, he had volunteered.
"Sure."
Quinlan channelled mana into his pocket ring, and the pot vanished from his hand in a brief flash.
Celia stopped adjusting her strap.
"Eh?"
Her gaze darted from his empty palm to the place where the pot had been.
Serika unfastened another from the pack and passed it to him, and that one disappeared too.
"A... a pocket ring?"
Celia stared up at his helmet.
She'd been worrying about how much this man and his companions would have to carry, and he had a pocket ring.
An actual pocket ring, which he was using to store her battered cookware.
These people were really, really rich.
"But those are just my cooking things..."
"They're worth their weight in gold if they'll help feed the misses," Quinlan mused.
"A-ah!
I'll do my best!"
Quinlan held out his hand for the lid still strapped to her pack.
Celia hurried to unfasten it, watching in fascination as he stored that too.
He was so casual about it.
Beside him, Serika was already checking what else they could take off her shoulders, as though making a kitchen disappear was the obvious solution to an overfilled pack.
"I appreciate your eagerness, and I'll do everything I can to help you," Serika told Celia.
"But when I look at you, all my danger senses scream at me, telling me I must do something before the worst happens."
I understand..." The girl's lips trembled as her gaze found her feet.
Serika couldn't help but smile at the sight, reaching out to pat the girl's shoulders.
"If you listen to me, you'll be an integral part of the mission without forcing us all to take on unnecessary risks to protect you.
Will you do that for me?
You can have your cooking items back when it's time to feed the 'misses'."
She finished her statement while sending Quinlan an amused sideways glance.
Celia's eyes widened, then she loosened the strap rubbing her hip so Serika could adjust the load.
"I'm sorry, I didn't think of it like that."
Serika's smile only deepened as she saw the girl understand how reckless her behavior was.
"This is why we're here."
"Are you really rookies...?" the girl couldn't help but ask.
"Rookie adventurers?
Yes.
But we might have a bit of relevant experience under our belts."
"A bit, huh..." Celia's eyes narrowed, going from one extremely competent woman to the next, before landing on Quinlan himself.
Then she bowed deep, in a perfect ninety-degree motion.
"Once again, thank you for accepting my quest, Unbound!
If I do something reckless, please tell me!
I'll listen to your every word.
I'll be in your care!"
The eagerness with which she spoke her declaration softened quite a few women's gazes.
"Celia is a very good girl!!" Blossom finally decreed, petting her lush hair with eager motion.
"Hie..." Celia yelped at the unexpected gesture.

Quinlan had their fifteen-crown share of the provision advance tucked away for their purchases.
How much that bought was something he intended to find out before spending it.
The signs along the street offered a useful start.
An eating house advertised stew, bread, and watered ale for two bits.
Bits seemed to be the bronze coins of Sarthal, but their exact exchange rates he didn't know.

We seduce.
We enchant.

chapters.title: Chapter 1981 Stealing Tech
paragraphs: Aurora laid her list on the counter, giving the man something else to look at. He set down the awl and lifted the paper, keeping the unfinished repair secured in his lower hands. While he read, Kaelira picked up a lantern from a shelf.
"May I open this?"
"Go ahead."
The smith opened the casing. A little light shone inside a metal cage, brightening when her fingertip brushed the rune beside its latch.
Kaelira turned the lantern over, running her thumb along the rim beneath it. Her attention caught on the gap between the cage and its outer frame.
"That's nice. You could cave this corner in and still keep it clear of the inscription."
The outfitter put Aurora's list down.
"That's right. Dented ones come back for repairs. Usually still lit."

Kaelira pressed the shutter's catch, turning the lantern toward an empty patch of wall before opening it. The light narrowed into a bright circle. She adjusted it again, spreading the glow across the shelves, then went straight back to examining the join underneath.
"A replaceable cage would make repairs easier."
"It would. Costs more to make it that way, though. These sell for two crowns."
<The light enchantment is simple. You've made much better,> Kaelira told Quinlan, turning the lantern over to study the attachment again.
<You're already making another one in your head, aren't you?> he asked.
<Perhaps...>
Kaelira looked up at him, then down at the lantern still occupying her hands.
<I... It would be useful for Celia. She could carry it attached to her backpack.>
Quinlan glanced toward their guide. She was studying a rack of carrying slings with Seraphiel, listening intently as the elf explained how they could support someone who couldn't climb out alone.
"We'll take it," he told the outfitter. <We can take it apart tonight if you want.>
<Gotta steal Sarthal tech?> Kaelira asked flatly, knowing her man far too well.
<Gotta steal Sarthal tech.> Her suspicions were confirmed, prompting the tomboy elf to smile softly.
"Good choice. Oil lamps are cheaper, but this keeps burning if you get it wet. You feed mana into the mark here when the light begins to weaken."
He demonstrated on the lantern's base, then began gathering the ordinary supplies. Serika looked up at Blossom.
"Good choice. Oil lamps are cheaper, but this keeps burning if you get it wet. You feed mana into the mark here when the light begins to weaken."
He demonstrated on the lantern's base, then began gathering the ordinary supplies. Serika looked up at Blossom.
"When are you planning to come down?"
The dogkin swallowed her mouthful.
"Blossom is scouting!"
"The shop?"
"She can see much farther from here!"
To demonstrate, Blossom looked over the shelves from her perch, with crumbs clinging to the corner of her mouth.
"Having the high ground is very important," Quinlan agreed.
His thumbs stroked the soft skin of her thighs as he spoke. Blossom squeezed them around his neck with a pleased hum, thoroughly enjoying the support.
Ayame followed the movement of his fingers before exchanging an extremely wry look with Serika.
"I can see how seriously you're taking it, Quin."
"As I should. It's my responsibility to keep her from falling."
He gave Blossom's thighs an affectionate squeeze, quite comfortable beneath their scrutiny.

The long coil of rope Sera selected cost eighteen bits. Beside it went the carrying slings, wrapped food for the road, spare cloth, and boxes for samples. Aurora checked the fastenings while Kaelira chose a padded box for Edric's armguard.
With the lantern included, their purchases came to three crowns and twenty bits.
Quinlan paid four crowns from the expedition purse and received eighty bits in change.
For little more than the reward on that leaf-gathering notice, they had bought everything piled before them, including an enchanted lantern.
While Kaelira packed the armguard, Aurora checked the purchases against her list.
"Could you recommend an apothecary? We'd like to look at antivenom."
"Across the street, green door. She supplies most of the parties who shop here."
At the apothecary across the street, Black Fang passed the shelves of healing draughts and stopped beside Aurora as she asked about antivenom.
Quinlan joined them as Blossom tucked her empty pastry bag away.

The apothecary was a female kobold with mottled reddish-brown scales and a short draconic snout. She stood on a raised wooden platform behind the counter, putting the rows of sealed bottles within easy reach of her clawed hands.
"Do you know which venom you need protection against?" the kobold asked.
"Possibly some spider monster's venom. We haven't identified them yet," Aurora explained.
The apothecary reached for a squat bottle with a green seal.
"Then I'd take a general antivenom. This covers the common venomous spiders around Sarthal, along with several biting insects. One crown a dose."
Black Fang read the label while Aurora took the bottle. Quinlan watched his alchemist rotate it beneath the light, already intent on the liquid inside.
"Does it neutralize the venom, or suppress the symptoms?" Black Fang asked.
"Neutralizes what it's formulated for. With something stronger, it may only slow the effects. I wouldn't promise more without knowing what you're facing."
"May I examine a sample?" Aurora asked.

The kobold brought out an open vial, holding it between the pads of her fingers with her claws clear of the rim. Aurora wafted its scent toward herself, then tilted the glass to watch the liquid coat its sides.
"Hmm... You've thickened it to keep the mixture stable in storage?"
"Yes. Most of my customers want something they can leave in a pack."
"Sensible. Though it won't act as quickly."
The apothecary's gaze returned to Aurora's face.
"You brew?"
"I do."
Quinlan watched his alchemist smile pleasantly, entirely failing to mention the rather outrageous things she brewed. Beside her, Black Fang accepted the sample and held it beneath her nose.
<Adequate for ordinary venom,> the assassin assessed.
<And for yours?> Quinlan asked.
The side glance Black Fang gave him was one of extreme personal insult.
He chuckled beneath his helmet. Fair enough.
Aurora had returned to the label. She traced an ingredient's name with her fingertip, then pointed it out to the seller.
"Could I see this separately?"
The kobold opened a shallow drawer beneath the bottles and offered her a dried leaf. Aurora rubbed its edge between her fingers, studying the powder it left on her skin.
"We buy it from growers inland," the apothecary explained. "Fresh is stronger. Dried travels better."
Aurora held the leaf beneath Black Fang's nose. The assassin inspected it without touching her hand, then glanced at the drawer.
<That is worth examining.>
<Oh? More interesting than the finished product?> Quinlan asked.
<Considerably. This woman is a mediocre Alchemist, but the ingredients are new to me.>

Aurora smiled down at the leaf. <I'd like to try it in my own preparation. I could probably brew a faster-acting batch for tomorrow, especially if you open a gate to my parents' apothecary for me tonight.>
"We'll take one dose," she told the seller, setting the leaf beside them. "And could you spare this for me to study? I'd also like to know how you dry it."
"You can have the leaf with the purchase. I'll write down the drying instructions for you. The full recipe costs extra."
"Of course." Aurora laughed. "I'm very protective of mine too."
The apothecary glanced at the single bottle.
"If you're planning to recreate it yourself, I'd recommend buying more. It's a difficult recipe I spent decades mastering."
Aurora's smile turned sly as she drew the bottle toward herself.
"Then if I fail, I'll be back for more."

"Hm. I like the attitude. But I might charge you more should that be the case." The apothecary drew a sheet of paper toward herself, warming to the conversation. As she wrote, she explained that the seal preserved the preparation; once opened, a dose should be used rather than saved for another trip.

Aurora listened with the leaf resting on her palm. Her eyes kept returning to it, and Quinlan found himself quite content. He liked seeing his women enjoy what they were good at, even when he only understood half of what fascinated them.
Celia came to the counter while the apothecary finished writing. Her eyes moved between Aurora and Black Fang before settling on the bottle.
"Will that be enough?"
"For me to study, yes," Aurora answered. "We have our own supplies as well, but until we know what we're dealing with, I can't tell you which remedy we'll need."
Celia looked down at the bottle again.
"I understand. Thank you for checking."
Quinlan paid one crown, leaving ten crowns and eighty bits of their allowance. Outside, they confirmed that they would meet at Celia's house in the morning.
Blossom leaned forward over his head, her blonde hair spilling across his visor.
"Master?"
"Yes?"
"Blossom found something noteworthy while scouting."
He followed her pointing finger to another stall, where skewers of meat sizzled over a brazier.
"So she has. Good girl."
And with that, it was time to set out on the expedition!

"For me to study, yes," Aurora answered.
"We have our own supplies as well, but until we know what we're dealing with, I can't tell you which remedy we'll need."
Celia looked down at the bottle again.
"I understand.
Thank you for checking."
Quinlan paid one crown, leaving ten crowns and eighty bits of their allowance.
Outside, they confirmed that they would meet at Celia's house in the morning.
Blossom leaned forward over his head, her blonde hair spilling across his visor.
"Master?"
"Yes?"
"Blossom found something noteworthy while scouting."
He followed her pointing finger to another stall, where skewers of meat sizzled over a brazier.
"So she has.
Good girl."
And with that, it was time to set out on the expedition!

chapters.title: Chapter 1982 Into the Wilderness
paragraphs: Quinlan left Sarthal through its southern gate the following morning, with Celia walking beside Serika and Marielle's new blue robe fluttering ahead of them.

The mage had arrived at Celia's house wearing it. She'd been wearing it when the neighbour wished them a safe journey, when the guards checked their contract, and when a passing woman complimented the embroidery.
That last encounter had delayed their departure considerably.
"A lovely piece, isn't it?" Marielle lifted her sleeve as they passed beyond the gate's shadow. "The temperature adjusts beneath my travelling clothes too. I barely felt the morning chill."
Kaelira glanced at Quinlan.
He could see the smith fighting a smile. She'd put a great deal of care into those tiny runes, and having someone appreciate the work was clearly pleasing her, even when that someone was a dumb cunt.
"I'm glad you like it," he said.
"I do. You should tell its maker that they have excellent taste."
"I'll be sure to pass it on."
Marielle smoothed the pale fabric over her hips before looking at Lucille.
"It really is a shame you never got to wear it."
"You seem to be enjoying it enough for both of us, dear."
"Well, someone should. There's no sense leaving a thing like this in a box."
She turned away with a satisfied little smile. Beside Quinlan, Lucille slipped her hand through his arm and squeezed hard enough for him to feel it through his armour.
<What a gem she is.>
<I'm enchanted.> He chuckled as the road carried them between low field walls. Ahead, the southern hills rose beyond strips of cultivated land, their exposed slopes broken by dark stands of trees.

Celia had her bow on her back and a much smaller pack than she'd had yesterday. The enchanted lantern hung from its side, where she kept checking the fastening Kaelira had adjusted for her that morning.
"Does it pull?" Serika asked.
"No. It's much better. Thank you."
"Good. Tell me if that changes."
"If we're finished discussing straps," Marielle said, "perhaps we can establish how this expedition will proceed. Yesterday gave me certain concerns."
Quinlan looked toward her.
"Did it?"
"I accepted responsibility for your party. That means when I tell you something, I expect you to listen. We cannot stop for a debate every time one of your women has a different idea."
Marielle slowed until she was walking beside him, obliging Lucille to move around a puddle at the road's edge.
"We're going into dangerous ruins, Adventurer Black. This isn't an outing for you and your girlfriends."
"Wives," Vex corrected pleasantly from his other side.
"How fortunate for you. Perhaps you could remember you're adventurers as well."
Quinlan rested his hand over Lucille's where it held his arm.
"We're here to investigate what happened to Celia's father. If one of my wives notices something useful, I intend to listen."
"And if I tell you it's irrelevant?"
"Then I will ignore you."
Andre exhaled through his nose. "Oh, Goddess..."
Marielle's gaze flicked toward her husband before returning to the black helmet.
"No, you won't. I won't let you."
"Okay."
Kitsara coughed into her hand. Marielle looked at the foxkin, whose innocent expression survived for the entire length of the inspection.
"We'll see how talkative you are when something tries to eat you."
She strode ahead to join Andre. Quinlan watched the embroidered hem sweep above the dust without catching in it.
<The clearance is good,> Kaelira told him.
<Beautiful work.>
<Thank you... You too.>
The shy pleasure in her voice made him smile beneath his helmet. He reached back, and she placed her hand in his for a brief squeeze before Celia asked her about the lantern's shutter.
They left the fields behind as the road began climbing. Andre took out the map where it divided around a rocky ridge, checking the faded marker set beside the narrower path.
"This way. The old survey road."
Blossom sniffed the air beyond his shoulder.
"There are spiders ahead."
"How many?" Serika asked her.
"Blossom can't tell yet. The wind keeps changing."
Marielle tapped her staff against the marker.
"Then perhaps you could tell us something useful when it stops."
Blossom's ears dipped. Quinlan turned his helmet toward the mage.
"A warning about what we're walking toward seems useful to me."
"We already knew to expect spiders."
"Now we know they're ahead."
"Wonderful. Shall I pet her?"
"Not if you want to keep your hand."
His voice had lost its amusement. Marielle met his stare for a moment, then turned toward the path Andre had chosen.
"Fine. Keep your scout ahead of us, then. Somewhere she can do her job."
Blossom looked up at Quinlan. He brushed his fingers over one blonde ear.
"Ignore this miserable wench."
"Excuse me?!" Marielle stomped, shrieking gutturally.
"Of course, Master!"
Blossom hurried ahead, her tail already lifting again. Marielle watched her go before giving Quinlan another appraising look.
"What level are you, anyway?"
"Who knows?"
Marielle stopped walking, forcing Andre to turn back toward her.
"You don't know your own level?"
Quinlan passed her without answering. Lucille stayed on his arm, stepping over a root while Marielle hurried to catch up.
"Oh, don't tell me you're embarrassed."
He glanced at her, then returned his attention to the path.
"Goddess preserve me..." She pressed her fingers to the circlet. "And here I thought you were experienced fighters who had neglected their Guild records. Which of you is the strongest?"
Her gaze settled on Black Fang, who continued studying the wooded slope.
"Did you hear me? You, black hair. I'm talking to you."
Marielle waited for the assassin to turn toward her. When Black Fang kept walking, the mage looked at Andre with her mouth hanging open.
"We accepted an entire nursery, and they think they can be rude to us."
"Marielle," he muttered.
"What? We're both approaching a hundred! They're Grade One and too ashamed to admit their levels!"
Her eyes returned to Quinlan's armour, then travelled over the women's equipment as she touched the circlet again. She smiled as she supplied the explanation none of them had offered her.
"Damned rich weaklings."
No one replied, so she kept going.
"Money won't make up for experience down there. You'd do well to remember that."
Quinlan watched Blossom bound over a fallen branch ahead of them. Beside him, Lucille's fingers tightened around his arm again.
This time, she was trying not to laugh.
By midday, the path had brought them to a stream beneath an overhang. Celia recognized the place from her notes and hurried ahead to check the dry ground beside it.
"We can stop here! There's room to sit, and... Oh, the hearth's still here too."
She pointed at a ring of blackened stones, then looked hopefully toward Quinlan.
"Could I have my things, please?"
He returned her cookware from his pocket ring. She caught the pot by both handles, still looking faintly astonished at how easily it appeared, then knelt beside the hearth.
"I can have something ready while you rest."
"We're stopping already?" Marielle asked.
"We've been walking all morning," Serika replied. She stretched her arms above her head before settling on a dry rock. "I could eat."
Blossom appeared beside Celia with a bundle of fallen twigs.
"Blossom can help!"
"Thank you! Could you put those here?"

Within minutes, Celia had a fire crackling beneath the pot. She sliced dried meat into the water, added vegetables from her pack, and crumbled herbs between her fingers while the broth began to steam.
Quinlan sat against the overhang with Ayame leaning on his shoulder. The samurai had closed her eyes, enjoying the shade, while Kitsara complained to Vex about burrs in her tails.
"That's because you keep dragging them through the bushes."
"I have five, you heartless woman. Where would you like me to put them? Up my butt?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1983 Spiders
paragraphs: "You could try."
Kitsara's ears lifted with interest.
Across the stream, their expedition leader was inspecting her reflection in the still water. She touched the circlet, adjusted a curl, then came back to find Celia laying out bowls on a clean cloth.
"Mine without those leaves."
The girl paused with the ladle in her hand.
"I'm sorry, they're already in the broth."
"Then pick them out."
Celia reached for a spoon, but Lucille caught the bowl before she could begin fishing through it.
"I'll have that one, sweetheart. It smells lovely."
"Thank you..."
"I'm sure Marielle can manage the leaves in hers."
"I didn't ask you."
Lucille smiled at the mage over the steaming bowl.
"I heard you perfectly."
Celia brought Quinlan his portion. She had tucked a slice of bread against the bowl's rim and wrapped a cloth beneath it so he could take it without burning his fingers.
His gauntlets made the precaution entirely unnecessary, but he appreciated it anyway.
"Thank you."
He turned toward the overhang before lifting his visor, keeping his face out of the others' view. Kaelira settled beside his free shoulder with her own bowl.
Across the fire, Marielle leaned to peer around the smith. Kaelira shifted closer to Quinlan, neatly blocking the gap.
The mage leaned the other way.
Kaelira turned her back fully toward her and raised her spoon, leaving Marielle staring at her armour.
<This bitch is getting old.>
<Patience. Just a bit more.>
<Yeah...>
"It's only simple food," Celia said. "I wasn't sure what you liked, so I..."
Blossom made a delighted sound around her first mouthful.
Celia turned toward her so quickly that the ladle knocked against her hip.
"Is it alright?"
"It's really good!"
The relief on the girl's face made Quinlan take a spoonful. The broth was hot and savoury, with enough softened vegetables to make a proper meal of it.
"She's right."
Celia stood a little straighter. "There's more if you'd like it."
"Blossom would!"
"After everyone has some," Ayame told the dogkin, opening one eye.
"Blossom knows! She's reserving her place!"
Even Andre smiled at that. Marielle ate her portion with the offending leaves arranged along one side of the bowl.

Quinlan lowered his visor before handing his empty bowl back to Celia. She added it to the other dishes and scrubbed them downstream from where she'd drawn the cooking water. She washed the pot, dried its handles, then spread the cloths over a sunlit stone.
Serika glanced at the girl's untouched bowl.
"Celia. Your lunch is getting cold."
"I'll just finish-"
"Could you eat first? We're resting too."
The girl looked from her to the waiting bowl, then finally sat beside her with a bashful smile.

After eating, Celia wiped the mud from the lantern's casing and cleaned the grit out of its fastening. She offered the damp cloth to Kaelira, who was checking the straps of her armour, then helped brush the road dust from the buckles where it had gathered.
Quinlan watched her pack everything only after it had dried. She had fed them, cleaned up, and was already checking that nothing would rattle loose on the next climb.
"You were worried about earning your place," he told her as he stored the cookware again. "How do you think you're doing?"
Celia glanced at the empty pot just before it vanished.
"I... I hope well?"
"Very well."
Her smile stayed with her when they returned to the road.
The first spider came out of a cleft beside the survey road, dragging a web-bound animal behind it.
"There!" Blossom called.
Andre brought his shield forward as the creature dropped its meal. Its body was as broad as the path, with hooked forelegs that scraped sparks off the exposed rock.
More legs unfolded in the cleft behind it.
Celia fumbled for an arrow. Serika caught her wrist before she could draw across Lucille's back and guided her toward the clear ground behind them.
"From here. You need room for the bow."
Marielle was already chanting.
"[Shield Reinforcement]!" Andre called, bracing as a silver sheen spread over the metal on his arm.
The spider struck his reinforced shield with a crash that sent loose gravel skipping around his boots. He drove it upward and forced the hooked legs apart.
"Now!"
"[Fireball]!"
Marielle thrust her staff forward, sending the spell through the opening he'd made.

The creature shrieked as Marielle's spell burst beneath its raised body. Flame poured from the cleft behind it, and the shapes crowding the entrance convulsed against one another before dropping out of sight.
Andre shoved the burning carcass off the road.
"Anything else?" he asked Blossom.
She sniffed, then pointed toward a crack above the cleft.
"One went up there."
Marielle followed Blossom's finger with her staff, already speaking the next incantation.
"[Flame Lance]!"
A narrow shaft of fire pierced the spider before it could pull its abdomen through. Its burning remains tumbled down the slope, bouncing past Celia's drawn arrow.
"There," the mage said, lowering her staff. "That's how we keep an expedition moving."
She looked directly at Quinlan.
"You may put your weapons away."
He glanced at his empty hands.
"Perhaps now you'll take this seriously," Marielle muttered, then touched the circlet's cooling rune while Andre checked his shield.
The blue robe stirred around her legs as she passed the scorched cleft, careful to lift its hem despite the fabric already clearing the ground.

Quinlan crouched beside the dead spider. The fire had entered through the softer underside, leaving the upper shell intact. He pressed a thumb against one of its ridges while Aurora studied the fangs.
<They work pretty well together,> Serika observed. <At least considering.>
<Both approaching a hundred,> Ayame replied. <I'd be embarrassed to boast about killing these.>
Their timing was good, but Quinlan had seen nothing to justify her smugness.
"Black?" Marielle called from farther up the road. "Are you coming, or do you need me to explain which feet should be placed where?"
Aurora held a sample vial beneath one fang while Black Fang pressed the venom sac through the split mouthparts.
"We have antivenom," Marielle said.
"A mediocre one."
"Yes, and I'd like to reach the ruins before nightfall."
Aurora stoppered the vial and stood. "Then you can run ahead."
"What?! I can't believe this! I'll have so much to tell the guild when I get back..." Marielle growled as she stomped ahead.
Quinlan waited beside Aurora until she'd packed the vial away, then rose and brushed the dust off his gauntlet. Behind Marielle, Andre had unfolded the map again.
The survey road ended at a hillside split by an old stone arch. Broken paving descended beyond it into darkness, with pale threads stretched between the weathered blocks.
Celia stepped past Quinlan to look inside.
"This is where they went."
Her hand closed around the strap of her father's expedition notes. Seraphiel stopped beside her while Kaelira opened the lantern's shutter.
Its light reached a flight of worn steps and a torn leather glove caught in the webbing below.

Andre spread the map against the arch while Celia found the matching page in her notes. The underground route continued across several sheets, with passages branching away into blank spaces at their edges.
"How far does this go?" Serika asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 1984 Entering the Depths
paragraphs: "Nobody marked an end," Andre replied. "These are the surveyed sections. Some join up, some stop where the surveyors stopped."
Celia looked down at the pages.
"That's why I brought so many supplies. If we have to search the branches, we might need to sleep down there."

Quinlan studied the lines descending beyond the last marked junction. Reaching the entrance had been the easy part. The missing expedition could have taken any of those routes, and they had yet to find a trail to follow.
"Could you keep close to me?" Sera asked Celia.
The girl nodded to her. Andre went down first with Marielle behind him, and Celia followed between Sera and Serika.

The stairway opened into a corridor whose walls had been cut square long before the hillside swallowed them. Water ran down one side, leaving the other dry enough for the old expedition's chalk marks to survive.
Andre checked each mark against his map. At a collapsed junction, he pointed out the turn the surveyors had used to bypass it.
"The lower galleries join up beyond here."
"Assuming they still do," Kaelira said. She angled the lantern toward a split in the ceiling. "That block has moved since someone marked this wall."
Marielle glanced up.
"Then we'll avoid standing under it."
"I'd suggest passing one at a time. The slab beside it is carrying the weight now."
"Andre first. The rest of you follow him."
She waited beside the junction while they crossed separately, then gave Quinlan an impatient look when he paused to study the damaged stone.
"Your smith has already inspected it."
"I like to learn from her. I'm studying what she saw."
Kaelira nearly bumped into Sera ahead of her. The healer caught her elbow, giggling, while Marielle looked at Quinlan as though he had just drooled on himself.
"You really are hopeless."

Beyond the collapse, the worked corridor ended at a shaft whose bottom lay beyond the lantern's reach. Worn steps wound down its inner wall, interrupted where slabs had broken away from their supports.
Andre tested the first landing before waving the others after him. Serika stayed beside Celia on the descent, offering her hand wherever the girl had to step across a gap.
Water dripped somewhere beneath them. The sound followed Quinlan down until they reached a lower arch, where Blossom paused with her nose raised.
"Master, the smell goes this way."
"The map says left," Marielle replied.
Blossom pointed through the arch to their right. A broken pack buckle lay beside a dark smear on the paving.
Andre crouched to examine it, then checked the next sheet.
"This joins the lower survey route. We can follow it."
Marielle folded her arms and scoffed while he marked their turn. Celia watched him add the arrow before putting her own papers away, careful to keep the pages dry.

They descended through another flight of galleries, stopping where fallen masonry forced them to crawl beneath a leaning beam. Quinlan waited while Celia passed her pack through to Serika, then followed her into a passage whose walls had vanished under sheets of silk.
By late afternoon, they had been underground for hours. At the next dry landing, Celia passed around bread and water while Andre compared the route they'd taken with the surveyors' marks.
The papers showed more junctions below them. Blossom kept finding scraps caught in the webbing: a torn strap, a strip of cloth, then the rusted head of a broken pick.
With that trail to guide them, they continued down.

The next sloping passage opened into a broad gallery with empty doorways along both sides. Webbing hung in sheets across the openings, thickening toward the far end until the lantern couldn't shine through it.
Blossom stopped sniffing.
"Master. There are people."
Celia lifted her head.
"Alive?"
"Blossom can smell blood. And..." Her ears turned toward the nearest doorway. "Someone's breathing."
Quinlan heard it when they stopped moving: a faint, wet drag of air behind the silk.
Marielle raised her staff, but Aurora caught her attention with an upraised palm.
"There might be someone directly behind it."
"I wasn't going to burn the whole room down."
"..." Aurora elected to say nothing.
Andre slit the sheet with his sword. The cut exposed a long chamber crowded with bundles suspended from the ceiling.
Something moved inside the nearest one.
Celia took a step toward it, then stopped when Sera touched her shoulder.
"Let me look first."

Serika guided Celia inside behind the others, keeping her near the back of the chamber while Lucille and Kaelira watched the doorway. Quinlan stayed beside Seraphiel; Marielle and Andre remained out in the gallery.
"[Divine Arsenal]," Seraphiel murmured.
She drew the spell's light into a blade and opened the outer wrapping. A woman's face emerged beneath strands of dirty hair, her eyes closed and her lips parted around a thread of saliva.
She was breathing.
"Oh, thank the Goddess..." Celia whispered.
Sera cut farther down the cocoon. The woman's arm slipped out, ending in a healed stump above the wrist.
Celia's hand rose to her mouth.
Above the stump, fresh punctures marked the exposed skin. A thin, hollow strand remained embedded near the elbow, running from her arm into a knotted mass of silk on the wall.
Dark fluid moved through it.
Aurora leaned close without touching the strand.
"Sera, wait. Something's feeding through that."
Quinlan followed the tube with his eyes. Smaller bodies stirred inside the wall's silken pockets, their legs pressing against the translucent covering as the fluid reached them.
From behind Serika, Celia made a strangled sound.
"They're eating them?"
Sera lowered the woman's weight carefully into the opened wrapping while she examined the tube. Before she could answer, a heavy scrape rolled down the gallery.
Blossom's ears snapped toward the sound.
"Master. Something powerful is coming."
The webbing over the far arch tightened. Dust trickled from its upper stones as a hooked leg pushed through, feeling along the floor with a tip longer than Andre's sword.
He raised his shield and backed toward Marielle.
"Something very big," he said hoarsely.
Another leg drove into the paving. Cracks spread beneath it, and the impact shook the hanging cocoons against one another.
Celia clutched Serika's arm. From the back of the room, she could see the doorway framing those enormous limbs, could hear the wet clicking coming from somewhere above them.
"That's what got Father...?"
Serika drew her behind her shoulder as the creature forced its forebody through the arch.

Armour grated against masonry. The monster folded her legs tightly along her flanks, scraping furrows into both walls as she dragged herself forward. Her swollen black abdomen remained wedged beyond the opening, pulsing beneath coarse hairs tangled with webbing.
Marielle's staff dipped.
"That can't... Andre, the ones outside weren't... Just what level is this monster?!"
"I don't fucking know, but this is way beyond us!"
He caught her sleeve and pulled her back as a foreleg stabbed into the place where she'd been standing. Chips of paving struck her boots.
"Away from the walls!"
The queen monster lowered her head between them.
Red eyes crowded the ridged plates above her fangs. As the lantern beam crossed them, they turned together toward the open feeding chamber, tracking Sera's hands on the captive.
Quinlan's women spread out inside the chamber, leaving each other room to fight. Ayame's thumb eased her katana free of its sheath, while Lucille lifted her hammer beside Kaelira at the door.
Kitsara's tails pulled tight against her legs.
"Oh, fuck that."

chapters.title: Chapter 1985 Terror
paragraphs: The queen's fangs opened wide enough to take Andre's shield between them. A wad of chewed leather fell from the joint of her mouth and struck the floor beside his foot.
He recoiled from it, catching sight of the boot buckle still attached.
Quinlan closed his hand around [Soul Reaper]'s hilt. The little spiders on the road had given him no idea there would be a thing like this waiting below them.
Wet folds worked inside a slit behind the queen's fangs. Her clicking slowed, grinding around the sound that forced its way out.
"Mine."
Marielle stared at the moving slit.
"It talks?"
The queen struck the doorway with her foreleg. Kaelira pulled back as the hooked tip gouged through the jamb, ripping out a block where her head had been.
"Mine!"
Her shriek sent the smaller bodies inside the feeding pockets scrambling over one another. Outside, legs began rattling against the gallery walls from both directions.
Blossom turned toward the way they'd come.
"More behind us!"
"[Protective Shield]!"

Aurora planted her staff on the paving, raising a barrier across the chamber entrance as the spiders outside sent silk lashing through the gallery. Threads slapped against its surface, trembling under the weight of things climbing along them.
The queen caught the webbing beneath her forelegs and wrenched it toward herself.
Inside the chamber, the strands joining the feeding sacs snapped taut. Swollen knots behind the captives squeezed shut, spraying a yellowish mist between the hanging bodies.
A bitter smell caught in Quinlan's nose.
"Cover your mouths!" Aurora shouted.
Serika covered her own mouth, then caught Celia around the waist as the girl began coughing and lost her grip on the brawler's arm.
"[Gust]."
Quinlan gathered the mist into a tight, spinning current above their heads. Aurora opened a gap at the top of her barrier, and he drove the poisoned air over the couple and into the queen's face.
Aurora closed the gap and repeated her incantation, sealing the leaking sacs beneath separate shells of ice-packed light.
Celia went limp in Serika's arms, unconscious from the mist she'd breathed in. Serika lowered her to the paving, supporting her head. "It's better if she sleeps for this one."
"Yep." Sera came over and crouched beside Celia to check her breathing. "She'll live."
Keeping her light blade in hand, the elf turned back toward the doorway. Quinlan hadn't taken his eyes off the queen.
The creature was dragging her fangs across Aurora's barrier, making the light ripple beneath their points.
"Sssleep..."
The word rasped between bursts of clicking. Drool threaded from her mouth as she stretched toward the limp girl behind the fighters.
Marielle's chant rose to a scream as she levelled her staff at the queen.
"[Greater Fireball]!"
Fire slammed into the queen's face, filling the gallery with a roar. Andre hauled his wife clear of the billowing heat while she kept her staff raised, staring into the flames.
"Burn, you disgusting freak! Killing you will become my legend!"
The queen thrust her head out through the fire.
"Fuck! Andre!! Hurry, do something!"
Andre threw himself sideways with Marielle as her fangs snapped shut where they'd been standing. A charred sheet of silk fell from the creature's unmarked face.
Marielle hit the floor hard enough to knock the breath out of her.
"It didn't... My spell didn't..."
Andre dragged her upright. She had poured enough mana into that cast to burn through the creatures on the road, and the queen hadn't even lost an eye.
It was still reaching for them.
Behind Marielle, something heavy struck Aurora's barrier.

Andre wheeled toward the sound from his place beside Marielle in the gallery. A spider twice the size of the creatures on the road clung to the wall by the chamber entrance, dragging a hooked leg across Aurora's shield of light.
"Back into the chamber!" he shouted.
"[Shield Reinforcement]!"
Andre met the spider's strike with his shield. Its silver sheen shattered beneath the hooked leg, and the metal folded around it.
Andre screamed as the impact drove him to one knee. His sword scraped across the creature's shell, carving a shallow white line.
"[Flame Lance]!" Marielle cried, driving another spell into its open mouth.
This spider kept coming.
"Move!" Andre roared at his wife.
He dragged his ruined shield sideways, taking the leg with it long enough for her to stumble clear. The spider tore the metal from his arm and flung it down the gallery.
Quinlan drew his saber as Aurora opened a gap for Kaelira to step into the doorway.
"[Runeweaver's Armory]."
Runes shone across the smith's armour as her spell reinforced it. Her shoulder caught Andre and shoved him behind her, while her weapon knocked the descending hook away from Marielle's head.
"Inside," the smith said through clenched teeth.
The couple scrambled past her. Aurora's barrier closed across the entrance, and the giant spider struck it hard enough to shake dust from the ceiling.
Marielle stared at the hooked limb pressed against the shield of light.
"What the fuck is that thing?"
"Hers," Andre panted.
More bodies moved outside. The scrape of their legs filled the gallery, with deeper impacts travelling through the floor as the queen shifted her weight.
Marielle turned toward the chamber's rear wall. She ran her fingers across the blocks, searching for an opening, then looked at the narrow doorway crowded with hungry eyes.
The room had only one doorway. Andre's map offered no second exit, and the creature that had destroyed his shield was standing between them and the stairs.
"We have to break through," she said.
Across the room, Marielle was chanting again. The head of her staff shook as she forced more mana into it, filling the chamber with an orange glare.
"Drop the barrier when I say!"
"There could be people in those other rooms," Aurora replied.
"Who cares? We're about to die!"
Her voice broke on the last word. She looked at Andre, waiting for him to deny it, but her husband was struggling to lift the arm that had held his shield.
The queen lowered her mouth toward the doorway again, her fangs scraping down its broken edges.
"That one..."
The slit behind her fangs worked around a grinding hiss.
"Mouth first."
Marielle's spell faltered.
The creature was looking straight at her.
"Tasty...."
Its mouthparts opened, strands of saliva stretching between the plates, and she could see scraps of cloth caught among the teeth.
Her precious robe brushed the backs of her legs. She clutched the staff against her chest and backed into the wall, unable to look away from the mouth that had chosen her.
She was going to be wrapped up in this room. Those little things would drink from her while she waited for something larger to get hungry.
"Andre..."
He stepped in front of her with his sword in his good hand.
Quinlan glanced at Aurora's barrier, then at the women gathered around him.
"Well, girls. It's been fun, but I'm kinda done pretending. Shall we take the masks off?"
"What the fuck are you talking about, you sad delirious fuck?!" Marielle screamed.
Ayame drew her katana with a smile that showed her teeth.
"Finally."
Quinlan walked past the couple toward the doorway, [Soul Reaper] hovering at his side. Aurora parted the centre of her barrier as he reached the threshold, keeping the rest of the entrance shielded.
The queen's eyes followed him.
Her mouth opened, strings of drool stretching between the fangs as she lowered her head toward the gap. The clicking quickened until it rattled against his helmet.
"Come... closer."
"Sure." He took another step.
Her foreleg struck through the opening with enough force to rip the remaining stone lintel from the wall.
"This fucking retard is going to kill us all!" Marielle screamed as the hooked tip plunged toward his chest.
Quinlan lifted his free hand, raising rock from the gallery floor beneath the descending limb.
The queen smashed through its upper edge, spraying broken slabs against Aurora's barrier, but the rest closed around her leg and stopped the hook just short of his armour.
She drove her weight against it.
The paving buckled beneath her supporting limbs. A crack split the gallery wall from floor to ceiling as she tried to force the trapped hook forward, close enough to scrape black metal.
Quinlan watched her strain, then slowly raised his head.
"What an adorable little spider you are."
His red eyes blazed through the helmet's narrow openings, casting crimson light across the wet plates of her face.
The queen met his gaze and shuddered.

chapters.title: Chapter 1986 Bad Girl
paragraphs: The spider monster shuddered in the ruined gallery, her hooked foreleg still trapped in the stone Quinlan held around it. When she tried to wrench the hook away from his chest, he tightened his fingers.
Chitin cracked inside the rock, and dark fluid squirted through the fracture onto his gauntlet.
*SKRIIIIEEEEE!*
The queen's shriek struck the gallery walls hard enough to make Marielle clap a hand over her ear.
The harder the queen pulled, the more she widened her own wound, and Quinlan enjoyed every wet crunch. She'd been so eager to put that thing through him a moment ago.
"Leaving already?"
Fear drove her backward into the arch. Her swollen abdomen scraped against the masonry while her trapped limb stretched between them, its exposed flesh coming apart under the strain.
The queen raised her head to shriek into the passages behind her, the piercing, sustained call setting the webs trembling along the gallery.
*KRRRIIIEEEEEEEEE!*
An answering cry rose from somewhere far below, followed by others through the walls. Soon they overlapped so thickly that Andre could no longer tell which direction they were coming from.
"She's calling them," he gasped. "Her minions..."
*KRRRIIIEEE! KRRRIIIEEE!*
The queen repeated the summons, pulling frantically against Quinlan's grip. He could feel the vibrations through the stone around her leg as something began moving in the depths.
From behind Quinlan's shoulder, Marielle stared at the huge body that had filled the gallery and driven them into a corner. The monster had reached in to choose which of them it would eat first.
Now it was trying to get away from a Grade One nobody.
The queen lowered her head toward Quinlan again, stopping well beyond the reach of his free hand. Crimson light from his visor shone across the saliva stretched between her fangs.
Between the rattling mouthparts, the wet slit opened in an attempt at speech. A shift of Quinlan's fingers against the stone holding her leg broke it into a rasp.
"Wh-what..."

Even with her leg torn open, the terrified creature kept drawing back, dragging on the trapped limb in her desperation to escape. Quinlan made no attempt to hide his pleasure as he watched fear drive her to hurt herself further.
Her clustered eyes stayed fixed on the red glow beneath his helmet as she forced the rest through her trembling mouth.
"What... are you...? Human...? No..."
"Just a humble adventurer," Quinlan replied as he released the crushed limb, letting her stumble back.
He drove his will through the surrounding stone. "I'm quite curious about you as well. So be a good girl and sit."
The queen thrust her head forward, snapping her fangs shut in front of his helmet.
"I... am queen!"
Fury drove her good foreleg into the gallery wall. The hook tore through a supporting block, sending broken masonry crashing against Aurora's shield as the monster forced herself higher over him.
"You sit! In silk! I eat you... slowly!"

Andre drew his wife behind his good shoulder as the masonry fell. Her strongest fire spell hadn't left a wound on that face, yet here the creature was, ripping apart stonework his sword wouldn't have scratched.
Black stood beneath her open fangs, apparently waiting for her to finish her tantrum.
"We'll work on that," he mused.
Once back through the doorway with his family, Quinlan pushed the feeding chamber's ceiling higher into the hillside. The floor rose beneath them at his will, carrying everyone above the gallery.
"No spell casting?! Again?!" Marielle grabbed Andre as the paving rose under her boots. "How is he-"

The giant spider that had crushed Andre's shield tried to climb after them, only for Quinlan to trap it between the rising floor's outer edge and the gallery ceiling. Its shell crumpled while its legs battered Aurora's barrier.
Its mouth kept working through the first impact, so he pushed again.
*KRRUNCH!*
Black pulp jetted out between the stones. One severed leg struck the queen across her eyes, and she recoiled with a furious hiss while Quinlan opened the neighbouring feeding rooms below them.
"Sera, could you cut them free?"
"Working on it! Kaelira, there's another behind that one!"
Quinlan brought the neighbouring captives up to them on broad slabs of their rooms' floors. As Sera cut the anchoring webs, Kaelira caught each cocoon and laid it beside the unconscious Celia.
Under the noise of breaking masonry, the answering cries grew louder. Loose threads twitched across the floor as the approaching brood shook the silk stretched through the passages below.
Blossom turned her ears toward the sound.
"Master, they're coming from everywhere!"

Aurora extended her shield across the opening while Quinlan joined the emptied slabs to the party's floor. They now stood on a wide balcony recessed into the rock, with a solid ceiling overhead and the queen in the gallery below.
Sera and Aurora stayed with Celia and the rescued captives at the back. Marielle and Andre huddled beside them, watching through the barrier as Kaelira returned to the balcony's front edge.
Below them, the queen stabbed her feet into the paving.
"Mine!"

The queen's tug on a trailing strand sent one cocoon sliding toward the balcony's edge. Kaelira caught the bundle against her chest before it could fall, while Quinlan ripped the gallery floor apart beneath the grasping monster.
*SKREEEEEE!*
Her shriek swallowed the noise of snapping webs as she plunged, catching herself with her legs braced against both walls. When Quinlan peeled those away too, the queen scrabbled backward.
"As my Pupcake will attest to, bad girls deserve to be punished." He shook his head in disappointment, then stepped off the balcony into a current of his own wind.
"S-silence..!!"
The queen hauled herself through the arch at the gallery's far end, retreating into the cavern beyond.
Quinlan floated after her, tearing away the arch and the rock above it to open a clear view from the balcony into the nest.

The cavern floor lay far below them, sloping toward tunnel mouths at the foot of the opposite wall. Web bridges crossed the open space overhead, with egg sacs hanging beneath them and human feeding bundles packed onto ledges along both sides.

The queen climbed the wall to the balcony's right, digging her hooks into the rock until her head rose level with Quinlan. He hovered out over the hollow, keeping himself between her and the people behind Aurora's shield.
"Oh. Your babies are here."
Spiders poured from every opening he could see.

The first streams spread along the walls until they met, then climbed over one another as those behind kept pushing. Bridges sagged beneath the gathering weight. Far below, fallen bodies vanished beneath the brood racing across the floor.

To Marielle, staring past Quinlan into the depths, there seemed to be no end to them. Each time she thought the flow must be ending, another passage disgorged more monsters. The smaller ones crawled between the giants' legs, and even those giants were emerging in packed ranks.

Thousands had already filled the hollow, with thousands more forcing their way in behind them. Tens of thousands were answering their queen, and the thunder of their legs drowned out Andre when he tried to speak.
At Andre's pull, Marielle retreated from the edge without taking her eyes off the nearest bridge. Spiders were spilling over both sides, catching themselves on strands below.

Among them were the ridged shells Andre recognized all too well. One creature like that had folded his reinforced shield around his arm, barely taking a scratch from his sword in return. Now they were climbing out shoulder to shoulder, with larger ones pushing through behind them.
"Those aren't little hatchlings," he said hoarsely. "The big ones... Marielle..."
She knew. Her [Flame Lance] had gone into one's open mouth, and it had kept coming at him.
"They have to be high-level," she whispered. "Even her fucking minions... Let alone Grade Three, this threat might not even be Grade Five..."
Above the swarm, Marielle's gaze found the immense body of their queen. Even her [Greater Fireball] had done nothing to that monster, who had chosen her next meal through the flames.
"A hundred and twenty," Marielle said. "She must be at least level a hundred and twenty. Maybe higher."

It was a frightened estimate, but even that number felt inadequate as another packed stream answered the queen's clicking. Marielle had no spell that could hurt her, Andre couldn't hold back one of her larger children, and the entire cavern was obeying her voice.
With her torn limb drawn against her chest and her brood answering from every passage, the queen began clicking at Quinlan again. Her fangs spread as the creatures beneath her climbed toward him.
"Eat... you. All of you."
Serika leaned past Ayame to look down.
"Quin... did we just find an all-you-can-eat XP buffet?"
When Marielle turned toward Serika, the redhead was grinning.
"Are you fucking insane?" Marielle demanded. "Look at them!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1987 Blazing Marks
paragraphs: "I am looking!" Serika leaned farther out, green eyes bright with anticipation.
"We need to run and sacrifice the shielder!" Marielle issued her command, eyeing Aurora. "Hold them as long as you can!"
By now, no one was even paying attention to her screeching as all of Quinlan's women grinned from ear to ear, the bottomless hunger for XP written all over their faces.
"Finally." Iris cracked her neck, stepping forward.
"Let's do this, girls!" Lucille giggled, unholstering her axe and hammer.
"Blossom wants to help Master turn a bad girl into a good one!!"
Quinlan's own grin spread behind his visor. "What a generous hostess you are."
The queen's clicking faltered as he raised his hand toward her nest.
"From the bottom of my heart, thank you."

With that, Quinlan cut the ledges holding the remaining captives free of the cavern walls and drew them toward the balcony. Sera severed the trailing silk as each arrived, while the web bridges caught beneath them stretched until their anchors ripped loose.

Spiders tumbled into the depths, shrieking and catching at one another. Quinlan crushed those clinging beneath the moving ledges against the wall below the balcony, keeping the mess well away from his family.
The gaps they left filled at once. Webbing lashed between the broken bridge ends, and fresh bodies scurried across it before the strands had stopped swinging.

The impacts of spiders crushed against the wall below jolted through Marielle's boots. Her strongest fire spell had achieved nothing against their queen, and Black was making room to fight the creature by opening the hillside.
Her fingers tightened around her staff. She couldn't find the incantation, the casting pause, any part of this she understood well enough to measure.
Still hovering in front of the balcony, Quinlan glanced back at her.
"You asked about my level."
"What?"
"Sixty-five."

Marielle shook her head at him. She and Andre were approaching a hundred, yet the queen had driven them into a room to wait for death. How could a man so far below them in level have crushed her foreleg and torn the gallery apart beneath her?
"You're lying."
"Is that so?"
"You're lying!" Marielle screamed in frantic disbelief, her knees buckling. "YOU'RE LYING!"
"Is that so?"
"You're lying!" Marielle screamed in frantic disbelief, her knees buckling. "YOU'RE LYING!"
"Up!" the queen rasped, stabbing her good foreleg toward the balcony. "Up there!"
At her cry, the brood changed direction, climbing through the ruined gallery below the balcony and up the wall toward Aurora's shield.

To meet them, Quinlan pushed rock out from that wall until a broad fighting terrace ran beneath the balcony and along both sides of the cavern. Leaving the central hollow open, he shaped steps from the balcony down to the terrace's centre.
"That's much better," Kaelira said, taking the steps to meet the first creatures hauling themselves onto the terrace.
"[Runeweaver's Armory]."

Runes blazed across the smith's armour as she caught a hooked leg on her raised forearm. Keeping the hook clear of her head, Kaelira drove her other fist into the joint with the earth power of her mark behind it. Shell crumpled beneath the blow.
The spider pitched forward, shrieking, and Iris came down the steps beside her.
"Move over."

As Kaelira shoved the broken limb aside, Iris drove her sword through the exposed mouth. The red-eyed swordswoman stepped into the creature even as its flailing legs tore a red line across her shoulder.
"Oh, fuck you."
With her mark flaring down her back, Iris wrenched the blade upward through its head and kicked the collapsing body off the terrace into the spiders below.
While Kaelira held the foot of the steps to keep the captives safe, Iris advanced on her left. The next monster to climb onto the terrace met her bloodied sword.

Above them, Blossom's mark blazed beneath her armour. Lightning crawled down her arms into the claws forming over her fists, and she disappeared from the balcony as a giant spider pulled itself onto the terrace to Kaelira's right.
"[Null Rend]!"
Both gauntlets sank beneath the giant's eyes as the dogkin reappeared against its face. Current burst through the joints of its legs, making the creature rear with a screech and expose its underside.
"Lucille! Blossom got one! Their defenses aren't high."
"Good job. Now repeat it a thousand times."
"Okay!!"
"Baby, into the fray, please~" Lucille purred.

Happy to oblige, Quinlan lowered his lovely berserker on a slab of rock, setting her beside Blossom's victim on the terrace. Lucille's mark blazed as she smashed its lower shell inward with her hammer, opening the way for her magma-coated axe.
The belly opened from end to end. Its entrails spilled over the axe haft, hissing against the molten coating while Blossom kicked free of its face.
Lucille laughed and drove her hammer into its mouth, knocking the dying creature backward onto the spiders below.

Above them, Andre tried to lift his injured arm as the corpse fell, remembering the blow that had ruined it. Lucille had broken through the same armoured shell with her hammer, then gutted it while praising the dogkin.
Lucille was already stepping toward the next giant when Andre looked up at it climbing the wall.
And Marielle knew that smile. The same woman had worn it while thanking Celia for a bowl of soup.
"Their equipment," she told Andre. "Did you see the axe? It has to be-"
Serika jumped from the balcony after the falling corpse, passing Lucille on her way down.
Wind from her Bloodfather mark curved the brawler's descent toward the cavern's right wall. With solar fire swelling around her fist, she plunged into the mass climbing toward the terrace there.
"[Solar Eruption]!"

The moment Serika's fist burst through the foremost spider's underside, solar fire detonated inside it. Its ruptured body hurtled down the wall amid a rolling sheet of flame and broken shell that stripped the other spiders from the rock.

Burning bodies rained into the swarm below, setting silk alight wherever they struck. The creatures behind them kept climbing through the flames, driving their hooks into the dead to reach the upper ledges.
Marielle's explanation died in her mouth. She had seen the bare fist go in.
Serika twisted through the recoil to land on the terrace's right arm, beneath the queen. Before the laughing brawler could turn, the monster swept her injured foreleg down the wall toward her back.
"[Heavenscar Blade]!"

Ayame came sprinting along the terrace's right arm, having followed Lucille down from the balcony. Her katana met the descending limb at its damaged joint, shearing straight through, and the water following her blade ripped the severed length away before it could reach Serika.
"You're welcome~"
"Thanks~!"
"They..." Andre whispered in full disbelief. "They're having fun..."
*KRRRIIIAAAAA!*
The queen's scream drowned out their laughter as she clutched the bleeding stump against her body. Below her, the petite samurai flicked the black fluid from her blade and looked up with a smile.
"I don't know, husband. She doesn't seem that bad of a girl to me."
"True. Compared to you, she's a saint." Quinlan was in agreement.
"Hahhh?!?!" The delicate samurai seemed to have some problems with his statement. "Say that again, I dare you!"
"In this situation... Where others would beg the Goddess for mercy..." Andre felt his head spin. "They're joking... Bantering..."

Every kill poured warmth into Quinlan's chest, feeding the Reservoir his women were drawing from through their marks. Their hunger delighted him, and he opened himself to it, enjoying how readily they spent what he gave them.
"Quin!" Serika called, driving her heel into a spider trying to crawl onto the terrace beside her. "Did you see the XP from those?! This quest fucking rocks!"
More notifications joined those from the spiders he'd crushed as Quinlan glanced toward the redhead, laughing beneath his helmet.
"I'm not looking because all my blood will rush into a certain place."
"Cruel man! Let Quinlan Junior have some fun!" Kitsara called from the balcony above them.
"I'll check right before our victory celebration."
"Ohh~ Deal~"

"Focus!" Ayame scoffed, still recovering from his terrible statement. Even as she scolded them, the Skysplitter swept her katana through the climbing brood. Water followed her blade across the wall, ripping spiders from their footholds and throwing them into the packed ranks behind.

"Nice going. You're getting a good girl brownie point from me!" Serika sprang through the opening Ayame had cleared. With another explosive punch against the wall, the brawler blasted spiders off the terrace ahead before they could spread out again.
"Fuck you too!" Ayame shouted after the tanned beauty.
"Sorry, I'm loyal to my husband. Ask the foxkin."
*Stomp!* *Stomp!* *Stomp!*
Ayame wasn't having the best of days.

As Serika advanced along the terrace's right arm, the disgruntled samurai followed through the wreckage. Near the steps, a fresh stream of spiders climbed toward Lucille over the remains of a web bridge.
Quinlan widened the terrace beneath her to give her room to swing both weapons.
"Oh, thank you, baby!"

Lucille met the first with her hammer, driving its head back into those behind it. Her axe tore through their exposed undersides while Blossom blinked along the wall above, striking at the giants trying to climb over the pile.

With a burst of lightning from her claws, the dogkin sent another convulsing monster toppling toward Lucille. Blossom was already vanishing through the grasping legs, calling out to the berserker as she reappeared farther along the stream.
Watching them advance filled Quinlan with immense satisfaction. Every opening his women carved revealed more prey, and they were eager to reach all of it.

Below the terrace, the cavern floor vanished beneath the swarm still pouring from the lower tunnels. Quinlan grew a broad stone bridge from the foot of the balcony steps, sloping down through the open hollow toward the floor.
Kaelira stood beside its upper end, with Iris fighting to her left and Lucille to her right. Quinlan hovered over the descending bridge and called.
"[Awaken]."
"WHAT IS THAT?!" Marielle screamed hysterically.
It was time to go all out.
