And Marielle knew that smile.
The same woman had worn it while thanking Celia for a bowl of soup.
"Their equipment," she told Andre.
"Did you see the axe?
It has to be-"
Serika jumped from the balcony after the falling corpse, passing Lucille on her way down.
Wind from her Bloodfather mark curved the brawler's descent toward the cavern's right wall.
With solar fire swelling around her fist, she plunged into the mass climbing toward the terrace there.
"[Solar Eruption]!"
The moment Serika's fist burst through the foremost spider's underside, solar fire detonated inside it.
Its ruptured body hurtled down the wall amid a rolling sheet of flame and broken shell that stripped the other spiders from the rock.
Burning bodies rained into the swarm below, setting silk alight wherever they struck.
The creatures behind them kept climbing through the flames, driving their hooks into the dead to reach the upper ledges.
Marielle's explanation died in her mouth.
She had seen the bare fist go in.
Serika twisted through the recoil to land on the terrace's right arm, beneath the queen.
Before the laughing brawler could turn, the monster swept her injured foreleg down the wall toward her back.
"[Heavenscar Blade]!"
Ayame came sprinting along the terrace's right arm, having followed Lucille down from the balcony.
Her katana met the descending limb at its damaged joint, shearing straight through, and the water following her blade ripped the severed length away before it could reach Serika.
"You're welcome~"
"Thanks~!"
"They..." Andre whispered in full disbelief.
"They're having fun..."
*KRRRIIIAAAAA!*
The queen's scream drowned out their laughter as she clutched the bleeding stump against her body.
Below her, the petite samurai flicked the black fluid from her blade and looked up with a smile.
"I don't know, husband.
She doesn't seem that bad of a girl to me."
"True.
Compared to you, she's a saint." Quinlan was in agreement.
"Hahhh?!?!" The delicate samurai seemed to have some problems with his statement.
"Say that again, I dare you!"
"In this situation...
Where others would beg the Goddess for mercy..." Andre felt his head spin.
"They're joking...
Bantering..."
Every kill poured warmth into Quinlan's chest, feeding the Reservoir his women were drawing from through their marks.
Their hunger delighted him, and he opened himself to it, enjoying how readily they spent what he gave them.
"Quin!" Serika called, driving her heel into a spider trying to crawl onto the terrace beside her.
"Did you see the XP from those?!
This quest fucking rocks!"
More notifications joined those from the spiders he'd crushed as Quinlan glanced toward the redhead, laughing beneath his helmet.
"I'm not looking because all my blood will rush into a certain place."
"Cruel man!
Let Quinlan Junior have some fun!" Kitsara called from the balcony above them.
"I'll check right before our victory celebration."
"Ohh~ Deal~"
"Focus!" Ayame scoffed, still recovering from his terrible statement.
Even as she scolded them, the Skysplitter swept her katana through the climbing brood.
Water followed her blade across the wall, ripping spiders from their footholds and throwing them into the packed ranks behind.
"Nice going.
You're getting a good girl brownie point from me!" Serika sprang through the opening Ayame had cleared.
With another explosive punch against the wall, the brawler blasted spiders off the terrace ahead before they could spread out again.
"Fuck you too!" Ayame shouted after the tanned beauty.
"Sorry, I'm loyal to my husband.
Ask the foxkin."
*Stomp!* *Stomp!* *Stomp!*
Ayame wasn't having the best of days.
As Serika advanced along the terrace's right arm, the disgruntled samurai followed through the wreckage.
Near the steps, a fresh stream of spiders climbed toward Lucille over the remains of a web bridge.
Quinlan widened the terrace beneath her to give her room to swing both weapons.
"Oh, thank you, baby!"
Lucille met the first with her hammer, driving its head back into those behind it.
Her axe tore through their exposed undersides while Blossom blinked along the wall above, striking at the giants trying to climb over the pile.
With a burst of lightning from her claws, the dogkin sent another convulsing monster toppling toward Lucille.
Blossom was already vanishing through the grasping legs, calling out to the berserker as she reappeared farther along the stream.
Watching them advance filled Quinlan with immense satisfaction.
Every opening his women carved revealed more prey, and they were eager to reach all of it.
Below the terrace, the cavern floor vanished beneath the swarm still pouring from the lower tunnels.
Quinlan grew a broad stone bridge from the foot of the balcony steps, sloping down through the open hollow toward the floor.
Kaelira stood beside its upper end, with Iris fighting to her left and Lucille to her right.
Quinlan hovered over the descending bridge and called.
"[Awaken]."
"WHAT IS THAT?!" Marielle screamed hysterically.
It was time to go all out.

chapters.title: Chapter 1988 Welcome to Thalorind
paragraphs: [Soul Reaper] erupted in brilliant blue flames beside Quinlan, flooding the spider cavern with light as his [Awaken] unleashed the souls within the saber.

Streams of fire plunged onto the stone bridge beneath him, swelling into armoured bodies before Marielle's eyes. Boots struck the sloping span in a rolling thunder, and weapons emerged from the blaze already gripped in their wielders' fists.
"Summons...?" Andre whispered. "Just how many...?"

Quinlan could feel every soul awaiting his will within the burning blade. One casting was enough to bring forth as many as he desired, and with the queen so generously emptying her nest for him, he saw no reason to be stingy.
"Welcome to Thalorind, my soldiers." His greeting reverberated through the depths, echoing off the walls.

Ito formed at the bridge's upper end and raised his sword to his chest, bowing to Quinlan through the swirling flames. The former Fujimori squad captain had lost his head to that same saber before Quinlan harvested his soul and sent him against his own men.
"Master. Thank you for letting us step foot outside."
Marielle's mouth opened.
"Clear the lower tunnels," Quinlan told the officer. "My wives and I are taking the upper nest."
"As you wish, Master."
"General Scar isn't here, so everyone! With me!" Ito roared, charging down the bridge with his blade raised.

Before he reached its lower end, he hurled himself over the side into the heaving mass below. An answering battle cry tore from the throats of the soldiers pouring after him, their armoured bodies plunging through the cavern with weapons aimed at the upturned mouths.
"RAAAAAH!"

The officer landed sword-first on a giant's head, driving his blade through an eye and burying it to the hilt. Its hooked foreleg punched through his chest, but he seized the limb and dragged himself farther down it to reach the sword lodged in its skull.
*SKRIIIIEE!*

Black fluid sprayed across his helmet as he ripped the blade sideways through the creature's head. Around him, his soldiers hit the swarm hard enough to buckle legs, hacking into the bodies beneath their boots while fangs closed on them from every side.

One lost his sword arm at the elbow and rammed the broken stump into the spider's eye. As its mouth opened in a shriek, he plunged his remaining hand between its fangs, holding it open for a comrade's blade.
"That hurt, you hideous thing!" the wounded soldier bellowed, shoving deeper into the jaws.

The fangs snapped shut through his neck, bursting his body into pale flame, but he'd held them apart long enough for his comrade to drive a sword through the soft flesh beneath the spider's head. A twist of the surviving soldier's blade folded the spider's legs, dumping him into the next creature's reach.

Above them, Marielle crouched at the edge of the stone balcony Quinlan had made by raising the feeding-room floor into the cavern wall. Aurora's barrier sheltered her and the rescued captives, with steps descending to the fighting terrace and the bridge below.

Even as she watched soldiers being torn apart, more leapt off the bridge, roaring as they fell. Those who landed among the wreckage climbed straight over their own dying comrades to reach the monsters beyond.
"They aren't even trying to protect themselves..."

At the centre of the slaughter, the officer tore free of the dead giant's leg and charged with a hole through his chest. Another spider caught him across the waist, pinning him between its fangs while he hacked at the plates above its mouth.
"Keep going!"
His blade split an eye before the jaws met through his middle. Pale fire burst between the fangs, spilling over the spider's face as the ruined body came apart.
Then the scattered flames drew together beneath its head, reforming Ito with his sword already rising toward its throat.
"Again!" he roared, driving the blade upward with both hands.

Marielle recoiled from the balcony's edge. The hole in his chest was gone. Farther back, the soldier she'd seen lose his arm and head was hauling himself onto another spider, using both hands to wrench its fangs apart.

[Reign of the Undying] was returning Quinlan's destroyed Elite Souls to the fight without another casting of [Awaken]. Each could return once per minute, and out here, beyond Iskaris, every resurrection cost them another ten percent of their strength until he set foot on his land again.

Splitting the shell took more effort now, enough for Quinlan to notice the cost of the resurrection. Even with a boot braced against the monster's face, Ito had to keep tearing at the wound before its throat finally opened over him.
"Forward!"
The soldiers answered with a roar, trampling the collapsing body as they drove toward the tunnels. Quinlan thrust ridges of rock through the swarm on either side, splitting its masses into channels.
"Stay... dead!"

On the wall to the balcony's right, the queen hooked a web bridge and dragged it down across the soldiers still descending Quinlan's stone span. Silk tightened around their weapons as she pulled, wrenching the front rank off their feet toward her waiting fangs.

Across the gap between her hook and the snared soldiers, Quinlan swept a blade of wind. The tether snapped, and he followed the cut with a torrent of water that struck her underside hard enough to send her supporting legs scraping furrows down the wall.
*SKRIIIIEE!*

Digging her hooks deeper into the rock let her brace against his torrent, though water still splashed over her screaming face. Until the last soldier had stripped the loose silk from his weapon, Quinlan held her there; then he swept the ruined web into the brood below.
"Keep them busy," he told Ito, grinning as his soldiers charged through the cleared crossing.
"Necromancer," Andre breathed. "But... what?" The Grade Three adventurer was more confused than ever in his life.
He lowered his sword. "What in the Goddess are you, Adventurer Black?"
Vex stepped past him, her crimson tattoos joining into a single burning lattice. Tiny horns pushed through her white hair while a black tail uncoiled behind her.
"He's not 'in the Goddess.'" The Hexwitch's eyes danced with amusement as she watched her lover. "That hypocrite doesn't deserve such a thing."
"Demon!" Marielle choked.
Vex turned her pentagram eyes toward the horrified mage, then rolled them, not even bothering to reply.

Instead, the woman who forced the Primordial Demon of Lust to sponsor her Bloodfather evolution began running down the balcony steps and past Kaelira at their foot to follow the soldiers onto the bridge.
When a giant spawn hauled itself over the lower end to block them, the Hexwitch caught its descending foreleg on her sword and pressed her free hand toward its shell.
"[Hex of Decay]."
The curse shattered into dark sparks before it could sink through the shell. Under the weight still pressing on her sword, Vex slid back a step, her heel scoring a line in the bridge.
"Oh? The pests are truly on another level over here." Vex's tongue reached out, licking her lips with immense satisfaction. "Let me exterminate you."
"[My Man Reigns Supreme]!"

Quinlan's towering silhouette rose behind her as her mark burned through her clothes. With the limb held against her blade, Vex let the curse measure the creature against her husband, her grin widening when the comparison reached Magic.
"[Hubby Supremacy Tax~]!"

Black threads stretched from the spider into Vex as she drained the gap between its Magic and Quinlan's, stealing only what the creature possessed and adding it to her own power. The resistance that had shattered her first curse weakened while magic swelled through her brand.
"[Hex of Decay]."
This time, her strengthened curse sank into the spider. Where its flesh had resisted her before, a black wound spread around her sword until the rotting leg buckled against the blade.
"There we go. Love you, Hubby!!"
Vex giggled while a sideways wrench of her blade tore the leg free in a spray of rotten tissue. As the spider pitched forward, her next thrust met it.
By the time Vex pulled her sword out of its head, Black Fang had come down the bridge behind her and was already passing her disciple.
"[Damnation's Fang]."
Violet light shone through the assassin's clothing as she ducked beneath the next creature's fangs. Her coated blade opened its throat, leaving serpent-venom seeping through the wound.

There was no soul for [Soul Reaper] to harvest from the monster, but Black Fang's venom took hold of its corpse. The dead spider drove its legs into the bridge and rose behind her, its movements guided by a fragment of her own combat awareness.
"Kill."
At her sword's gesture, it leapt onto the spider climbing beside it. The living creature screamed as its dead sibling drove its fangs beneath its head and tore backward.
Through the opening her puppet made, Black Fang slipped farther into the swarm. Each kill rose behind the Venomborne Terror to turn upon the next living body.
"Master, you're having too much fun!"

Vex came after her with a delighted laugh, driving curses into the creatures struggling beneath the puppets. The brood packed the bridge so tightly that the dying could scarcely fall before another spider was climbing over them.
"You should smile more like this. Such an unhinged grin on a powerful woman is a dangerous drug for Hubby."
"I'm not smiling."
Vex held up a hand mirror so Black Fang could see them grinning side by side. "Master... You're having the time of your life and you're very sexy while doing it."
She giggled, "Well, if you ask me, you look like a savage psychopathic maniac on the loose, but it's not my opinion that matters, right~?"
"I'll deal with you later," Black Fang decreed flatly, descending into the chaos.
"Hehe! Wait for me!" Vex rushed after her, grinning from ear to ear like the happiest of daughters.
How couldn't she?
Her beloved master was finally free, and it was all thanks to the same man who did so much for them all...
"Master, isn't it about time you ditch your stupid pills and drink from the tap?!"

Marielle grabbed her husband's good arm. All she'd been waiting for was a chance to leave with their rescuers once the monsters died. Now Black's soldiers were returning from destruction, and the quiet woman was making corpses fight for her while an unhinged demon was running after her, screaming utter nonsense.
Then the officer's greeting came back to her.
Master. Thank you for letting us step foot outside.
All morning she'd been explaining adventuring to the man now floating above the slaughter. He'd let her carry on with an army of the dead inside his sword, and every woman with him had known.
"Why?" Her voice scraped her throat. "Why are you showing us this?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1989 The Villain's Gratitude
paragraphs: Quinlan turned toward the balcony, still hovering above the bridge. Marielle almost wished he hadn't heard her; the red light behind his visor settled on her face, and her fingers tightened painfully around Andre's sleeve.
"Answer already...!" She stomped, but her outlash had none of her prior ferocity.

Quinlan grinned beneath his helmet, and [Synchra] reshaped its sealed faceplate to match. Black metal drew into sharp cheek ridges while a crimson line curved across his mouth, widening into a cruel smile edged with pointed metal teeth.
Every inch of his skin remained covered, yet Marielle could see his vicious delight in the face the armour made for him.
A low chuckle reached her through the helmet, and she recoiled.
"Why, you ask?"
She'd imagined a rich fool ashamed of his weakness beneath that armour, whose women and equipment had carried him far beyond his ability. Someone who needed a proper adventurer to keep him alive.
The man watching her now was enjoying every moment of her fear.
"Because neither of you will tell anyone."
Marielle stopped breathing. Beside her, Andre pulled his sleeve from her grip so he could step in front of her, raising his sword with his good arm.
"Stay behind me."

She caught the back of his clothes and pulled herself upright behind him, desperate to keep him close. That sword hadn't saved him from one of the queen's children. His ruined arm hung uselessly at his side, and terror swallowed the last of her relief at being rescued.
"We... we wouldn't..."

The promise wouldn't come out. She had threatened to report them, sneered at their levels, ordered his shielder to stay behind and die. Now that burning grin was aimed at her, and she couldn't find a single reason he would let her leave.
Below the balcony, a spider hauled itself over the terrace's edge behind Kaelira. Quinlan curled his fingers, closing the rock around its forebody before it could strike her.
*KRRUNCH!*

Its abdomen burst under the pressure, spraying black fluid down the wall. The trapped head kept shrieking, so he squeezed again, slowly enough for Marielle to hear its shell splitting before its mouth collapsed.
She flinched into Andre's back. Quinlan was still looking at her.
"Please..."

He heard her despite the fighting. Watching her hide behind the husband he could crush just as easily filled him with vicious satisfaction. She'd been so eager to spend Aurora's life to save her own, and now she was begging him to be kind.

Even after Quinlan let the mangled spider drop into the swarm, Marielle couldn't find another word. All she could do was bury her face against Andre's shoulder, shaking too badly to lift her staff while the man above them waited.
"I do owe you my thanks, though," Quinlan continued.
Marielle lifted her head at his thanks, struggling to understand him through the pounding in her ears. "What...?"

"I thought leaving Iskaris might make me feel a level-one nobody again next to the fighters here. A second transmigration of sorts. But thanks to you two, I know I'm not starting from the bottom this time."
"Iskaris?" Andre repeated.
Marielle's grip tightened. "That continent? You're claiming you came from the lost continent?!"
On the cavern's right wall, the queen tore a dead spawn off her foreleg and flung it toward Black Fang at the foot of the bridge. The assassin slipped beneath the tumbling body.
Along the terrace's right arm came Kitsara, fresh from the balcony steps. Her white hair and tails drowned in demonic darkness as the foxkin joined Ayame beneath the queen.
"[Demon Fox's Domain]."
Foxkin silhouettes spread across the surviving webs, their weight drawing the strands taut beneath the queen's feet.
"False flesh..." The queen's fangs clicked together as the web trembled beneath the copies. "I feel you crawling. All of you."
"Then count them fast, darling."
Kitsara's lower voice came from beneath the queen. Another copy spoke from her back.
"Take your time."

The queen's sweeping leg burst the nearest copy into darkness. When the figure reformed astride the limb, she ground it against the cavern wall, tearing a furrow through the rock while another copy landed beside her eyes.
"Get... off!"
"But you wanted to eat us. Or are foxies too much for your tummy? Am I not invited to the fun?"

The copy's dagger scraped across the plates above an eye without penetrating. The queen snapped her head sideways and crushed it between her face and the wall, then drove her foreleg down toward the real foxkin on the terrace.
"Kitsara, stop messing around." Ayame caught her arm and pulled her clear.
"Oopsie. I had it under control."

The hook smashed through the terrace where Kitsara had stood. Its outer edge broke away beneath their feet, and Quinlan thrust a support up from the wall to catch the slab before it could carry both women into the swarm.
"Little meat!" the queen shrieked, dragging her hook through the broken paving toward them.
A copy caught the rim of her eye while she reached, driving its dagger beneath the plate from the side. Blood jetted over its hand, and the queen's scream shook dust from the ceiling.
"Found it," Kitsara decreed from beside Ayame, her next copies climbing toward the wound.
Shaking loose the copies, the queen hurled herself off the right wall toward Quinlan over the hollow. A pillar rose from the cavern floor at his command to meet her descending abdomen.
*KRRRAK!*

The pillar broke beneath her weight, leaving Quinlan staring into her open fangs through a shower of stone. A blast of his own wind carried him clear of her jaws, but her hook caught his raised forearm before he could escape her reach.
Pain rang through his arm as the blow hurled him sideways, the hook carving a groove through Synchra's black plating.
"You're a tough one," he muttered.

Quinlan caught her extended limb in a rising fist of rock and drove a second pillar into her exposed underside. Her shell cracked this time, spilling dark fluid as he slammed her against a broad ledge above the lower tunnel mouths.
With the queen clinging to a ledge directly across the cavern from the balcony, Quinlan flew after her, leaving his family to continue the fighting along the terrace behind him.
"Above! Ch-children, above him!"
The surviving webs overhead sagged as the queen's brood rushed across them. Spiders dropped toward Quinlan in a writhing mass, their falling bodies blotting out the cavern roof.

Quinlan sent branching columns of water surging upward to swallow the descending ranks. By spreading the current along the webs, he swept up more bodies and tore the strands down with their occupants.
Screeches rang through the hollow. Quinlan watched the tangled limbs claw through his water, then began freezing the columns from the outside inward.
When one forced its screaming head through the hardening surface, Quinlan turned the column holding it toward the queen and hurled it through the air.
Her remaining foreleg smashed the missile apart before it reached her face. The next followed through the spray, and she caught it between her fangs, crushing the frozen body into fragments.
"Come down!" she shrieked through the falling ice. "Come here!"
By sending another missile straight at her eyes, Quinlan drew her foreleg up to meet it, opening a gap for the frozen body he curved beneath the limb into her mouth.
The impact broke one fang at the root. Her scream sprayed blood and pieces of her own child over the ledge while Quinlan drove the remaining missiles into the brood climbing on either side of her.
Frozen bodies burst against the walls, shredding the packed swarm with jagged chunks of ice and shell.

Through the wreckage, the queen lunged again. Quinlan drove lightning into her broken mouth, holding the current until her legs convulsed against the ledge, but her hook kept reaching for him through the pain.
There it was, the pleasure he'd been missing while reading notices and waiting for strangers to decide whether he was qualified to pick their fucking weeds.
Quinlan swept himself beyond the hook with another gust. His forearm still ached from the last blow, and he laughed as the queen dragged herself upright, burning saliva dripping between her fangs.
"Are you ready to be a good girl now?"
"Not... your pet!"

Her hook stabbed toward his face, and Quinlan closed the ledge's stone around it. As she strained against the restraint, he flooded it with magma, filling the gaps around her foreleg until molten rock welled between its plates.
*SKRIIIIIAAAAA!*

Ripping herself loose left glowing fragments clinging to the queen's limb. Before she could shake them off, a blast of Quinlan's wind drove the molten coating into the joint, splitting the shell until cooked flesh bulged through the crack.
"H-hurts!"

Each blow of her leg against the ledge scraped away magma and strips of her own flesh. For every glob she dislodged, Quinlan sent another jet of molten rock into the exposed joint until she dragged the limb against her chest to shelter it.
"Aww. I even need to teach you how to shake paws?"
The queen's eyes shifted past him to the balcony. Bracing her surviving legs against the wall, she spat a broad sheet of venom toward the rescued captives.
"[Dreamveil]!" Aurora planted her staff, thickening the barrier over the balcony.

Quinlan swept a wall of water across the venom's path. The lower edge escaped beneath his current and struck the terrace, eating through its lip in a boiling cascade that sent Iris leaping back beside Kaelira.

Across the hollow, the queen lunged through the spray at Quinlan, thrusting her burned foreleg toward his visor. He blocked the hook with a slab of rock, but she drove her whole weight behind it, forcing him backward through the air while blood poured from the split joint.
Marielle looked from him to Aurora, whose shield was hissing beneath the venom. At the back of the balcony, Seraphiel finished closing the last captive's wounds and rose.
"[Divine Arsenal]."
A bow of light formed in the elf's hands. Through a gap Aurora opened above the barrier, Sera sent an arrow into a spider descending toward the shelter, punching it off its strand.
Marielle moved behind Sera, drawing breath for an incantation as she raised her staff and aimed its tip at the elf's back.
"Black! Let us live or your healer is dead!"

"Answer already...!" She stomped, but her outlash had none of her prior ferocity.

Black metal drew into sharp cheek ridges while a crimson line curved across his mouth, widening into a cruel smile edged with pointed metal teeth.
Every inch of his skin remained covered, yet Marielle could see his vicious delight in the face the armour made for him.
A low chuckle reached her through the helmet, and she recoiled.
"Why, you ask?"
She'd imagined a rich fool ashamed of his weakness beneath that armour, whose women and equipment had carried him far beyond his ability.

"Because neither of you will tell anyone."

Beside her, Andre pulled his sleeve from her grip so he could step in front of her, raising his sword with his good arm.
"Stay behind me."
She caught the back of his clothes and pulled herself upright behind him, desperate to keep him close.
That sword hadn't saved him from one of the queen's children.

Its abdomen burst under the pressure, spraying black fluid down the wall.
The trapped head kept shrieking, so he squeezed again, slowly enough for Marielle to hear its shell splitting before its mouth collapsed.
She flinched into Andre's back.
Quinlan was still looking at her.
"Please..."
He heard her despite the fighting.
Watching her hide behind the husband he could crush just as easily filled him with vicious satisfaction.
She'd been so eager to spend Aurora's life to save her own, and now she was begging him to be kind.
Even after Quinlan let the mangled spider drop into the swarm, Marielle couldn't find another word.

"I do owe you my thanks, though," Quinlan continued.

"What...?"

The assassin slipped beneath the tumbling body.

Foxkin silhouettes spread across the surviving webs, their weight drawing the strands taut beneath the queen's feet.
"False flesh..." The queen's fangs clicked together as the web trembled beneath the copies.
"I feel you crawling.
All of you."
"Then count them fast, darling."
Kitsara's lower voice came from beneath the queen.
Another copy spoke from her back.
"Take your time."
The queen's sweeping leg burst the nearest copy into darkness.
When the figure reformed astride the limb, she ground it against the cavern wall, tearing a furrow through the rock while another copy landed beside her eyes.
"Get... off!"
"But you wanted to eat us.

Am I not invited to the fun?"
The copy's dagger scraped across the plates above an eye without penetrating.
The queen snapped her head sideways and crushed it between her face and the wall, then drove her foreleg down toward the real foxkin on the terrace.

"Oopsie.
I had it under control."
The hook smashed through the terrace where Kitsara had stood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1990 Kidnapped
paragraphs: "Black! Let me live or your healer is dead!"
Marielle aimed her staff at Seraphiel's back on the sheltered balcony, waiting for Black to look at her. If he wanted his healer alive, he would have to let them leave.
Seraphiel glanced over her shoulder at the staff, then turned toward the woman holding it. Her bow of light hung loosely from one hand.
"Oh~ You picked me?"
"Stay still!" Marielle jabbed the staff toward her chest. "Black! Are you listening?! Tell your women to move away!"
The elf looked down at the staff's tip with a spreading smile.
"You thought I was the weak one? Oh, Quin, did you hear that? Your hopeless little healer has been taken hostage~"
She sounded delighted. Marielle pressed the tip against her, desperate to make the laughing bitch understand that her life was being threatened.
"I'll burn a hole through you!"
"Okay." Seraphiel's smile widened, baring her teeth. The cruelty on her delicate face made Marielle want to snatch the staff back.
"Try me, bitch."
The Dawnbringer's bow contracted into a dagger as she stepped past the staff with staggering speed, slicing Marielle's wrist on the way in.
"What?!"
Before the mage could pull back, an elbow smashed into her mouth and a knee drove up beneath her ribs, folding her over the blow.
The scream caught in Marielle's empty lungs. Seraphiel closed her free hand around the mage's throat and slammed her against the wall hard enough to knock dust from the blocks.

Only when her staff clattered to the floor did Marielle look down. Blood was running over fingers that no longer obeyed her, dripping from the deep cut across her wrist. She'd been looking straight at Seraphiel and still hadn't seen the blade coming.
"A-AAAH!"
The cry broke into a strangled squeal as the blonde elf lifted her. Marielle's boots scraped up the wall, searching for a foothold until even their tips hung clear of the paving.
All her weight dangled from the delicate fingers around her throat.

She grabbed Seraphiel's wrist with her good hand, trying to force it down. The curvaceous woman watched her struggle with a delighted smile, her dagger hanging idly beside her hip. Marielle pulled harder, kicking against the wall, but couldn't make the elf's arm bend.
"There it is." The Dawnbringer smiled with extreme cruelty. "You're finally singing after all the terrible things you said about my friends and husband."
Her fingers tightened, cutting the next breath into a thin, desperate whistle. Marielle dug her nails into the hand holding her, and the Dawnbringer laughed at the effort.
"Keep going~ It's a beautiful tune I longed to hear~"
A shake of Seraphiel's arm tore Marielle's grip loose and sent her legs swinging. Before she could catch the wrist again, the elf shook her harder, knocking the back of her head against the wall.
"Still trying to tell us what to do?"

Marielle's mouth worked around a reply that wouldn't come. She could hear the wet choking sounds she was making, could feel the blood from her split lip running over the fingers buried in her throat. The woman holding her only looked happier as she struggled.

Seraphiel was enjoying every kick. All day she'd listened to this bitch insult her family, and now she could feel Marielle's frantic attempts to breathe against her palm. She kept her suspended a little longer, savouring the terror in the eyes that had looked down on them.

Through [Empowerment], the Magic that fed Seraphiel's healing also strengthened her body and accelerated her movements. Marielle had felt the blows one after another without managing to raise her free hand against any of them.

When the mage's kicks began to falter, the Dawnbringer eased her fingers enough to let her drag in a ragged breath. Marielle coughed blood down her chin, clutching at the wrist again while her boots swung above the floor.
"You're... a healer..."
"Yes~ But waiting for someone to hurt my family so I can be useful got old quick. Now I kill the bastards before they can do it. Aren't I smart?"

Marielle tried to brace her heels against the wall and lift some of her weight off her throat. She'd chosen the woman tending the wounded, the one whose hands had been so gentle opening their cocoons. Now she hung from one of those hands while the elf mocked her.
"No! Please, no!"
"Aww. But you were being so brave a moment ago."

The blonde beauty drew her away from the wall, taking even that support from her. Marielle's legs thrashed in empty air as Seraphiel brought them face-to-face, inspecting her tear-streaked features with shameless pleasure.
"There. That's a much nicer expression on you."
"Nyxara's influence is clear on you..." Behind the blonde elf, Aurora sighed as she sealed the patients beneath a second barrier.
"What do you mean? I always was a vicious woman~ I can just hide it better than some."
Marielle tried to look toward Andre. Seraphiel followed her gaze, then turned the mage in her grip and drove her face into the wall.
*CRACK!*

Released from the elf's hand, Marielle dropped into a heap at its foot. The blow left her staring at the paving through swimming patches of light, unable to make sense of the blood dripping beneath her face.
"Marielle!"
Andre charged the Dawnbringer with his sword in his good hand.
"Let her go!"
His next step faltered. Before he could bring his sword down, a surge of mana from the open cavern bore against him, filling him with such sudden dread that he stopped short of the elf.
*KRRZZZT!*
The sharp crackle drew his head around. White-blue light flared across his blade as Quinlan's lightning gathered beyond the balcony, and the hatred pouring through that mana made Andre recoil.
He could feel how badly its owner wanted to hurt him. Under that crushing malice, reaching Marielle ceased to matter for one terrified instant; he needed his sword between himself and the light.
"Shit-!"
Andre hauled the blade across his chest as the bolt tore toward him. Lightning burst against the steel before he could brace his feet.

The impact flung him backward. He hit the paving with his sword still clenched in a smoking hand, his injured arm trapped beneath him, and screamed as another bolt ripped through the spot beside his head.
Searching across the hollow for the man attacking him, Andre found Black still facing the monster.

Her hook hammered against his raised saber while a torrent of his water drove her supporting legs down the ledge. Lightning branched from the air behind his shoulders, crossing the cavern through the gap Aurora opened in her outer shield.
Andre dragged his ruined arm free and rolled before the next strike blasted chips across his face.
"He isn't even looking?!"
He'd heard no incantation. Black's hands were occupied with the monster trying to tear him apart, yet every attempt Andre made to rise brought another white-blue flash aimed straight at him.
"He's casting without a chant or a gesture... while looking the other way?!"

Quinlan drove a blade of wind through the queen's burned foreleg, peeling the damaged shell back from its joint. Her shriek rang through the hollow as another bolt struck Andre's raised sword and hurled him back onto his side.
Marielle had threatened to burn through his wife's body, and now her husband was raising a sword at that same woman.

chapters.title: Chapter 1991 Savage Seraphiel
paragraphs: What they'd done just now was an unforgivable crime, and they'd pay. That was what his mana told them.

Andre could feel that malice crawling over his skin between the strikes. Even the fading sparks carried a hatred so savage that he flinched from them, clutching his sword against his chest while his teeth rattled together.
Beside the wall, Seraphiel looked past the lightning toward her husband, her cheeks warming as another bolt drove Andre back from her.
"Even now, you're protecting me..."

He had a cavern full of monsters in front of him, yet the moment Andre raised his sword at her, Quinlan's fury had reached across it. Affection swelled in her chest at the sight of him fighting for her without even breaking from his own battle.
"You wonderful man," she murmured, smiling helplessly as she drew a second dagger from her light and twirled both blades around her fingers.
A groan at her feet drew her gaze down. Marielle had managed to push herself onto one elbow beside the wall, blood running from her nose as she tried to lift her face.
Seraphiel kicked it straight back into the bloodstained blocks.
*Crunch!*
Leaving the mage crumpled against the wall, the elf began walking toward Andre with a dagger in each hand. Aurora stepped away from the shielded patients to join her.
"Let me join you."
"Sure~"

At Quinlan's call, the Elite Souls dissolved into streams of blue fire and returned to [Soul Reaper].
Black Fang's dead spiders kept tearing at the swarm as the last soldier vanished from the lower bridge.
The queen strained toward the empty span.
Before she could pull her belly free, Quinlan closed a collar of stone over her head and cut her ledge from the wall, keeping the rock clamped around her abdomen attached to it.
He drew the whole block across the cavern and anchored it at the balcony's far right end, beyond his gathered women and the prisoners pinned beneath Aurora's barriers.
Marielle heard the queen's broken clicking from farther along the balcony.
Under Quinlan's earth magic, the wall beneath their shelter thickened into a solid buttress.
He reinforced the balcony and its rear wall together, leaving them firmly anchored above the cavern floor while Aurora enclosed the whole shelter beneath ice-packed light.
Quinlan flew out over the bridge, rising toward the cavern roof with his family's shelter behind him.
"There's no escape."
Below him, the brood surged toward every passage still open.
At Quinlan's will, the tunnel mouths slammed shut, crushing the spiders wedged between them.
Under his earth magic, the plugs compressed until the giants' hooks scraped pale grooves across them without breaking through.
Frost raced over the sealed entrances as Quinlan froze their surfaces into thick, interlocked plates.
Spiders striking the barriers skidded off and fell beneath those still pushing forward, their shrieks filling the cavern.
"Up!" the queen rasped from her prison at the balcony's far end.
"Up!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1993 Monster
paragraphs: Andre's scream followed her down, but Quinlan kept her from falling. Her head sagged in his grip, her chin hanging crooked beneath a ruined cheek. The breath that came through her mouth bubbled in blood.
Quinlan's silent [Subjugation] reached her next.
Marielle convulsed in his hand. Through the wreckage of pain, she felt the binding closing inside her and tried to resist, but all that escaped her shattered mouth was a wet, terrified rasp.
The spell took hold. Quinlan watched her surviving resistance fail before lowering her onto the floor beneath the blood smeared across the wall.
"Seraphiel."
"Leave it to me."

The Dawnbringer crouched beside Marielle, [Healing Light] gathering beneath her palm. As her magic stemmed the bleeding inside the mage's head and throat, the bubbling breaths eased into a hoarse drag of air.
Under the light, the fractured bones drew back into place. Her mouth still hung open around the broken stumps of her teeth.
Beside them, Andre strained against Aurora's barrier until his injured arm shook. His eyes stayed on his wife's face, following each shallow breath.
Quinlan crouched in front of him.
"Your wife is irredeemable trash and you were ready to hurt my women too. But I can respect a man who stands by his woman, even if she deserves the worst."
Andre looked up at the blood on Quinlan's gauntlet.

chapters.title: Chapter 1994 Silky
paragraphs: Ayame heard Marielle's broken warning from beside the treasure piled along the upper gallery.
"A monster?" The samurai turned toward the woman trembling in Andre's arms. "No. A primordial demigod who has already killed a god? Yes."
Marielle tried to pull herself higher against her husband's chest. Pain tore through her ruined mouth as she attempted to answer, but she couldn't get past the first sound.
Beyond Ayame, Black bent to inspect a weapon the spiders had brought him. He turned it over, then let it disappear into his ring with the rest of the offerings.
A god.
The woman had said he'd killed a god while he stood there sorting through a sack of fucking loot.
"He's met the Goddess too," Seraphiel added, smiling at Marielle. "He even wounded her."
"He ruined the bitch's purity~" Vex purred, her pentagram eyes bright with pride.
"The... Goddess...?"
Andre's voice cracked on the word. Marielle felt his arm tighten around her, holding her so hard that the broken stumps of her teeth scraped together.

She wanted him to tell them to stop. To call them liars. The Goddess watched over Thalorind, heard their prayers, stood above everything they had ever feared. These women were discussing hurting her with the same fond amusement they'd shown while their husband boiled the nest alive.
"Oh, you girls are making him sound so small~" Lucille purred. "Baby is so much more than that."
The caramel-haired woman came closer, her bloodied weapons resting at her sides. Marielle shrank against Andre as Lucille bent to meet her eyes.
Utter sadism shone in that beautiful green gaze. She was enjoying this, taking her time with the woman who had demanded they sacrifice Aurora and then threatened to burn through Sera's chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 1995 Home Sweet Home
paragraphs: With the last captives safely through, Quinlan crossed after Lucille and Kaelira. Behind Serika, who carried Celia, the other women made their way into the garden before the queen squeezed her abdomen past the gate's edge.
Sera stayed beside her, healing light moving over the torn shell. The spider shuddered as the bleeding wounds closed, then gingerly put weight on a leg she'd been dragging.
"Better?"
"Yes... First time I... Heal magic."
"Oh?" The blonde beauty's eyes lit up. "I hope I didn't disappoint~"
"No... I... Amazed..."
"Hehe! You truly are a good girl, aren't you?"
"Great, I love you already. Try not to step on anybody."
"Okay..."
Quinlan closed the gate behind them.
"DADDY!!"
A green blur came racing across the lawn.
Quinlan caught Rosie under the arms and lifted her into an embrace. Her legs wrapped around his waist while she squeezed his neck, pressing her face against the side of his helmet.
"You're all covered up!"
At his will, Synchra drew away from his head. Rosie immediately kissed his cheek, then held his face between her hands to inspect him.
"Much better. Did Daddy miss Rosie?"
"Terribly."
"Good."

chapters.title: Chapter 1996 Charitable Hexwitch
paragraphs: The smell of lunch drew Blossom's attention to Anna and Beatrice as they reached Quinlan's chair on the terrace of his Iskaris estate. Beyond the garden wall, Ayame and Iris were still trading blows and shouted insults.
"Master..."
With Vex occupying his right knee, Blossom had settled on the left. From there, the dogkin leaned across him to inspect the twins' tray, her ears rising in anticipation.
"That smells delicious! Even after tasting so many new flavors, Blossom loves the maids' cooking the most!"
"Lady Blossom..." Anna and Beatrice beamed at her, immense pride lighting their matching faces. Even Clarisse's composed expression gave way to a broad smile as she set down her tray.

All those new things to taste in the wider world, and Lady Blossom still wanted their cooking most! Returning from the house, Emily paused beside Dorothy with her chest swelling with pride. Dorothy's grin told her she'd heard it too.
"Then we'll make sure you have plenty, Lady Blossom," Emily said warmly.
"It does smell phenomenal, doesn't it?" Vex accepted a plate from Beatrice with a smile. "Thank you. I'll take care of Hubby."

The tray held everything Vex needed to spoil him: sliced meat from Anna, bread and sauce from Clarisse. She balanced the plate on her lap and offered Quinlan the first bite, watching his face as he tasted it.
"Good?"
"Very."
A swallow came from his other side.

chapters.title: Chapter 1997 Cruel Women
paragraphs: "Don't put me back..."
"You're out," the elf told her. "Look around."
Her frightened gaze moved from Sera's face to the roof, then toward the open lawn.
"Outside...?"
Aurora waited through another breath before nodding to Black Fang.
"The repeating flow has stopped. Her own mana was keeping her trapped after the venom started it, just as we thought."
"And she can see where she is," Sera said softly, keeping hold of the woman's hand.
Quinlan watched the patient loosen her grip. She was still frightened, but when Sera offered her water, she took the cup and drank instead of clawing at silk that wasn't there.
Aurora returned to the bench to fill the remaining vials.
"We'll take this back for Celia's father. If Edric responds as well as she has..."
"Well done, ladies, Silky."
At the acknowledgment, Silky raised her head a little, then froze when Rosie shifted against her.
The child had fallen asleep.

Once Blossom and Vex had slipped from his knees, Quinlan went to lift his sleeping daughter from the spider's head. The sight of his approaching hands set Silky's surviving legs moving anxiously against the paving.
"I... stay."
He paused.

chapters.title: Chapter 1998 And?
paragraphs: "Has he caused trouble?"
"Not... exactly."
"Then he can wait. These supply wagons can't."
Zorvanna returned to the report, reclining along the broad couch with one powerful leg stretched over its cushions. Her long black hair fell across her bare arm as she turned the page.
"Your Majesty. Please."
The page stopped halfway over.
"He's registered as an adventurer," the younger woman persisted. "And what we've heard since... I'd feel much better if you let me explain."
"We have a Guild for that. Unless you think I should start interviewing every newcomer myself?"
"I'm asking you to hear about this one."
Zorvanna studied her over the report. The assistant held her gaze, though her pink tail had curled tightly around the leg of her chair.
"My, Lysara, you really aren't letting this go."
"No, Your Majesty."
With a sigh, the queen let the papers rest against her thigh. Heavy horns swept back from her temples, and crimson scales framed the gold eyes now giving her assistant their full attention.

chapters.title: Chapter 1999 Gossiping Chicks
paragraphs: A week had passed since Adventurer Black returned from the southern ruins, and the women at Sarthal's Guild still hadn't run out of things to say about him and his people.
"The Scarlet Lilies went out again."
"Already? They were here this morning!"
"Collected their payment, asked about something stronger, and left. I heard Lilith complaining that the journey took longer than the fight."

The short-haired adventurer leaned across the table, lowering her mug. She had claimed this particular seat because it faced both the counter and the entrance, giving her an excellent view of everything worth discussing.
Her own contract lay beneath the mug, forgotten. Rent wasn't due for three more weeks.
"Those are his bodyguards," she reminded her companions. "Imagine what he needs protecting from."
"His wives?"
Laughter broke out around the table.
"I mean, can you imagine what Kitsara gets up to behind closed doors? Considering how shameless she already is in public?"
"She might be a bad bitch, but let me tell you, it's the quiet ones that are the real trouble. My bet is that Kaelira is a real freak in the sheets."
"Her? The most innocent of them all? I'd venture to guess it's that scary woman, Black Fang, who rides him to near malnutrition every night."
At that, one of them leaned in. "Actually, I heard she wasn't... you know?"
"Taking the D up the P?"
"...Yea. She and the other scary black-haired one."
"Ayame?"
"Nah, that bitch is gobbling him up every night. The red-eyed one, Iris."
"Hmm... Makes sense. She's rather distant and frightening."
"But wait, how do you know all this?"
"I spent my last quest's income buying a room in their inn. Those two don't even sleep in the same room as him. Same for the bodyguards."

chapters.title: Chapter 2000
paragraphs: Blossom, while listening to the chatter, reached past Quinlan's arm to point at the badges, her tail beginning to wag.
"Master, Blossom gets a new one too?!"
"You heard her."
"Hehe!"
Her delighted laugh brought a chuckle from the clerk, who found the dogkin's name before moving her badge to the front.
"You've certainly earned it. All of you."
From beside the table, the newcomer smoothed her neckline, took a breath, and stepped into the space left by the other women.
"Lord Black, Unbound, congratulations on making history! If you happen to be free this evening, I'd love to buy you a drink. To celebrate."
Her friend's mug stopped halfway to her mouth.
"You just said you were resting!"
"I've rested."
Kitsara covered her grin with her fingers. Even Quinlan's helmet couldn't hide the amusement in his voice when he answered.
"I already have plans with my ladies."
"Ah... Of course. Another time, perhaps."
She retreated beneath her companions' delighted scrutiny, red-faced but visibly pleased with herself for having tried. Beside the counter, Marielle barely heard the laughter following her.
"At least you shot your shot, even if it was a slingshot aimed at the sun. That's more than many can say!"
"Fuck you all... I'm going to sleep."
"Don't get depressed on me just because you couldn't suck your way into generational wealth and power, bitch."
"Fuck you... Sob... I want to freeload so bad..."
Grade Three.
Marielle's fingers found the badge on her own robe.
That had been her use. The single, precious reason he still brought her along instead of leaving her somewhere to rot. When a contract required a qualified party, he needed her name on it.
